anchors.claim: At least one non-test nuclear detonation (war use) occurs before 2035
anchors.provenance: FORECAST-ANCHORS §6: blend of Metaculus Q3150 (~26%, flagged by the brief as a known high outlier) and superforecaster estimates (~2-4%), midpoint ~8%.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: Metaculus counts any non-test detonation anywhere, including states this model does not represent, so the model should read at or below the anchor. The 26%-vs-supers spread is itself the finding — the band spans it deliberately rather than picking a side.

anchors.claim: A durable Russia–Ukraine ceasefire begins by end-2026
anchors.provenance: FORECAST-ANCHORS §4.2: conflicting Metaculus snapshots (15% and 40%); Polymarket 25.5% in May 2026; anchored at 20% given the Duma-election dynamic and Lavrov's 14 Aug position.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: THE dominant wording trap in the whole table, and as of W4.5 it is verified rather than suspected. The brief could only say the market 'appears to have' resolved Yes on the three-day May-2026 truce, from a search summary. Read directly (gamma-api, 2026-08-20): `russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-before-2027`, $14.5M turnover, umaResolutionStatus `resolved`, outcomePrices [1, 0], closedTime 2026-05-09 — Yes, the day the Trump-brokered 9-11 May truce began. Two things the guess got wrong. It was not the monthly ladder but the flagship annual market. And the mechanism is not 'looser wording': the rule disclaims durability outright — 'If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to Yes, regardless of whether the ceasefire officially starts afterward.' It does exclude humanitarian pauses and energy/Black-Sea-only deals, so it is not simply a loose market; it prices *an agreement being announced*, an event that neither has to last nor to begin. This model's target is the durable event (in effect ≥30 days), which is a strictly different question, so this market must never be compared against it and its 25.5%-in-May price is a weaker input to the 20% anchor than FORECAST-ANCHORS §4.2 presents it as. Restoring a sourceKey here would be an error.

anchors.claim: A durable Russia–Ukraine ceasefire begins by end-2028
anchors.provenance: FORECAST-ANCHORS §4.2: extrapolated from a Metaculus-derived median first-lasting-agreement date of ~24 Nov 2027.

anchors.claim: Putin ceases to hold power by mid-2027
anchors.documentedDivergence: The model's early-exit hazard is the Phase-2 calibrated one, still pinned by the standalone Russia suite; it is not retuned to meet a market the anchor brief itself calls long-shot-inflated (Polymarket 14%, discounted to an 8% anchor). Ten months is also the shortest horizon in the table, where the actuarial and elite-fracture hazards have had least time to accumulate. Note this row's band edge also sits inside sampling noise, so its verdict is weak evidence in either direction.
anchors.provenance: FORECAST-ANCHORS §5: Polymarket 14% by 30 Jun 2027, discounted for long-shot bias to an 8% anchor. The 14% is the June-2027 rung of Polymarket's 'Putin out as President of Russia by…?' ladder, which read 12.5% on 2026-08-20.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: The market asks about the presidency; the model asks whether the primary machine has left the two Putin-in-power states, which also counts incapacity without formal departure. The long-shot-bias discount is applied to the anchor and stated here rather than silently. HORIZON, corrected in W4.5. This row was bound to `putin-out-before-2027-346` under a note asserting that 'the only open Polymarket market asks by 31 Dec 2026' — so the dashboard compared a through-2027-06 model quantity against a through-2026-12 price for six months. The premise was false: the same event carries an open `putin-out-as-president-of-russia-by-june-30-2027` rung at this anchor's exact horizon, and the key now points there. The slug was the trap — `putin-out-before-2027-346` reads like a 2027 horizon and asks 'by December 31, 2026'. Measured cost of the old binding, 30k/seed 77: the model reads 1.4% through 2026-12 against 4.1% through 2027-06, so the live column was set beside a model number computed over twice its window. One quirk to know before reading the ledger for this row: Gamma reports the *event's* end date on a ladder rung, so this market's recorded note says 'resolves 2026-12-31' while its question asks about June 2027. The question text is the only authority on a rung's horizon; the adapter's header says the same beside the field. LIQUIDITY, stated because the fix is not free: the December rung turns $19.4M and the June-2027 rung $308k, below the brief's own $1M Tier-1 line. A thin price on this row's question beats a deep price on a different one, but the tier stays 1 on the brief's authority rather than being re-graded here, and a reader should weigh the live number accordingly. The live price remains context beside the row, not a re-pricing of the anchor.

anchors.provenance: US-COMMITMENT §5: P(2028 winner reverses drawdown direction) ≈ 0.45-0.55, an (A)-tagged analyst band, Tier-2 by construction. byMonth 29 = 2029-02, one month after the scheduled month-28 inauguration, so the query reads the machine's post-election state, not the campaign. anchors.claim: The Rassemblement National holds the French presidency with an Assembly majority after the 2027 elections
anchors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.3, from Odoxa-Mascaret (May 2026): Bardella 32% in the first round and winning every tested run-off pairing. TIER 3 — a poll-derived band, not a market and not a brief's recommended table, so it is deliberately wide (32 points) and is the weakest-constrained anchor in the model. The band's centre sits well below the polled run-off share for the three reasons the fr.presidential-outcome reference class states: the republican front, the legislative conversion, and eleven months of drift.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: THE FLAG UNDER-READS ITS OWN QUESTION, in a known direction and by a known mechanism. `fr.national_presidency` is the union of the national-majority state ALONE, because the cohabitation state does not record which bloc holds the presidency. An RN president facing a hostile Assembly — a live outcome, weighted at 22 of 100 in the branch and pushed UP by the same nationalist_strength that drives this anchor — is therefore NOT counted here, while a plain reading of the claim would count it. The model should read at or BELOW the anchor for that reason alone, and a reading near the band's floor is evidence about the flag's narrowness before it is evidence about the world. Splitting the cohabitation state by presidential bloc is the named v1.1 fix.

anchors.claim: A Social Democrat-led government takes office after the September 2026 Riksdag election
anchors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.4: red-green bloc 52-55% against the governing bloc's 42-46%, Social Democrats largest at ~33%, three weeks before the poll. TIER 3 — a poll-derived band, not a market. Deliberately wide (34 points) for the reason the se.election-outcome reference class states: Swedish bloc polling tightens into election day and 2022 went the other way from a similar position. THE SHORTEST-HORIZON ANCHOR IN THE MODEL: it resolves on 2026-09-13, inside the model's own first month, and government formation normally completes by November — the window runs to end-2026 to cover formation rather than the vote.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: The flag resolves on a red-green government TAKING OFFICE, not on the bloc winning the most votes or seats. Those come apart exactly in the case the reference class names: 2022, where the larger bloc by one measure did not form the government. A reader scoring this row after the election must score it on who took office, and if the election produces a formation crisis first, the flag can still resolve true later in the window — which is why the window runs to end-2026 rather than to the election month.

anchors.claim: An SDP-led government takes office following the April 2027 Eduskunta election
anchors.provenance: G4.A, fetched 2026-08-29; centre re-derived by the block's adversarial review. The August 2026 Yle poll (via Helsinki Times) has SDP FIRST at 23.8% against the NCP's 17.0%, the lead widening 0.6pp on the prior round; the same outlet's spring coverage of the HS series ('SDP lead narrows as Left Alliance breaks record') is the measured drift risk, fetched in the same session. CENTRE DERIVED, not felt: P(SDP largest at the 2027-04 election | +6.8pp eight months out) is read at ~0.65, times the largest-party-takes-PM regularity — every Finnish government since 1991 has been led from the largest party — discounted to ~0.9 for formation friction, giving 0.585, rounded to 0.60. TIER 3, se.red-green-2026's shape under G4.A section 1.4's amended rule, 40 points wide [0.40, 0.80] because eight months of drift dominate the derivation. Model read 47.7% at registration (6000 runs, seed 77), measured BEFORE this band was authored — the in-band margin is consistency, not an out-of-sample pass. Window to end 2027-07, three months past the election.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: Resolves on an SDP-led government taking office by end 2027-07, not on SDP's vote share or seat count -- the largest-party regularity is the ARGUMENT for the band, not the resolution criterion.

anchors.claim: An Isamaa-led government takes office following the March 2027 Riigikogu election
anchors.provenance: G4.A, fetched 2026-08-29; centre re-derived and the majority sentence corrected by the block's adversarial review. PolitPro's poll trend has Isamaa FIRST at 26.5% against Keskerakond's 21.8% (SDE 14.2, EKRE 13.8, Reform 12.6), and the ERR ratings series agrees ('Isamaa doubles its lead over Center Party'). The incumbent Reform-led coalition is ALREADY a minority at t=0 — 50/101 after the August 2026 defections, this pack's own michal-coalition record — and is projected to fall further. CENTRE DERIVED, not felt: P(Isamaa largest at the 2027-03 election | +4.7pp seven months out) is read at ~0.55 from the lead's size against Estonian poll drift, times P(Isamaa LEADS the government | largest) at ~0.8 — Estonian formation does not mechanically follow first place (2016: the government formed around the runner-up), though no cordon applies to Isamaa — giving 0.44, rounded to 0.45. TIER 3, se.red-green-2026's shape under G4.A section 1.4's amended rule: the band is 40 points [0.25, 0.65] because seven months of drift dominate every term of that arithmetic. Model read 50.8% at registration (6000 runs, seed 77), measured BEFORE this band was authored — the in-band margin is consistency, not an out-of-sample pass. Window to end 2027-06, three months past the election.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: Resolves on an Isamaa-LED government TAKING OFFICE by end 2027-06 -- not on Isamaa winning the most votes or seats. Those come apart in Estonian practice: the largest party has been left in opposition before under coalition cordons. Score on who leads the government that takes office, and if formation is still unresolved at the window's close, the flag is FALSE even if Isamaa later forms.

anchors.claim: A post-election government takes office following the 3 October 2026 Saeima election, by end January 2027
anchors.provenance: G4.A: RECORDED FORECAST, no band -- and the missing band is the finding, not missing evidence. The source number 0.90 is a JUDGMENT-BEARING tier-3 number, and says so: the public record prices EVENTUAL formation at ~1.0 (every Saeima election since 1993 has seated a government) and formation-within-this-window at 2 for 2 in the last two cycles (second Karins cabinet sworn 2022-12-14, ~2.4 months; Karins cabinet sworn 2019-01-23, ~3.6 months and eight days inside a January boundary) -- the 0.90 is that record read onto the ~4-month window and discounted BY JUDGMENT, not by any source, for this cycle's fragmentation (PolitPro / LSM 2026-08-27: United List ~18.7%, For Stability ~16.4%, Latvia First ~14.8%, no bloc near a majority, the caretaker PM's party leading). The MODEL reads 48.3% (6000 runs, seed 77): an enforced band anywhere near the record would breach on first run, and gate G-A.6 forbids shipping a band chosen to fail, so the ~42-point gap ships as a recorded divergence instead. Its cause is structural and measured (G4.A-REPORT-2026-08-29 section 2.2): this machine carries exactly one transition, fired only by the scheduled election, so formation-crisis cannot resolve between elections. Named successor: a formation-resolution mechanism for the five E1-shape machines. Resolves 2027-01 -- the roster's earliest scoreable row after se.red-green-2026.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: Within the window the model can only enter this state AT the election month -- the machine has no formation-resolution transition -- while real Latvian formations complete one to four months after the vote (2022: +2.4 months; 2018-19: +3.6). The window runs to end January 2027 so the real-world question ('was a post-election government seated by end January') is scoreable as worded; a real formation completing in February or March resolves FALSE here exactly as the claim says, and the structural gap this row exists to record is documented in G4.A-REPORT section 2.2. Score the claim as worded; never re-window it to rescue either side.

anchors.claim: The Neutrality Initiative is approved in the 27 September 2026 federal popular vote, entrenching perpetual armed neutrality in the Federal Constitution
anchors.provenance: THE MODEL'S FIRST RECORDED FORECAST (C4.11 R3), AND IT DECLARES NO BAND ON PURPOSE. Primary sources read live on 2026-08-25, not glossed. SOURCE: Polymarket market 'will-the-safeguarding-swiss-neutrality-neutrality-initiative-initiative-be-approved-in-switzerlands-september-27-2026-popular-vote-20260713144919277', inside event 'switzerlands-september-referendum-what-will-pass-20260713144919276', read from the Gamma API: outcomePrices ["0.022","0.978"], $23,823 market volume, $69,908 market liquidity ($33,947 / $108,201 across the event's two markets), endDate 2026-09-27, open. Its rules text: 'This market will resolve to Yes if the listed referendum is approved under the applicable legal threshold in the specified popular vote', resolving on 'the official certified referendum results published by Swiss government authorities, such as the Swiss Federal Chancellery'. BALLOT CONFIRMED AT THE FEDERAL COUNCIL'S OWN PORTAL (admin.ch/en/popular-vote-on-27-september-2026, fetched 2026-08-25): 'On 27 September 2026, Swiss citizens will vote on two proposals' -- the Neutrality Initiative and the Food Initiative, both plain federal popular initiatives, neither carrying a counter-proposal. TIER 2, NOT TIER 1, and the reason is arithmetic rather than modesty: $23.8k of volume is not the 'liquid market' tier 1 describes. The roster's own working standard is bg.json calling $122k 'genuinely liquid' and gr.json weighing a $1.27m market; this is a fifth of the former. Real money and published rules, thinly traded. WHY NO BAND. A band is a calibration constraint the suite enforces, and there is no band here that would not be one of two dishonest things. The model reads 27.2% (16,000 runs) against the market's 2.2%: any band drawn round the market makes this a breach on the first run, and the only fix for a breach is to retune ch.neutrality-vote's 74/26 base weights -- a deliberately argued split with its own provenance, retuned to match a market, which is the exact move the calibration doctrine exists to forbid. A band wide enough to contain both is not a claim about anything. So the row records BOTH numbers and constrains neither, which is what a recorded forecast is for. WHAT MAKES IT WORTH RECORDING: the correspondence is exact -- the market's 'approved under the applicable legal threshold' IS the Art. 139/195 double majority, and the model's ch.constitutional-neutrality state is entered by nothing except the initiative passing -- and it resolves on 2026-09-27, THIRTY-THREE DAYS AFTER THIS ROW WAS WRITTEN. The gap is 25.0 points and the ratio 12.4x. One of the two numbers is about to be wrong in public, which is the whole argument of design doc S11 for keeping a prospective ledger at all. THE DISAGREEMENT IS NOT ADJUDICATED HERE AND NO CONSTANT MOVED. ch.neutrality-vote's own provenance argues 26 rather than the ~11% its base rate implies because 42% yes in the August 2026 gfs.bern/SRG wave (n>17,000) 'is not a trivial starting position'; the market, holding the same polls plus the double-majority requirement and the 11.3% historical initiative pass rate, says 2.2%. Whether a yes-vote-share is being read as a pass-probability is a real question and it belongs to whichever block re-prices ch, with this row's outcome in hand.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: THREE WAYS THE SOURCE AND THE CLAIM COULD COME APART, none of them live today, all recorded before the fact because that is the only time it counts. (1) COUNTER-PROPOSAL. The market resolves YES if 'either the popular initiative or, where applicable, the federal counter-proposal is approved'. The model's ch.constitutional-neutrality state represents the INITIATIVE's text passing -- perpetual armed neutrality, no alliance cooperation except under attack, near-total sanctions ban. A counter-proposal carrying weaker text would resolve the market YES and would NOT be this state. Confirmed inapplicable on 2026-08-25: the Federal Council's ballot page lists two plain popular initiatives and no counter-proposal. If that changes, this row's market half is void, not merely noisy. (2) TIMING. The market resolves NO if the result is not definitively known by the next Swiss referendum date. The model's flag carries no such condition; a delayed but eventual YES splits them. (3) HORIZON. The claim's window closes with the vote month itself (throughEndOf 2026-09). The flag is cumulative over the horizon and the state is absorbing, so a later entry -- there is no other way in, but the schema permits one -- would be true of the flag and false of this claim. SCORE THIS ROW ON THE FEDERAL CHANCELLERY'S CERTIFIED RESULT FOR THE INITIATIVE ITSELF, not on the market's settlement.

anchors.claim: A NATO–Russia military encounter above the munition threshold occurs by end-2026 — a two-way exchange, or NATO downing a reusable Russian platform; intercepting one-way munitions bound for Ukraine is excluded
anchors.documentedDivergence: RATE, on a class both sides now scope the same way. The scope question this note used to pose — whether to count Russian fire at NATO ISR platforms outside NATO territory — was decided in W3 and implemented: the model prices the market's own geography-free, symmetric reading, and `russian-fire-on-nato` is authored on exactly the two cases that reading admits (the Sep-2022 Su-27/RC-135 missile release and the Nov-2022 Syria SAM/MQ-9 engagement). It carries 0.17 of the model's 0.25/yr. What remains is a straight disagreement about the RATE of a shared class: 0.22-0.45/yr on that record against the market's 0.67-0.68/yr — 1.5-2.7x, and 2x the market's own 2026 median for the same year. Zero of the ten NATO weapon discharges over allied territory since 2022 are verified engagements of a reusable Russian platform — six fail on the munition clause this market states by name, four on attribution or on never having been identified; its family has resolved three legs No across exactly those events, and a companion market on downing a Russian drone BY ANY MEANS trades near-certain over two weeks while this one trades 22.5% over four and a half months. That gap is the exclusion, priced. Three things would still settle the rate (ENGAGEMENT-THRESHOLD §5): an adjudicated 'aimed at NATO' attribution on a Romanian shoot-down, whether the on-chain Gerbera-as-munition amendment binds the 2026 legs, and the type of the unidentified Cankiri object. The band is a Tier-1 anchor and is not moved to fit the model.
anchors.provenance: ENGAGEMENT-THRESHOLD §1, §4, correcting three errors carried from FORECAST-ANCHORS §3.2. Polymarket 'NATO x Russia military clash by 31 Dec 2026', mid 0.225 (the site's '23%' is round-half-up), leg volume $1.27M and $4.26M across the family — not the '$2M' previously recorded. The brief's causal claim that the price was 'driven by the 30 Jul 2026 Kh-101 incident' is also wrong: the re-pricing ran 0.185 → 0.305 on the 24-26 Jul Romanian shoot-down sequence, with the Kh-101 worth a further ~5pp after a decay — and BOTH drivers are events this market's own rules exclude.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: THRESHOLD, and it is not the one the anchor brief assumed. Read off the market page (NATO-RUSSIA-ENGAGEMENT-THRESHOLD-BRIEF §1), a qualifying encounter is a two-way exchange of fire or NATO 'shooting down UAVs which are not munitions'; intercepting one-way attack or loitering munitions aimed at a third party is excluded by name. FORECAST-ANCHORS §3.2 characterised this market as resolving on ANY direct engagement, tagged (B) because every fetch was blocked when it was written. The model quantity is now the market's class, not the looser one. ALSO A WINDOW MISMATCH: the market runs to 31 Dec 2026 and was priced in Aug 2026, so it covers about 4.5 forward months against this row's 4.

anchors.claim: Armed conflict between Russia and a non-US NATO member before 2030
anchors.provenance: FRI Oct-2024, 'Can Humanity Achieve a Century of Nuclear Peace?', read directly (W4.4 §1) rather than through FORECAST-ANCHORS §3.2, which reported it correctly: 'The median expert forecast a 10% chance of this happening before 2030, and the median superforecaster a 5.5% chance', for conflict between Russia and a NATO member other than the USA. Band shaded up for staleness (pre-Poland-missile).
anchors.resolutionMismatch: TWO reasons this row reads as an UPPER bound on the FRI-worded quantity, and the second is the larger of the two and was not written down until W4.4 read the source. (a) FRI asks about armed conflict with a non-US member; the model's clash rung does not distinguish which ally is engaged, so this row reads as an UPPER bound on the FRI-worded quantity. W3 removed the larger half of this note: the rung used to double as the Polymarket 'any exchange of fire' threshold, which is materially lower than FRI's 'armed conflict', and the 2026 engagement row shared it. That row now names its own quantity, so `clash` is the armed-conflict grade only and the brief's own three-threshold split (engagement / armed conflict / Article-5 war, §3.2) is reproduced in the model. (b) FRI's threshold is not 'armed conflict' colloquially: the question resolves on **more than 500 deaths in militarized conflict between the parties in one calendar year**, by default from Uppsala Conflict Data Program data. The model's clash rung is an escalation-ladder state, not a 500-battle-death count, and is certainly reached at lower intensity — so the model quantity sits above the FRI quantity for this reason too, and by more than (a). Both push the same way, which is why the row can be read as a one-sided bound rather than a muddle. Deliberately NOT a documentedDivergence: the row is inside its band, so a note here would be a dormant excuse pre-authorising a future miss in either direction rather than a judgment about a disagreement that exists.

anchors.claim: An Article-5-grade Russia–NATO war occurs by 2035
anchors.documentedDivergence: Carried forward from W1 §4, which recorded this outcome at 4.3% against a band widened down to a 2.5% low edge to span the superforecaster/expert split: FRI puts Russia–NATO conflict involving the US before 2030 at 1.8% (supers) against 5% (experts), a near-threefold disagreement that a single Tier-3 midpoint hides. This registry keeps the brief's published 6-15% band rather than W1's widened one, deliberately — so the disagreement stays visible on the dashboard every run instead of being absorbed into a band edge where nobody looks at it again.
anchors.provenance: FORECAST-ANCHORS §3.2: assessment built on FRI plus European intel-chief statements about a 2029-33 reconstitution window. No live Article-5 CP was recoverable. HORIZON CONVENTION: the brief writes this row's horizon as 'by 2035' while the two market-sourced rows in the same table say 'before 2035'. Read here as 'before 2035' (through end-2034) for consistency with them. W3 called the twelve-month reading 'not load-bearing' on the grounds that the band is 9 points wide. W4.5 measured it and that was wrong: at 30k runs the shipped reading gives 5.2/5.4/5.2% on seeds 77/20260818/4242 (-6.3/-5.0/-6.2 SE below the 6% floor — decisively below), while reading it as through-2035-12 gives 5.8/5.9/5.8% (-1.7/-0.6/-1.4 SE — inside sampling noise, verdict undecided). The twelve months are worth ~0.6 points on a row sitting ~0.8 points from its floor, so the calendar choice decides whether this row is a settled divergence or an open question. The 'before' reading stands; what changes is that it is now a load-bearing judgment and is labelled as one.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: Article 5 invocation is a political choice that lags kinetic events — it has been invoked once ever. The model's `war` rung is the kinetic threshold, so it should read at or above an invocation-based anchor.

anchors.claim: China launches an invasion attempt against Taiwan proper by end-2026
anchors.documentedDivergence: W1 divergence #1 at its sharpest horizon. `invasion-launch` is hard-gated on PLA readiness ≥45, which the readiness factor cannot reach from its 2026-09 value within four months, so the model holds this foreclosed on materiel grounds rather than merely unlikely. The gate is the PLA-READINESS brief's lift and C2 constraint and is deliberate; a market pricing 4% is pricing a possibility this model treats as structurally unavailable, which is a substantive disagreement about the constraint, not about the odds.
anchors.provenance: FORECAST-ANCHORS §1.2: Polymarket (liquid, Tier 1) ~3.8% Yes; path 30% Dec-2025 → 13% early-2026 → ~4%.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: Read from the market's own rules text (gamma-api, 2026-08-20), which contradicts what this note said until W4.5 on both of its points. The market resolves Yes if China 'commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of the Republic of China (Taiwan)' — it does NOT require a landing or a sustained assault, only commencement. And 'Territory under the administration of the Republic of China including any inhabited islands will qualify, however uninhabited islands will not qualify' — so a Kinmen or Matsu seizure DOES resolve it Yes, where this note previously claimed outlying-island seizures did not. The market is therefore materially broader than the model query on both counts, and should read above a Taiwan-proper-only model: the error ran in the direction that overstated agreement. Gray-zone action and quarantine still do not resolve it. `invasion-launch` is hard-gated on PLA lift readiness and remains the closest available match, but the comparison is looser than the old note admitted.

anchors.claim: China attacks or blockades Taiwan during 2026
anchors.documentedDivergence: W2/W3 divergence — SHORT-HORIZON ESCALATION FLOOR. Reaching this flag needs the cn-tw ladder to leave its base rung, which takes a hazard draw plus a state transition, and the window this row covers is four months (2026-09 to 2026-12). Unlike the ru-nato near-term row — which W2 filed under the same cause and which W3 found to be a mis-mapped anchor instead — this one is not a cold-start artifact that grounding the initial rung would fix: the pack's base rung is the correct starting state, since the standing gray-zone coercion campaign IS the 2026 status quo. It is the quarantine hazard (4.5%/yr, gated on tension >= 60) that makes a four-month climb rare. Read together with this row's window mismatch, which is the larger effect: the anchor covers all of calendar 2026 and eight of its months had already passed uneventfully before the model's t=0.
anchors.provenance: FORECAST-ANCHORS §1.2: Metaculus Q41139, n=98, 26%. Read by the brief as an upper bound on kinetic-or-blockade action in 2026.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: Deliberately broad: 'attack OR blockade' plausibly includes outlying islands and sustained quarantine. The union flag is the like-for-like counterpart; any single rung would understate it. ALSO A WINDOW MISMATCH: the question covers all of calendar 2026, but the model's t=0 is 2026-09, so only four of its twelve months are in scope. The comparison is over an overlap, not a shared window, and the model is structurally incapable of speaking to the eight months that already happened.

anchors.claim: A full-scale blockade of Taiwan occurs by end-2030

anchors.claim: India conducts a cross-border strike episode against Pakistan by end-2026
anchors.documentedDivergence: C3 §2: the pre-recorded direction realized, and the measured decomposition apportions it. The model reads ~1.2% by month 4 against the 8-14 band — and 9.8% by month 12, INSIDE the band — so the disagreement is the window, not the strike conditional (the engine's crisis-resolution strike share is 79.4% at t=0, and the onset composite 0.228/yr sits in its own registered bracket). Two mechanisms, both structural: (1) the 4-month cold start from a standing TENSION state with no live crisis at t=0 — P(any crisis opens by month 4) is only 5.5%; (2) the crisis dwell (1-10 months, deliberately blending the 2001-02/2008 long-crisis era with the post-2016 11-15-day era) schedules most within-window crises to resolve after the anchor month — of the 5.5% that open, under a fifth reach the strike rung in-window against the 79% era share. A market pricing 11% for its last 4.3 months is pricing attack-to-strike sequences inside ONE month (the realized post-2016 tempo), which a monthly-resolution ladder with a ≥1-month crisis rung structurally underproduces. Splitting the dwell by era is the named v1.1 refinement; the band is not moved and the dwell is not retuned.
anchors.provenance: Polymarket 'India strike on Pakistan by...?' — the 'December 31, 2026' bucket at 11%, fetched live 2026-08-21 twice (research agent and session independently; both read 11%). D5.2 paid the C0-refresh debt: the sourceKey was wired after the rung was re-verified live 2026-08-23 (open, accepting orders, 13.5% — in-band), through the model-carried fetch plan; the refresh loop now re-prices this row.
anchors.resolutionMismatch: The market's rules count only Indian aerial bombs, drones, or missiles IMPACTING Pakistani territory — interceptions outside Pakistani airspace, ground raids, and artillery exchanges are all excluded. The model's `strikes` flag is the whole S3 band, which INCLUDES the 2016-class deniable ground raid, so the flag is slightly broader than the market's question and should read at or a little above a rules-exact match. Recorded in advance: if the model lands BELOW band, the first thing to examine is the 4-month window from a standing tension start (the same cold-start shape as W2 §2), not the strike conditional — the divergence taxonomy exists for this.

Alliance rearmament is the sum of member defence efforts; the UK is one of the three largest contributors to it. A second channel was authored — each member's nationalist_strength into nato.populist_pressure — and it is NOT shipped. A coupling adds a CONSTANT drift w*(source-50)/month, so a source durably above 50 shifts its target's EQUILIBRIUM by drift/reversion rather than by w: the first sizing (0.0105 total) shifted nato.populist_pressure by +8.0 points and drove P(nato fragmented) from 18.9% to 26.2%, past the EUROPE-POLITICS briefed band of <0.20; re-sized to a +2.0 point shift it still read 20.7%. coverage.note: Exact. The state union IS the class: ru.main's states other than the two in which Putin holds office, and those states are non-returnable, so ever-occupied and terminal agree. Reads 75.2% at 6000/seed 77 on the C2.d composition (75.0% before the us pack joined — cited values are composition-stamped because B1 measured that the composition moves them).

Exact: the union is the machine's own `contested-interregnum` outcome class. Reads 40.2% at 6000/seed 77 (C2.d composition; 41.5% pre-us), i.e. P(contested | exit) = 53.5% against `incumbent_exit`'s 75.2% — the majority of modelled Putin exits pass through an open contest, which is a statement of this pack's succession weights, not of a brief (the pack states no contested-at-exit rate directly; use `simcli transition-shares`, not hand-read base weights, to interrogate it).

The `fragmentation` state is absorbing and is reached only via `to-fragmentation` from interregnum or violent-interregnum, i.e. after central authority has already contested. Reads 9.1% (C2.d composition; 10.0% pre-us). NOTE the adjacent band: `ru-nato` and `cn-tw` carry their own fragmentation-like flags meaning different things — see nato's declaration.

An alliance has no chief executive. `nato.alliance` tracks cohesion (cohesive / strained / us-decoupled / fragmented), not officeholding, and no amount of authoring would give it an incumbent to lose.

Follows from the `incumbent-exit` absence above, and no amount of authoring changes it: a subset class of a notApplicableByKind class is notApplicableByKind. An alliance with no incumbent has no succession to contest — NATO's secretary-general turnover is real but is not what `nato.alliance` models, and contested SecGen selection is not an intra-elite struggle over who RULES.

IMPORTANT, and the reason this declaration exists rather than a flag: `nato.fragmented` (9.8% at F1, 12,000 runs — down substantially from C2.d-era's 17.6%, because the roster has grown from a handful of polities to 37 since that reading and most individual members are now separately modelled rather than folded into this aggregate; ru.fragmentation's own 9.1% citation is the same C2.d vintage and was not re-measured here, out of F1's scope) looks like an answer and is not. It is ATOP alliance abrogation — members ceasing to honour a pact — whereas the class is PITF loss of central control over territory. Placing either beside the other under one heading would tell a reader NATO and Russia are comparably likely to fall apart, comparing two different literatures with different base rates. Alliance rupture is a real and interesting quantity; it is not this class.

Exact, and in the same state form ru uses. Reads 61.9% at 6000/seed 77 (C2.d composition; 61.0% pre-us). The event form read 53.1% in A2's measurement — a 7.9pp gap caused by `political-crisis` reaching `instability` with no named exit event — so the form is fixed by the vocabulary rather than chosen per pack.

Exact: the machine's one unresolved-contest state. Reads 12.8% at 6000/seed 77 (C2.d composition; 12.6% pre-us), i.e. P(contested | exit) = 20.7% against `incumbent_exit`'s 61.9%. B1 §5 measured this exact quantity as the pilot's largest authored-vs-generated gap — the blind regeneration read it 3× higher from the same corpus paragraph — and the CONDITIONAL is composition-stable where the marginals are not: 20.9% focused (B1's 10.3/49.4), 20.7% four-polity full, 20.7% with the us pack in — three compositions, one split, while the marginals move 11.6pp. The split is a property of the machine; the level is a property of the composition.

The PRC pack models leadership discontinuity, not territorial disintegration: none of cn.party's six states describes loss of central control over territory, and no event triggers one. This is a gap in the pack rather than a fact about the world — a Xinjiang or Tibet secession branch is authorable and simply is not authored. It is NOT `notApplicableByKind`.

`presidential-election` fires in 97.5% of runs — it is the scheduled four-yearly election, i.e. ROUTINE turnover, and `tw.gov` tracks which party won rather than whether an incumbent was lost. The class asks about an incumbent ceasing to hold office as a risk event; routine alternation in a consolidated democracy is not that, and reporting 97.5% under this heading beside Russia's 75.0% would be the single most misleading row the panel could print.

NOT the same reason as `incumbent-exit`'s absence above, and the difference is the point of the taxonomy. Routine alternation is excluded from the parent class as belowThreshold; a CONTESTED succession — an extra-constitutional struggle over who rules — is a real question for a democracy (Taiwan's own martial-law-era transition is precedent that such contests are authorable), and `tw.gov`'s two party-control states simply do not model it. A gap statement, not a nature claim.

Taiwan's sovereignty risk is annexation by an external actor, which is a different class (external subordination, Fazal state death) and is modelled in the cn-tw dyad as `cn-tw.annexation` (9.4%). It is deliberately NOT borrowed into this pack: a polity flag referencing dyad content makes the pack unable to compile without that dyad, which is exactly what a focus-ordered sub-world must be able to do.

The `tw` precedent applied to the other consolidated democracy in the model: `administration-change` is the scheduled quadrennial election, i.e. ROUTINE turnover, and `us.admin` tracks the winner's orientation rather than whether an incumbent was lost. Reporting a near-certain routine alternation beside Russia's 75.0% would be exactly the misleading row the tw declaration refuses to print.

January 6, 2021 is precedent that an extra-constitutional contest over the transfer of power is AUTHORABLE for this polity, and v1 deliberately does not author it: the pack models the politics of external commitment, and pricing a contested-transfer branch is internal-stability content with its own evidentiary bar. A gap statement, not a nature claim — the same reason class as tw's.

No state or event in this pack describes loss of central control over territory, and none is priced. Authorable in principle (secession movements exist in the literature); not authored, and nothing about the dyads this pack exists to serve needs it. NOT `notApplicableByKind` — that reason is reserved for polities where no amount of authoring would produce the machine.

The tw precedent applied to the world's largest democracy: the exit mechanism is the ballot plus actuarial age (8/8 peaceful national alternations since 1952, zero Powell-Thyne coup attempts in 79 years). Read as ever-exit over 120 months it saturates at ~88-92% (age 75→86 plus two scheduled elections) and answers nothing; read as a risk quantity it is below threshold. The one asterisk — the 1975-77 Emergency, ~1.3%/yr unconditioned — is carried by the institutional_erosion factor, not a state ladder (IN brief §3.1).

India has the adjudicators the cn machine lacks: elections, floor tests, the anti-defection law, party organs with the RSS as tie-breaker — regime-level contested succession <2%. The LIVE question, an open BJP factional fight conditional on bjp-post-modi (plausibly 40-60%), is a PARTY-level succession — a different question that must not ship under this class's name (B1 §4's exact trap). Authorable as in.bjp-leadership-contest; not authored.

Zero successful secessions in 79 years against a state that ended or contained every insurgency it faced — Punjab by ~1995, Mizoram 1986, the Maoists declared over March 2026; Kashmir at a two-decade violence low (92 deaths 2025) with an elected government; Manipur is horizontal conflict in which both sides petition Delhi. At this resolution the realistic worst case is President's-Rule-class disorder in one state — a factor excursion, not topology (IN brief §5.4).

The vocabulary's operationalisation is state form over officeholding states, and this machine deliberately tracks regime CONFIGURATION, not the officeholder: Munir's exit — the load-bearing incumbent question (PK brief §5.4) — is an EVENT (munir-exit, flagged munir_exit, ~16% over 120 months as composed), not a state boundary, and the PM's ~20%/yr churn is deliberately no state boundary either. Restructuring to officeholder-resolution states is the named v2 path. The honest asymmetry: contested-succession is ANSWERED below while its parent question is not.

Answered in state form via {army-succession-contest} — a state entered only through munir-exit's contested branch (20 inside the brief's 15-25% band), so the union genuinely means an unresolved leadership contest. A declared SUBSET of an unanswered parent: incumbent-exit is unauthored (see above), so the panel shows P(contested) with the exit denominator carried by the munir_exit flag rather than by a state — shown, not hidden (C3 §1.3).

The 1971 reference class fails on all three of its conditions (PK brief §5.4): no lost interstate war, no foreign armed intervention, no physical separation. Balochistan is ~6% of population under a ~600k army, and record 2025-26 violence is train attacks, not territorial control — modelled as insurgency_intensity, not topology. The brief's authorable pk.baloch_secession low flag (~1-2%) is NOT authored in v1; recorded as the gap.

The tw and us declarations' argument, applied verbatim and for the same reason. The class's fixed operationalisation is the union of machine states in which the t=0 incumbent no longer holds office; over a 120-month horizon containing two scheduled general elections that union approaches certainty through ROUTINE alternation, and printing a near-certain figure beside Russia's 74.9% would be the most misleading row the panel could carry. The genuinely non-routine part — a Prime Minister leaving without a general election, which is what actually happened five weeks before t=0 — IS modelled and IS reported, as uk.mid_term_leader_exit, and it is deliberately not offered as an answer to this class because it is a different question with a different denominator.

Succession to the premiership is decided by a governing party's own leadership rules and, since 1965, has never been contested in the sense this class means — an unresolved leadership dispute leaving the state without a settled chief executive. Burnham's July 2026 succession is the live example: a competitive party election, concluded in four weeks, with an uninterrupted transfer at the palace. No amount of authoring on THIS machine would produce the class's object, which is why the reason is notApplicableByKind rather than notModelled.

Scottish independence is a real branch in the world and is NOT authored here. Recorded exactly as cn's Xinjiang gap is: this is a gap in the pack, not a fact about the world, and it is NOT notApplicableByKind — a second machine over the Union's territorial integrity is authorable and simply is not authored in v1. The 2014 referendum and the post-2016 constitutional argument are the reference material a v1.1 would price it from.

The tw and us argument, applied for the same reason. Over 120 months containing two scheduled Bundestag elections, the class's fixed state-form union approaches certainty through ROUTINE alternation, and printing that beside Russia's 74.9% would be misleading. The non-routine part — a chancellor leaving mid-term, which has happened four times since 1949 — IS modelled and IS reported as de.mid_term_leader_exit, and is deliberately not offered as this class's answer because it has a different denominator.

The Basic Law resolves chancellor succession by construction: the constructive vote of no confidence (Art. 67) requires the Bundestag to elect a successor IN THE SAME VOTE that removes the incumbent, which is a mechanism designed precisely to make an unresolved succession impossible. It was used successfully once, in 1982, and it produced a chancellor the same day. No amount of authoring on this machine would produce the class's object.

No state or event here describes loss of central control over territory, and none is priced. Authorable in principle; nothing about the alliance dials this pack exists to feed needs it. NOT notApplicableByKind — that reason is reserved for polities where no amount of authoring would produce the machine.

The tw and us argument. The horizon contains two scheduled presidential elections and Macron is CONSTITUTIONALLY BARRED from contesting the first, so the class's fixed state-form union is not merely near-certain but certain by month 8 — which makes it the clearest case in the model of a class reporting a calendar rather than a risk. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as fr.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.030/yr, the lowest of the four packs.

France is the one of the four D8 packs where this class has a genuine referent and is NOT authored, so the honest reason is unauthored rather than notApplicableByKind. Art. 7 hands an interim presidency to the president of the Senate with an election in 20-35 days — orderly on paper — but a mid-term vacancy under a hung Assembly with the RN leading the polls is exactly the condition under which the succession would be contested in substance if not in law. Pricing it would need a reference class the Fifth Republic has only two members of (1969, 1974), both under a functioning majority. Recorded as the pack's most interesting gap.

No state or event here describes loss of central control over territory. Authorable in principle (New Caledonia is the live case in the world, and the 2024 unrest there is real); not authored, and nothing this pack exists to feed needs it.

The tw and us argument. The horizon contains THREE scheduled Riksdag elections — more than any other polity in the model — so the class's fixed state-form union is dominated by routine alternation more thoroughly here than anywhere else. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as se.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.049/yr.

Swedish government formation is settled by the Speaker's mandate and the negative-parliamentarism rule: a prime minister takes office unless an absolute majority votes against, which is a mechanism designed to prevent an unresolved succession and which resolved even the 134-day 2018 crisis without a vacancy in the office. The formation-crisis STATE models the delay, which is a durability phenomenon; it is not an unresolved leadership contest, and no authoring on this machine would produce one.

Sweden is a unitary state with no secessionist movement of any scale, no autonomous region contesting central authority, and no territorial dispute. This is the only one of the four D8 packs where the absence is a fact about the polity rather than a gap in the pack — for the UK it is notModelled because Scottish independence is real and unauthored.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by the scheduled 2027 Sejm election, an ordinary alternation. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as pl.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.243/yr and pl.president_mid_term_exit at 0.010/yr.

Polish government formation, like Sweden's, resolves through ordinary parliamentary arithmetic (a Sejm confidence vote) rather than through an unresolved leadership contest. The formation-crisis STATE models the delay, which is a durability phenomenon, not a contested succession. The president-exit event has no succession ambiguity either: the constitution names the Sejm Marshal as acting president pending a new election.
Poland is a unitary state with no active secessionist movement or contested territorial claim of any modelled scale.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by the scheduled 2027 Eduskunta election, an ordinary alternation. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as fi.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.114/yr and fi.president_mid_term_exit at 0.0125/yr.
Finnish government formation resolves through ordinary Eduskunta arithmetic, not an unresolved leadership contest. The formation-delay STATE models the delay, which is a durability phenomenon.
Finland is a unitary state (the autonomous Aland Islands notwithstanding, which have no active independence movement of modelled scale) with no contested territorial claim.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by the scheduled 2027 Riigikogu election, an ordinary alternation. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as ee.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.235/yr.

Estonian government formation resolves through ordinary Riigikogu arithmetic. The presidential-selection event schedules a genuinely live succession (see its own provenance) but the mechanism itself -- a two-thirds vote or electoral-college fallback -- is a defined constitutional procedure, not an unresolved contest in the sense this scenario class tracks; this pack does not model who is elected.

Estonia is a unitary state with no active secessionist movement of modelled scale, notwithstanding the concentrated Russian-speaking population in Ida-Viru county tracked by russian_minority_alignment -- a political-representation factor, not a territorial claim.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by the scheduled Oct 2026 Saeima election, one month into this pack's own horizon. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as lv.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.364/yr, the highest rate in the roster.

Latvian government formation resolves through ordinary Saeima arithmetic (a confidence vote on the President's nominee), not an unresolved leadership contest. The formation-crisis STATE models the delay, which is a durability phenomenon.

Latvia is a unitary state with no active secessionist movement of modelled scale, notwithstanding a large Russian-speaking population (~24-25%) -- currently the LEAST politically mobilised of the three Baltic states behind any single vehicle (For Stability! polls only 2.5%, below threshold), which is why this pack does NOT carry a russian_minority_alignment factor, unlike ee.json.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by the scheduled 2028 Seimas election, an ordinary alternation. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as lt.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.206/yr and lt.president_mid_term_exit at 0.030/yr.

Lithuanian government formation resolves through ordinary Seimas confidence votes, and the presidency's succession mechanism (the Seimas Speaker as acting president) is a defined constitutional procedure, not an unresolved contest. The formation-crisis STATE models delay, a durability phenomenon.

Lithuania is a unitary state with no active secessionist movement of modelled scale. The Polish-minority-aligned LLRA-KSS electoral vehicle (~3.89%, three constituency seats) is constituency-based ethnic-Polish representation, a materially smaller and differently-shaped phenomenon than Estonia's russian_minority_alignment factor -- see ee.json's own provenance for the comparison this brief draws across the three Baltic states.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by the scheduled 2030 and 2034 elections. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as hu.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.083/yr -- the lowest such rate in the roster -- and hu.president_mid_term_exit at 0.185/yr.

Hungary uses a CONSTRUCTIVE vote of no confidence: a successor must be named in the same motion, so the mechanism cannot produce a vacancy. It has been used once since 1990 (2009, Gyurcsany to Bajnai) and resolved immediately by construction. The presidential succession is likewise defined -- the Speaker acts pending a new election.

Hungary is a unitary state with no secessionist movement of modelled scale and no contested territorial claim. NOTE what this absence does NOT cover: the contested-legitimacy condition the brief flags as Hungary's most important domestic risk (Fidesz's 21 July 2026 'Declaration of Resistance' and its refusal to participate in constitutional appointments) is a dispute about who legitimately holds office, not about the state's territorial integrity, and is deliberately unauthored in v1 rather than folded into this class.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by the scheduled 2027 and 2032 elections. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as it.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.217/yr and it.president_mid_term_exit at 0.050/yr.

Italian government formation resolves through the President's appointment power plus a confidence vote in both chambers -- a defined procedure that has never failed to produce a government, and whose fallback (a technocratic cabinet) is modelled here as a STATE rather than as a contest. The presidential succession is likewise defined: the Senate President acts. NOTE one dated constitutional constraint the model does not otherwise capture: from 3 August 2028, Article 88 bars the President from dissolving the chambers in the final six months of his term, so a government crisis in that window has no early-election exit.

Italy is a unitary state with strong regional autonomy but no secessionist movement of modelled scale -- the Lega's own northern-independence project was formally abandoned when it became a national party, and no current parliamentary force contests the state's territorial integrity.
The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by the scheduled 2027, 2031 and 2035 elections. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as es.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.042/yr.

Spain's motion of censure is CONSTRUCTIVE (Art. 113): it must name an alternative prime minister, so the mechanism cannot produce a vacancy -- the one time it succeeded, in June 2018, Sanchez took office directly the next day. Investiture failure produces a formation crisis, modelled here as a STATE, not an unresolved leadership contest.

THE FIRST PACK IN PROGRAMME E TO DECLARE THIS ABSENCE AS A GAP RATHER THAN A NATURE CLAIM, and the reason is Catalonia. Every D8/E1 pack declared notApplicableByKind because no secessionist movement of scale existed; Spain's does. The CEO barometer of 9 July 2026 reads 45% yes / 51% no on independence -- up six points in six months, the narrowest gap in years -- with about 75% saying they would participate in a unilateral referendum, an asymmetry between referendum DEMAND and independence SUPPORT that is the real quantity. The Constitutional Court rules on Puigdemont's amparo appeal in October 2026, inside this model's first months. It is NOT authored in v1 because authoring it requires deciding what 'independence' means when the fastest-growing pro-independence party (Alianca Catalana, polling 20-22 Catalan seats and overtaking Junts) is a nativist one -- a reference-class judgement, not a hazard rate. Recorded exactly as uk.json records Scottish independence.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by the scheduled 2030 and 2034 elections. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as nl.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.037/yr -- the lowest in the model. NOTE that nl.cabinet_collapsed at ~0.24/yr is NOT this class: a Dutch cabinet falling does not remove the incumbent, and the whole pack is built on keeping the two apart.

Dutch cabinet formation is conducted by the Tweede Kamer itself -- since a March 2012 change to its own Rules of Order the verkenner, informateur and formateur are appointed by the House, not the monarch, so the head of state has no role in it at all. A fallen cabinet continues in a defined demissionary status until a successor is formed; the mechanism cannot produce a vacancy or an unresolved contest. The caretaker-cabinet STATE models the interval, which is a durability phenomenon.

The Netherlands is a unitary state with no secessionist movement of modelled scale. The Caribbean constituent countries of the Kingdom (Aruba, Curacao, Sint Maarten) sit outside the European territory this pack claims and have no active independence contest of the kind this class tracks.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by the scheduled 2029 and 2034 elections. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as be.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.066/yr. NOTE that be.government_collapsed at ~0.17/yr is NOT this class: a Belgian government falling leaves the prime minister in office as caretaker, and keeping the two apart is what this pack is built on.

Belgian government formation is a negotiation conducted under the King's informateur/formateur procedure, and its failure mode is a caretaker cabinet of indefinite duration -- modelled here as a STATE with a dwell, never a vacancy. The office is never unoccupied; that is precisely what makes 541 days survivable.

THE SECOND PACK IN THE ROSTER TO DECLARE THIS AS A GAP RATHER THAN A NATURE CLAIM, after es.json and Catalonia. Belgium's Flemish-Walloon cleavage is real, constitutionally entrenched and load-bearing: Art. 43 splits both Houses into linguistic groups, Art. 4 requires a majority in EACH group plus two-thirds overall for special laws, Art. 54's alarm-bell procedure lets three-quarters of one group suspend a bill, and the sitting government is led by a confederalist party. It is NOT authored in v1 for a specific and checkable reason: the arithmetic says nothing can move this legislature. The coalition holds 80 of 150 and needs 100 for the seventh state reform its own agreement promises -- it clears both linguistic-group majorities but is twenty votes short of two-thirds, and the available twenty sit with the PS, Anders, or a Vlaams Belang under cordon sanitaire. A state-disintegration branch whose gate cannot open inside the horizon would be authoring a number rather than a mechanism.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by the scheduled 2028 and 2033 elections. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as lu.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.030/yr, the lowest such rate in the model.

Luxembourg government formation resolves through ordinary Chamber arithmetic under the Grand Duke's formateur procedure, in 40 days at the most recent instance. The head of state's own succession is hereditary and executed smoothly in October 2025 when Grand Duke Henri abdicated after 25 years and Guillaume V acceded, having served as Regent for the preceding year -- a defined constitutional procedure, not a contest.

Luxembourg is a unitary state with no secessionist movement and no territorial dispute. WORTH RECORDING because it is the pack's real structure: Luxembourg's exposure is external rather than internal -- 47% of its salaried workforce commutes from France, Germany and Belgium, and finance is a quarter to a third of output -- so shocks arrive through its neighbours' economies rather than through its own institutions. That is a coupling story, and this programme has ruled couplings out until nato's aggregate attractor is re-based, so v1 carries the internal politics only and says so.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by elections -- and in Austria's case by MORE of them than the calendar shows, since early dissolution is the ordinary path. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as at.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.099/yr.

Austrian government formation resolves through the President's appointment power plus a Nationalrat confidence position, and its failure mode is a caretaker chancellor -- modelled here as a STATE with a dwell, not an unresolved contest. The one successful no-confidence vote in Second Republic history (Kurz, 27 May 2019) produced an orderly handover to an expert government within days.
Austria is a federal republic with no secessionist movement of modelled scale and no contested territorial claim.

THE ROSTER'S FIRST TYPED ABSENCE ON THIS CLASS FOR A STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A THRESHOLD REASON, and it is the pack's central claim. Switzerland has no head of government to lose: executive power is collective in the seven-member Federal Council, the presidency rotates annually by design and confers no authority beyond chairing, and there is no confidence vote, no recall and no dissolution -- parliament cannot remove a Federal Councillor mid-term. The class's quantity is not merely small here, it does not exist; recording it as belowThreshold would imply a low rate where the honest statement is 'no referent'. The three analogous quantities were considered and are recorded in the pack's own reference class: involuntary non-re-election of a sitting Councillor (four times in 178 years, and only ever at a quadrennial renewal), a magic-formula composition change (four in 67 years), and policy reversal by referendum -- the last of which this pack models, because it is the only one that couples to anything else in the world.

Follows from the incumbent-exit absence and is not a separate judgement: an executive that cannot be removed cannot have a contested succession. Federal Council resignations are routine, individual and non-crisis -- announced months ahead, the seat refilled by the Assembly for the remainder of the term, the government continuing unchanged. Amherd's is the recent template: announced 15 January 2025, successor elected 12 March, in office 1 April.

Switzerland is a federation of 26 cantons with no secessionist movement of modelled scale. The Jura question -- the one modern instance of a territorial dispute -- was resolved through the constitutional process, most recently by Moutier's 2021 vote to transfer cantons, which is the system working rather than failing.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by elections, and in Portugal by MORE of them than the calendar shows since premature dissolution is the ordinary path. The non-routine part -- the part the class is actually interesting for -- is modelled and reported as pt.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.120/yr. Declaring the class answered here would put Portugal's election frequency into a column other packs fill with leader instability, which is exactly the comparison E2 §3.2 warns against.

Portuguese government formation resolves through the President's appointment power under Art. 187(1) plus the Assembly's power to reject the Programme, and its failure mode is a dissolution and an election -- not an unresolved contest. The 2015 case is the sharpest test and it went the orderly way: Passos Coelho was appointed, his Programme was rejected 53 days later, and Costa formed a government inside the same chamber with no interregnum.

Portugal is a unitary state with two autonomous regions (Azores, Madeira) whose statutes are constitutional and whose independence movements are not of modelled scale. Recorded separately in this pack's notes and NOT as a disintegration question: neither archipelago is drawn by any polygon in this model, so even an authored branch would paint nothing.

ANSWERED, in the same state form ru and cn use -- and the correspondence claim carries a caveat unique in the roster. The union is exact: ie.government's states other than the one in which the t=0 Taoiseach holds office. But in Ireland the class's answer is fixed by a CALENDAR rather than by a hazard: the Programme for Government fixes the departure at 16 November 2027, month 14, so this reads at or near 100% by construction.
