Irish government formation is slow but not contested: the Dail elects a Taoiseach by simple majority and Art. 28.11 keeps the outgoing ministers in office until it does, so the failure mode is a long caretaker period -- modelled here as a STATE with a 1-5 month dwell -- rather than an unresolved contest over who holds authority. The 2020 formation took about five months and at no point was it unclear who was governing.

THE BORDER POLL IS NOT THIS PACK'S QUESTION, and the reasoning is worth reading because the obvious authoring move is wrong. Under the model's own accounting, state-disintegration for ie asks whether IRELAND loses territory. It cannot. The question is whether territory inside uk's claim moves to Ireland -- and uk.state-disintegration is already a declared coverage row with absence 'unauthored'. Adding ie creates no new question; it creates a second polity that would answer the same question FROM THE ACCRETING SIDE, and the shipped vocabulary has no class for accretion. Authoring it here would need a flag on ie reading uk's territory, which is exactly what the vocabulary's own rejection of external-armed-conflict forbids ('a polity flag referencing dyad content makes the pack unloadable'). Typed notApplicableByKind rather than unauthored on the class's own words: it requires secession 'by extrajudicial means', and a Good Friday Agreement border poll is the paradigm of the opposite -- Northern Ireland Act 1998 Sch. 1 para 2 makes it a DUTY on the Secretary of State ('shall exercise the power... if at any time it appears likely to him'), a treaty-based statutory procedure with a named decision-maker. The consistency objection is recorded rather than dodged: uk's row stays 'unauthored', so the model now holds two different types for one event, and the honest reading is that uk's row is itself mis-typed under the class's wording. Not re-typed here, because that is a decision about existing content and should be made deliberately rather than as a side effect. SCHEMA ITEM LEFT BEHIND (v1.1): the vocabulary can express 'this polity loses territory' and has no counterpart for 'this polity gains it'. Northern Ireland is the first instance in this model.

The class's fixed state-form union is dominated by elections, and in Denmark by far more of them than the calendar shows -- 28 of 29 post-war intervals fell short of the four-year term. The non-routine part is modelled and reported as dk.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.098/yr. Declaring the class answered here would put Denmark's election frequency into a column other packs fill with leader instability, which is the comparison E2 §3.2 warns against and which this block's pt.json makes for the same reason.

Danish government formation resolves through the monarch's rounds of consultation and a Folketing that can censure but need not name a successor, and its failure mode is an election rather than an unresolved contest. The three rounds of talks after the 24 March 2026 election took ten weeks and at no point was it unclear who was governing -- Art. 15's censure mechanism has never produced an interregnum.

GREENLAND, AND THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL ABSENCE IN THE ROSTER. Greenland has a formal statutory route to independence -- the only such route among this model's territorial questions -- and it is NOT authored, for a measured reason rather than a shrug. Act no. 473 of 12 June 2009, Chapter 8, is a single section, and §21 specifies FOUR consents in sequence: a decision by the people of Greenland; negotiations that Denmark is obliged to open but not to conclude; an agreement requiring the consent of Inatsisartut AND endorsement by a second Greenlandic referendum ON THE AGREEMENT; and the consent of the Folketing. The popular vote most commentary describes is the LAST gate, not the first. Gates 1 and 2 have evidence and are authorable: two independence polls (Verian January 2025 -- 56% yes in principle, 45% opposed if living standards fall; a January 2026 poll -- 25% yes to independence NOW, 62% no, with 24% support if living standards fall), a legal review of the §21 activation process commissioned September 2024 and due to report in late 2026, and party positions with seat counts. GATES 3 AND 4 HAVE NONE: the Act contains no clock anywhere, so a negotiation that never concludes is fully compliant with §21; and the single most relevant observation for gate 4 went the other way -- the Faroes voted yes in 1946, declared independence, and were annulled by the Danish Crown under the same Realm and the same §19 constraint on reducing its territory. The reference class cannot be priced either: 2 of 10 post-war referendums succeeded, but BOTH successes (Montenegro 2006, South Sudan 2011) had a pre-agreed BINDING referendum on a clock, which is the opposite of §21's architecture. Conditioned on 'binding referendum with a clock' the class is 2 of 2; conditioned on 'negotiation-gated' it is 0 of 8, and Greenland is unambiguously in the second -- so on B3 §2's typing every success is an ADJACENT-QUESTION alternative, and a class whose alternatives are all adjacent has recorded no choice. Typed 'unauthored' rather than notApplicableByKind because the class genuinely applies and this is a gap in the pack, which is the honest and most useful absence: it names work that could be done once the legal review reports. The three live Polymarket markets (Trump acquires Greenland before 2027 at 3.65%, US acquires part of Greenland in 2026 at 6.50%, US invades Greenland in 2026 at 3.05%) are NOT bound as anchors: all three resolve 31 December 2026, month 4 of 120, the in-pk.strike-2026 resolution-mismatch class C3 pre-recorded.

ANSWERED, in the state form the class fixes, and the union is exact rather than approximate for once: the model starts in no-government, which is precisely the state in which the t=0 incumbent still holds office under Art. 110(4). The caveat is priced rather than hand-waved -- Bolojan could be invested as the next Prime Minister, which the market puts at 5.25%, and this flag would count that path as an exit. The quantity that supports a cross-pack comparison of Romanian leader instability is ro.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.331/yr, not this flag.

UNAUTHORED, and this row carries the block's largest deliberate omission. Romania's 2024-25 sequence -- CCR Ruling 32/2024 annulling an ENTIRE presidential process unanimously on 6 December 2024 under Art. 146(f) with no appeal; the Central Electoral Bureau barring the leading candidate 10-4 on 9 March 2025; the CCR upholding the bar 9-0; President Iohannis resigning on 10 February 2025 in front of a third suspension vote -- is authored as REALIZED INITIAL CONDITIONS on ro.constitutional_crisis, and NO ANNULMENT HAZARD IS AUTHORED. THE REFERENCE-CLASS ARGUMENT IS WHY. The class 'a national election annulled by a constitutional court in a European democracy' has TWO members in a decade and they disagree in the decisive variable: Austria 2016 annulled a RUNOFF on counting irregularities, with the court explicitly finding NO evidence of intentional fraud, and barred nobody; Romania 2024 annulled the ENTIRE process over a foreign information operation and then barred the beneficiary. On B3 §2's typing Austria is an ADJACENT-QUESTION member, and a class whose alternatives are all adjacent has recorded no choice and does not compose. EXPLICITLY REJECTED: taking one annulment in ten Romanian elections and calling it 10%, which would put a double-digit probability on an event whose only European analogue turned on ballot-box seals. SCHEMA ITEM LEFT BEHIND (v1.1): the shipped vocabulary has no class for 'a national election is voided', so this declaration sits on contested-succession because that is where a reader would look, not because the fit is good. That is the ie.json accretion finding in a second form -- the vocabulary has three classes and the roster keeps meeting questions outside them.

Romania is a unitary state (Art. 1: 'a sovereign, independent, unitary and indivisible National State') with no autonomous region, no secessionist movement of modelled scale, and a constitutional prohibition (Art. 152) on any revision suppressing the unitary form. The Hungarian minority's UDMR has been inside governing coalitions for most of the post-communist period rather than outside the state. NOT MODELLED and recorded here rather than in the notes because it is the nearest thing to an argument on the other side: AUR's founding programme is Romanian-Moldovan unification and Simion has been barred from entering Moldova. That is an ACCRETION question, not a disintegration one, and the vocabulary has no class for it -- the same gap ie.json recorded for Northern Ireland. Moldova is not in the roster and not on the map.

ANSWERED, in the state form the class fixes. THE CAVEAT IS LARGER HERE THAN IN MOST PACKS and is stated rather than buried: a configuration machine cannot separate 'Radev left' from 'Progressive Bulgaria lost its majority', and the two come apart in both directions -- PB could return to a single-party majority under a different leader, or Radev could lead a coalition. Both paths are real. The comparable cross-pack quantity is bg.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.274/yr, and the informative state-level quantity is bg.caretaker_government's occupancy against a measured 45.6%.

Bulgarian government formation FAILS RATHER THAN CONTESTS, and the constitution makes that a deadline rather than a struggle. Art. 99 gives three mandates of seven days each -- largest group, second-largest, one of the minor groups -- and then the President SHALL appoint a caretaker government and dissolve. There is no interval in which it is unclear who governs: the outgoing Council of Ministers continues under Art. 111 until a new one is elected, and the caretaker is appointed by a named actor from a closed statutory list. Bulgaria ran that sequence to its terminal state SIX TIMES between 2021 and 2026 and on no occasion was the identity of the government in doubt. Typed notApplicableByKind rather than unauthored for that reason: the class asks about an unresolved contest over who rules, and this constitution is built so that question always has an answer within twenty-one days.

Bulgaria is a unitary state with no autonomous region and no territorial claim on it. NOT MODELLED and recorded here because it is the nearest thing to a counter-argument: the DPS fractured in 2025 into DPS-New Beginning under Delyan Peevski, who is under US and UK Magnitsky sanctions, and APS -- and the Movement's historic base is the Turkish-speaking minority. That is a party split, not a territorial question, and this brief did not research it; the pack should not be read as assuming the DPS label means what it meant in 2021.

ANSWERED, in the state form the class fixes, AND THE CORRESPONDENCE CAVEAT IS THE PACK'S CENTRAL FINDING rather than a footnote. The union includes the Article 37 caretaker state, so this column reports Greece on the WIDE reading of what 'ceased to hold office' means -- the reading in which Mitsotakis left office on 25 May 2023 and returned on 26 June, having WON the 21 May election with 40.79% and been unable to form a government under simple PR. gr.pm-exit adopts the STRICT reading at 0.0576/yr and declares the wide one at 0.1151/yr as a same-question alternative. Both are in this pack, in different slots, and a reader must not average them.

Greek government formation FAILS ON A CLOCK, and the clock makes an unresolved contest structurally impossible. Article 37 gives three exploratory mandates of THREE DAYS EACH to the largest, second and third parties, then an all-party attempt, then a senior judge -- so the maximum interval in which the identity of the next government is open is measured in days, and the identity of the government ADMINISTERING is never open at all. Greece ran that sequence to its terminal state in May 2023 and in May 2012 and on neither occasion was there a contest over who ruled; there was a procedure that concluded. Typed notApplicableByKind rather than unauthored for that reason: the class asks about an open intra-elite struggle, and this constitution answers the question by appointing a judge.

GREECE'S TERRITORIAL QUESTION IS THE AEGEAN AND THIS PACK CANNOT ASK IT. Typed notApplicableByKind and NOT unauthored, and the distinction is the whole point: unauthored means work that could be done in this pack and was not; this work CANNOT be done in this pack. Airspace violations, EEZ delimitation, mock dogfights and the 1995 casus belli resolution are joint products of two states' behaviour, and a factor on gr whose value is set mostly by Turkish decisions is B1 §4's correspondence failure -- which is also what the vocabulary's own rejection of external-armed-conflict says operationally ('a polity flag referencing dyad content makes the pack unloadable'). It requires either a tr polity or a gr-tr dyad, and Programme E forbids new couplings for a fifth block. WHAT THE PACK CARRIES INSTEAD, all with Greek predicates: gr.accommodation_posture, gr.safe-veto-lifted and gr.maritime-zone-extension. AND A READER MUST KNOW THIS: TURKIYE DRAWS ON THE MAP IN NATO'S FILL, because TUR is in nato.territories. Looking at the Aegean you will see Greece in its own colour and Turkey in the alliance's, and you will reasonably infer that this model holds a view about the relationship. IT DOES NOT. NO ANCHOR IS BOUND, AND THE EVIDENCE FOR WHY IS WORTH READING: Polymarket's greece-x-turkey-military-engagement event carries $1.27m of volume and prices actual exchange of fire at 5.1% for December 2026, while the observed tempo is at an all-time high -- 433 airspace violations in 2026 against 225 in all of 2025 -- because the market's rules EXPLICITLY EXCLUDE airspace violations, warning shots and intercepted munitions. The two measure different variables. An anchor would need a model quantity whose union matches that rule, and gr has none; binding one anyway is C4.1 §6.4e's unevaluable row.

ANSWERED, in the state form the class fixes, and the under-read is larger here than in any other E5 pack because the incumbent has outlasted two elections and three cabinets. A configuration machine cannot separate 'Plenkovic left' from 'HDZ left office', and after 9.87 years those are visibly different questions. The rate-bearing quantity is hr.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.0775/yr.

Croatian government formation has never taken more than about a month after a scheduled election, and the constitution supplies a deadline rather than a contest: Article 113 gives the chamber THIRTY DAYS to elect a replacement Prime Minister after a successful no-confidence vote, failing which 'the President of the Republic shall IMMEDIATELY dissolve Parliament and simultaneously call a parliamentary election'. The one occasion the chamber removed a Prime Minister -- Oreskovic, 125-15 on 16 June 2016 -- it self-dissolved four days later rather than contest a succession. Typed notApplicableByKind rather than unauthored: the class asks about an open intra-elite struggle over who rules, and this constitution converts that question into a dissolution on a one-month timer.

Croatia is a unitary state with no autonomous region and no secessionist movement of modelled scale; the Serb minority's SDSS has been inside or supporting governing majorities for most of the post-2000 period. NOT MODELLED and recorded here rather than in the notes because the honest counter-argument is historical rather than current: the territorial question that defined Croatia's first decade was settled by 1998, and nothing in the current politics reopens it.

ANSWERED, in the state form the class fixes, WITH THE ROSTER'S LARGEST STRUCTURAL UNDER-READ and it is declared rather than discovered. A two-state machine cannot represent a change of Prime Minister within a bloc, and one of the five members of si.pm-exit's own class -- Drnovsek resigning in December 2002 to become President, with Rop succeeding from the same party -- was exactly that. The two-state machine is chosen because Article 116 makes an interregnum impossible and because Slovenian government changes ARE bloc changes four times in five; the cost is that this column reads bloc alternation rather than leader turnover. si.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.1421/yr is the comparable quantity.

THE CONSTITUTION MAKES A CONTESTED SUCCESSION UNEXPRESSIBLE, and this is the cleanest instance of the typing in the roster. Article 116: 'The National Assembly may pass a vote of no confidence in the Government ONLY BY ELECTING A NEW PRESIDENT OF THE GOVERNMENT ... The incumbent President of the Government is thereby dismissed, but together with his ministers he must continue to perform his regular duties until the swearing in of a new Government.' A Slovenian government cannot be removed until its successor has been named and elected by 46 votes, and it keeps governing until that successor is sworn in -- so there is no interval in which who rules is open. Where the chamber CANNOT agree, Articles 111 and 117 convert the deadlock into a dissolution on a fourteen- or thirty-day timer rather than into a contest. Typed notApplicableByKind rather than unauthored: the class asks about an open intra-elite struggle over who rules, and this constitution is built so that the question never arises.

Slovenia is a unitary state of two million people with no autonomous region, no secessionist movement, and two constitutionally guaranteed national-minority seats (Italian and Hungarian) whose holders have supported governments of both blocs -- including this one. NOT MODELLED and nothing on the other side was found to record.
ANSWERED, in the state form the class fixes.

This pack's machine tracks the STEADY-STATE government configuration, not the formation process itself, so the investiture-cascade mechanism (Art. 68's repeated-nomination sequence) is unmodelled. Cyprus's two-round presidential system is specifically designed to eliminate majority-legitimacy ambiguity: an outright first-round majority wins outright, and otherwise the top two go to a runoff a week later, so the office is never settled on a plurality a rival could contest. Zero disputed presidential results found across twelve elections since 1968.

THE AEGEAN ARGUMENT, applied to the island's own division. The north's status is a joint product of the Republic, Turkey, the unrecognized 'TRNC' and the guarantor powers (Greece, Turkey, the UK) -- a cy-only pack cannot ask whether reunification or further fragmentation occurs any more than gr.json's pack can ask the equivalent Aegean question, and for the identical reason: it would require a cy-tur or trilateral dyad, and Programme E forbids new couplings this block. What the pack carries instead is Cyprus's own side: reunification_momentum, and the reunification-conference-convened and safe-eda-veto-lifted events, both Greek/Cypriot-authored and gated on that factor alone.

ANSWERED, in the state form the class fixes. Unlike Austria, Malta's state-form union is NOT dominated by routine churn (average PM tenure ~6.5-6.9 years, only two elections per decade), so it answers the class directly rather than needing a separate non-routine flag the way at.mid_term_leader_exit does -- mid_term_pm_change is carried alongside as additional detail, not as a replacement.

Malta's two corrective-seat mechanisms (Article 52 proportionality, Article 52A gender) are specifically engineered to guarantee the top vote-getter a working single-party majority. No coalition-formation crisis is structurally possible: every government since 1966 has been single-party, and this pack's own machine has no coalition or minority state to contest.
No secessionist movement of modelled scale and no contested territorial claim, on at.json's identical reasoning -- the simplest case in the roster.

The uk/tw/us declarations' argument, applied to Canada's own calendar: the class's fixed operationalisation is the union of machine states in which the t=0 incumbent no longer holds office, and over a 120-month horizon containing two scheduled general elections (2029-10, 2033-10) that union approaches certainty through ROUTINE alternation. The genuinely non-routine part -- a Prime Minister leaving without a general election -- IS modelled and IS reported, as ca.mid_term_leader_exit, and is deliberately not offered as an answer to this class because it is a different question with a different denominator.

Succession to the premiership is decided by a governing party's own leadership rules and has never left Canada without a settled chief executive -- Carney's own succession is the concrete case: Trudeau announced his resignation 2025-01-06, the Liberal leadership race concluded and Carney was sworn in 2025-03-14, a bounded nine weeks with an uninterrupted transfer of office throughout. No amount of authoring on THIS machine would produce the class's object (an unresolved dispute over who holds power), which is why the reason is notApplicableByKind rather than notModelled -- uk.json's identical argument, with Canada's own evidence now over a year settled rather than five weeks.

Quebec sovereignty is a real branch in the world -- two referenda (1980, 1995, the latter 50.58/49.42) and an ongoing, currently low-salience constitutional argument -- and is NOT authored here. Recorded exactly as uk's Scotland gap is: this is a gap in the pack, not a fact about the world, and it is NOT notApplicableByKind -- a second machine over Confederation's territorial integrity is authorable and simply is not authored in a tier-2 close-out block. events.name: Government falls to a censure motion
events.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.3/§4.2. Gated on the hung-assembly state, where alone it has a referent: censure motions succeed against a government with no majority and fail against one with a majority (a single successful censure in the Fifth Republic before 2024, in 1962). The 2024-25 sequence is the live reference: censure was attempted repeatedly, succeeded against Barnier, and failed narrowly against Lecornu twice. Baseline 0.09/yr DE-RATED against the durability modifier: at 22, exp(-0.8 x -28/50) = 1.564, giving an effective 0.141/yr in the hung state — roughly one successful censure per seven years of hung-Assembly government, against a realised 2024-25 rate that was higher still. Deliberately conservative: the realised rate is drawn from the worst 18 months in the Republic's history and treating it as stationary would be the C4.6 error. This event does NOT trigger a transition — a fallen government is replaced within the same configuration, which is what happened four times in 2024-25. CASCADE EXEMPT.

Attaching the usual modifier would import exactly the five-fold over-prediction this pack was built to avoid. CASCADE EXEMPT.

events.name: The government falls and a formation opens
events.provenance: E3-BENELUX-BRIEF §B6, and the event that carries Belgium's real instability. THE DUTCH TRAP APPLIES HERE TOO AND HARDER: in Belgium a government falling does NOT remove the prime minister -- the outgoing PM stays on in caretaker capacity, and in the four longest formations he stayed for most or all of it. Leterme remained Prime Minister through the ENTIRE 541-day record formation; Michel stayed on after submitting his cabinet's resignation in December 2018; Verhofstadt stayed 284 days after losing an election. So the world-record formation produced ZERO prime-ministerial departures while it ran. This event is therefore separate from be.pm-exit and carries a much higher rate, exactly as nl.cabinet-collapse is separate from nl.pm-exit. UNIT CHECK (the C4.4 defect): at the t=0 durability of 42 the modifier is exp(-0.7 x -8/50) = 1.119, so the declared baseline is rated DOWN to 0.150 to draw ~0.168/yr. Verified against simcli hazard-rates. CASCADE EXEMPT: a coalition falling over a budget is a domestic durability shock, not an escalation trigger.

events.name: The Nationalrat dissolves itself early
events.provenance: E3-NEUTRALS-BRIEF §A6, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT EVENT IN THIS PACK. Of the Nationalrat's 27 legislative periods only FIVE ran their full length; nineteen ended by premature self-dissolution via simple federal law -- the ORDINARY mechanism, not an emergency one, and parliament's own account notes government crisis was often not even the reason. Restricted to the Second Republic: 5 of 23 completed periods ran full term (21.7%). The empirical cadence is 24 elections between 1945 and 2024, a mean interval of 3.43 years against a nominal four (pre-2008) then five (post-2008). A pack that scheduled only 2029 and 2034 would encode a ~22%-likely path and put two elections in a 120-month window where the history puts about three. Governed by reference class at.early-dissolution. UNIT CHECK (the C4.4 defect): at the t=0 durability of 44 the modifier is exp(-0.6 x -6/50) = 1.074, so the declared baseline is rated DOWN to 0.130 to draw ~0.140/yr. Verified against simcli hazard-rates. CASCADE EXEMPT.

events.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §C15, governed by reference class ro.president-exit. ONE effective departure in 36.201 years -- Klaus Iohannis, who resigned on 10 February 2025 rather than face a third parliamentary suspension vote scheduled for 11 February, leaving office on the 12th -- so 0.0276/yr. NO MODIFIER, deliberately: the mechanism is an Art. 95 joint-session suspension by 233 of 465 followed by a removal referendum within 30 days, and nothing this pack models measures the parliament's appetite for one. NO TRANSITION: this pack has no president machine. THE SYMMETRY WITH bg.president-exit IS A COINCIDENCE AND IS NAMED AS ONE. Bulgaria's identical class reads 0.0277/yr on one departure in 36.086 years, and the two departures happened within nineteen months of each other for OPPOSITE reasons -- Iohannis was pushed out under nationalist pressure after an annulled election he helped precipitate by declassifying the intelligence; Radev left voluntarily at the height of his popularity to take over the government. events.name: The President dissolves Parliament under Article 89
events.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A2.1, §A2.2. THE GATE, AND DELIBERATELY NOT A FLAT HAZARD. Art. 89 permits dissolution only if no government has been invested within 60 days of the first request AND after at least two rejected investitures, at most once a year, and never in the last six months of the President's term. Modelled as a hazard that can only fire from no-government, which is the constitutional precondition rendered as the only thing the schema can express. THIS IS THE SOFTEST NUMBER IN THE PACK AND IT IS MARKED AS SUCH, on E3's ch.cooperation-deepens precedent. The empirical rate is EXACTLY ZERO: Art. 89 has never been used in 36 years, and conditional on being in a material formation failure it is zero events in roughly 0.6 years of exposure -- an interval too short to price. It is ANALYST-ASSESSED rather than reference-classed, and it is authored at a positive number for three stated reasons: the gate is live for the first time in 36 years (Vestea designated 14 June, 60 days expired 13 August), its second condition is ONE REJECTION SHORT (Tomac withdrew before presenting a cabinet, so only Vestea's 22 June rejection counts), and AUR is publicly seeking early elections while President Dan has publicly ruled them out. At roughly a twentieth of the horizon spent in no-government this draws well under one dissolution per century, which is the pack saying 'essentially never, but no longer structurally impossible'. NOT MODELLED, and recorded: the once-a-year cap, and the two dissolution-barred windows at months 39-45 and about 99-105 (Art. 89(3), Dan's term ending 26 May 2030) -- the schema cannot gate a hazard on a calendar, which is the same limitation pt.json records. A SOURCE DISAGREEMENT RESOLVED AND RECORDED: Romania Insider states the 60-day timer 'began from the vote for the Vestea government' (22 June, expiring 21 August); Art. 89 says 'within 60 days of the first request' and the designation reading is taken. The disagreement is a week and changes nothing today. MARKET RECORDED AND EXPLICITLY NOT USED: Polymarket's 'romanian-parliament-dissolved-by' December leg quotes 23.5% on FIVE DOLLARS of volume -- a market-maker's book, not a price -- while its August leg reads 0.4% on $350 and correctly says it has not happened. CASCADE EXEMPT.

impulses.note: Small and one-directional, because the office's only model-relevant power is the Art. 99 caretaker appointment and a President aligned with the governing majority lowers formation risk. The pack does NOT encode who wins.

events.name: Presidential election (scheduled)
events.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B8.5, §B12. THE EARLIEST SCHEDULED NATIONAL ELECTION ANY ROSTER PACK HAS EVER CARRIED: 25 October 2026, MONTH 1, with a runoff seven days later if needed. It beats se.json's 13 September 2026 by six weeks and matches ch.json's 27 September 2026 referendum for immediacy. Art. 93(5) times it from the incumbent TERM's January 2027 expiry rather than from Radev's resignation -- Iotova inherited the remainder of the term under Art. 97(4), not a new one -- and the next falls around October 2031 (month ~61). CALENDAR-AUTHORED (D6.1). NO TRANSITION: the presidency does not resolve this machine. THE IMPULSE IS DELIBERATELY SMALL AND DELIBERATELY NOT A FORECAST. Polymarket's bulgaria-presidential-election market is genuinely liquid -- $338k volume, $547k liquidity -- and prices the incumbent Iliana Iotova at 75.5% on $122k against Andrey Gyurov, the former caretaker Prime Minister, at 21%. NO ANCHOR IS BOUND (E5.9): a row resolving at month 1 of 120 constrains essentially nothing about this ensemble, and binding it would be theatre dressed as calibration. It is recorded instead as the best scoreable candidate the forecast ledger has ever had, shorter-horizon than us.divided-government-2026 at month 4, and left for a block doing ledger work. TWO TRAPS RECORDED FOR WHOEVER BINDS IT. Art. 93(3) requires more than half the valid ballots AND turnout above half the electorate, so a candidate can win an absolute majority in round one and still face a runoff -- a model quantity named 'wins the first round' would not answer the market, whose rules include any second round. And Kalshi's KXBULGARIAPRES tickers are named '-26NOV15-' with a 2027-11-15 close, encoding an election date THREE WEEKS AFTER the confirmed 25 October: W4.5's 'a market slug is not a horizon' in a new form, and its eleven candidate markets have no price, no volume and no open interest. CASCADE EXEMPT.

events.name: Parliament is dissolved early
events.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A2, governed by reference class gr.early-dissolution. THE SMALLEST EARLY-DISSOLUTION HAZARD IN THE E SERIES, IN THE COUNTRY WITH THE ROSTER'S HIGHEST RAW ELECTION COUNT, and it is a legislative fact rather than a behavioural one -- see the class. A SOURCE CORRECTION THE PACK MUST NOT INHERIT UNCORRECTED, and it is the W4.5 class exactly: Wikisource states that Article 41 'was repealed by the 1986 Amendment' and prints no current text. That is WRONG. The 1986 revision removed the President's DISCRETIONARY dissolution power -- the pre-1986 Article 41(1) let him dissolve at will -- and left the two conditional limbs, which Constitute Project prints in full. Had the repeal been believed, this channel would have been unauthorable. NOT AUTHORED, AND IT IS THE PACK'S SECOND-LARGEST DELIBERATE OMISSION: the February 2030 presidential election (month 41). Under the pre-2019 Article 32, failure to elect a President by three-fifths at the third ballot REQUIRED dissolution within ten days, and that is exactly what produced the January 2015 election and Tsipras's first government. The constitutional revision of 25 November 2019 decoupled them: five ballots at 200, 200, 180, 151 and then a relative majority, with NO dissolution at any stage. February 2025 is the demonstration -- Tasoulas took 160 against 200 required on 25 January, 160 against 200 on 31 January, 156 against 180 on 6 February, and was elected on the fourth ballot with 160 against 151 on 12 February. Under the rules in force ten years earlier that sequence would have dissolved the Parliament. The event is NOT authored because its only model-relevant consequence was legislated away, and authoring one to represent a repealed mechanism would be worse than recording it here. UNIT CHECK (the C4.4 defect): at the durability attractor of 42 the modifier is exp(-0.6 x -8/50) = 1.1008 and the realised multiplier is 1.05, so the declared baseline is rated DOWN to 0.0572 to draw 0.0600/yr. Verified against simcli hazard-rates. AND A CONSTITUTIONAL REVISION IS PROPOSED AND CANNOT PLAUSIBLY BE ENACTED INSIDE THIS HORIZON, which was checked before authoring rather than assumed. The first act completed on 28 July 2026 and carries Articles 16 (non-state universities), 24 (environment), 30 (A SINGLE SIX-YEAR PRESIDENTIAL TERM), 44(2) (referendums) and 86 (ministerial liability), on votes of 158-161. THE VOTE TOTALS DECIDE THE REST: Article 110 requires three-fifths — 180 of 300 — in the PROPOSING parliament for the next parliament to revise by absolute majority, and an absolute majority in the first phase forces three-fifths in the second. Greece achieved 158-161, so every proposed change now needs 180 votes in the parliament elected in 2027, where New Democracy polls to roughly 118 seats with the bonus. ARTICLES 32, 37, 41 AND 53 — the four this pack is built on — ARE NOT AMONG THE CARRIED ARTICLES. So gr authors the five-year presidential term and the February 2030 election unchanged, and Article 30's six-year term is recorded as live-but-blocked. CASCADE EXEMPT.

events.name: Greece lifts its veto on Turkish access to EU defence instruments
events.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A7.4, and E-PLAN §E5.12: the single most authorable thing about the Greek-Turkish relationship that does not require a Turkey pack, BECAUSE A VETO IS AN ACT OF THE VETOING STATE. Turkey applied to the EUR 150bn SAFE facility and was excluded alongside the UK and South Korea, on veto threats from Greece and Cyprus; Greece's stated condition for lifting is that Turkey revoke the 1995 casus belli resolution, and Cyprus's is that a state threatening a member state cannot access EU defence funding. ONESHOT: a veto once lifted is consumed. UNIT CHECK (the C4.4 defect), AND THIS EVENT'S MODIFIER IS THE LARGEST DE-RATING IN THE BLOCK: the modifier is exp(+0.9 x (x-50)/50) on a posture that starts at 22, giving exp(0.9 x -28/50) = 0.604, so the declared baseline is rated UP to 0.1656 to draw 0.100/yr. A POSITIVE weight on a factor BELOW the neutral 50 suppresses rather than inflates, which is the mirror of E1 §3.2's error and the reason this pack states the sign in every modifier note. Verified against simcli hazard-rates. THIS RATE IS ANALYST-ASSESSED, NOT REFERENCE-CLASSED, AND IS MARKED AS THE SOFTEST NUMBER IN THE PACK on E3's ch.cooperation-deepens precedent: there is no historical series of 'Greece traded an alliance good for a Turkish concession' events to count, the condition attached is a specific act of the Turkish parliament that has stood for thirty-one years, and the diplomatic track (an annual High-Level Cooperation Council, next round due) is warming while the military tempo is at an all-time high. A future block with a better instrument should replace it. CASCADE EXEMPT: a de-escalatory diplomatic act must not arm a hazard multiplier.

THE GREEK ESCALATION-RESPONSE CHANNEL, and every predicate in it is Greek: Greece declared an EEZ boundary with Italy (June 2020), one with Egypt (August 2020), and extended its Ionian territorial waters from 6 to 12 nautical miles by Law 4767/2021 (January 2021) -- three acts in roughly six years. THE RATE IS DE-RATED FROM THAT BURST DELIBERATELY, to 0.12/yr rather than ~0.5/yr, because the easy delimitations are DONE: Italy and Egypt were willing counterparties, and what remains -- the Aegean, and any extension of Aegean territorial waters -- is precisely what the 1995 Turkish parliamentary resolution names as a casus belli. The remaining acts are of a different and much rarer kind than the completed ones, and the pack says so rather than projecting the burst. Also live and not separately authored: the marine-parks and 'Blue Homeland' legislative track. ANALYST-ASSESSED IN ITS DE-RATING, class-based in its numerator. events.name: The Sabor dissolves itself early
events.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B10, governed by reference class hr.early-dissolution. THE PACK'S ONE DELIBERATE OVER-COUNT, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. Croatia's empirical cadence is 0.2838/yr and this pack already schedules three elections in 120 months, which is 0.30/yr -- so the calendar ALONE already over-supplies, and adding any hazard makes it worse. The alternative was authoring nothing, and that would make the single premature Croatian parliament in 34 years UNREPRESENTABLE: a pack in which early dissolution has probability zero asserts something stronger than the evidence, in a country that did it in 2016. So the hazard is authored at the RAW premature rate -- one termination in 31.71 years, 0.0315/yr -- and the consequence is recorded: the pack's implied cadence is about 0.33/yr against an observed 0.284, an over-count of roughly 0.046/yr or one extra election every twenty-two years. Compare pt.json, which subtracts its scheduled legs from a cadence that exceeds them; Croatia's does not exceed them, so there is nothing to subtract and the excess form of the calculation would give a NEGATIVE rate. THE FIRST ROSTER PACK WHERE THAT IS TRUE. UNIT CHECK (the C4.4 defect): at the durability attractor of 52 the modifier is exp(-0.6 x 2/50) = 0.9763 and the realised multiplier is 0.93, so the declared baseline is rated UP to 0.0338 to draw 0.0315/yr -- NOTE THE DIRECTION, which is the opposite of every other pack in the E series and is the E1 §3.2 sign error's mirror image: hr is the only E5 pack whose durability attractor sits ABOVE the neutral 50, so its modifiers are below 1 and its declared baselines must be rated UP. Verified against simcli hazard-rates. CASCADE EXEMPT.

FOLLOWING be.json, NOT at.json OR pt.json, AND THE REASON INVERTS E4's PORTUGAL ARGUMENT RATHER THAN CONTRADICTING IT: Portugal's 1982 boundary explained ONE of four early departures and was therefore a coincidence of dates with a story attached; CROATIA'S 2000 BOUNDARY EXPLAINS TWO OF TWO. The 2000/2001 amendments abolished Croatian semi-presidentialism -- the President could no longer appoint and dismiss the Prime Minister or ministers -- and both pre-2000 departures ARE exactly that mechanism (Manolic and Sarinic were Tudman's appointees, removed at his discretion, with no parliamentary act involved), while both post-2000 ones are parliamentary mechanisms that still exist. When the stated cause accounts for the whole effect, the split is a regime distinction. NO TRANSITION: see the government-falls transition. UNIT CHECK (the C4.4 defect): at the durability attractor of 52 the modifier is exp(-0.5 x 2/50) = 0.9802 and the realised multiplier is 0.94, so the declared baseline is rated UP to 0.0823 to draw 0.0775/yr -- rated UP, not down, for the reason hr.self-dissolution's provenance gives. events.name: The President's deployment veto expires (scheduled)
events.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B8, and E-PLAN §E5.13. THE ROSTER'S SECOND SCHEDULED FACTOR CHANGE AND ITS FIRST SCHEDULED REMOVAL OF A CONSTRAINT -- ie.taoiseach-rotation is the first scheduled head-of-government departure, and this is its structural counterpart. President Milanovic was re-elected on 12 January 2025 with 74.7% against 25.3%, a record margin; he was first inaugurated on 19 February 2020; the term is five years and HE IS TERM-LIMITED. So the veto that keeps Croatia out of NSATU has an expiry date inside this horizon, and a hazard would be the wrong shape for it: this is a date, not a risk. CALENDAR-AUTHORED (D6.1), ONESHOT because a term ends once. THE DATE IS APPROXIMATE AND SAYS SO: February 2030 is reconstructed from the 2020 inauguration plus the five-year term rather than fetched, so treat the month as +/- one. WHAT THIS EVENT DOES NOT ASSERT: that the successor will be an Atlanticist. It asserts that THIS President's particular veto ends, and the impulse decays at 0.004/month back toward an unchanged attractor of 48 -- roughly +9 of the +12 surviving to the horizon's end. The schema cannot re-point an attractor, so a durable structural change has to be authored as a shock plus a slow reversion; see hr.atlanticism's provenance for the v1.1 item. events.name: Cyprus lifts its veto on Turkish access to EU defence instruments
events.provenance: POLITICO, December 2025: Christodoulides said Cyprus (with Greece) currently blocks Turkey's access to the EU's EUR150bn SAFE defence-procurement fund and the European Defence Agency, and proposed a step-by-step deal -- Turkey lets Cyprus into NATO's Partnership for Peace, Cyprus/EU ease Turkey's SAFE/EDA access, talks resume. THE DIRECT STRUCTURAL COUNTERPART TO gr.safe-veto-lifted OVER THE IDENTICAL FACILITY -- Cyprus is a second, independent veto-holder, not a shared one, so this event is priced independently rather than coupled (Programme E forbids new couplings this block); the double-counting risk this creates for any reader summing both packs' effects is named here rather than hidden. ONESHOT: a veto once lifted is consumed. UNIT CHECK (C4.4): weight +0.6 on reunification_momentum starting at 38 gives exp(0.6*(38-50)/50)=0.8659, so the declared baseline is rated UP to draw 0.06/yr. Lower than gr's drawn 0.100/yr: this proposal is one month old at t=0 against Greece's standing, years-argued condition, and has no comparable diplomatic track record to draw on. Verify against simcli hazard-rates. THIS RATE IS ANALYST-ASSESSED, THE SOFTEST NUMBER IN THE PACK, on E3's ch.cooperation-deepens precedent.

impulses.note: A convened full-format conference is itself the largest single reunification-track development this pack can represent short of a settlement, which the pack deliberately does not attempt to model (see state-disintegration coverage).

events.name: A full-format 5+1 reunification conference convenes
events.provenance: UN News, 29 July 2026: Guterres announced he would convene a new 5+1 format meeting (both communities plus guarantor powers Greece, Turkey, the UK) 'after adequate preparations,' with no date fixed as of end-July 2026 -- only preparatory diplomacy exists as of t=0. UNIT CHECK: weight +0.5 at momentum=38 gives exp(0.5*(38-50)/50)=0.8869, so the declared baseline is rated UP to draw 0.10/yr -- a decade horizon giving genuine but not confident odds of a full conference (as opposed to more of the same six informal 5+1 exploratory meetings already held 2017-2026) actually convening. Verify against simcli hazard-rates.

impulses.note: Sized off the one dated instance: the 12 January 2026 resignation of Christodoulides's own office director, Charalambos Charalambous, after a video alleging the government would work to block EU sanctions against Russian oligarchs for cash -- Cypriot authorities called the video disinformation 'bearing all the hallmarks' of prior Russian influence campaigns, but it broke as a domestic scandal regardless of its origin.

events.name: A sanctions-adjacent corruption or influence-operation scandal breaks
events.provenance: Cyprus was a major hub for Russian offshore finance; post-2022 sanctions drove Russian bank deposits down 76% (2014-2022) and banks severed ties with ~60,000 mostly Russian/Ukrainian clients. RECURRING rather than one-shot: this is the kind of exposure that produces periodic scandals rather than a single settled event, and the January 2026 episode is one dated instance of an ongoing pattern rather than the whole of it. 0.28/yr is ANALYST-ASSESSED against that one instance and the scale of the underlying exposure, not reference-classed -- no comparable prior series exists to count. Flagged as the pack's other soft number alongside safe-eda-veto-lifted. CASCADE EXEMPT: a domestic corruption scandal is not an interstate escalation trigger.

events.name: Scheduled general election
events.provenance: CALENDAR-AUTHORED (D6.1). Malta's Parliament runs a constitutional maximum of 5 years; Robert Abela was sworn in for his fourth consecutive term 1 June 2026 (30 May 2026 election), so the next election is due by ~2031-05/06 at the latest, and the one after by ~2036-05/06 -- both inside the 120-month horizon. FOURTEEN elections since 1966, at least 4 confirmed early relative to the maximum (1992, 1996, 1998, 2026) -- so 2031-05 is a ceiling rather than a confident point estimate, and the model necessarily under-represents the chance of an EARLIER election, since no early-dissolution hazard is separately authored (see pm-exit's provenance for why that gap is deliberate). CASCADE EXEMPT: a scheduled election is not an escalation.

impulses.note: Sized off at.chancellor-exit's identical impulse: a mid-term handover costs the incoming PM some of the outgoing one's standing, whatever the cause.

modifiers.note: A government that is holding does not change Prime Minister.

events.name: Prime Minister leaves office mid-term, same party continues
events.provenance: docs/research/E6-MALTA-BRIEF-2026-08-25.md §4. Two mid-term, non-election, same-party PM handovers in 7 individuals / 8 stints since 1974: Mintoff resigned 1984 (succeeded within Labour by Karmenu Mifsud Bonnici), Muscat resigned 2020 (succeeded within Labour by Abela, Caruana Galizia fallout). ZERO of Malta's PM exits were floor no-confidence removals -- every exit is an election loss or a voluntary, INTRA-PARTY resignation, so this event deliberately does NOT trigger the general-election transition: the government state (labour-majority / nationalist-majority) is unchanged by a handover inside the governing party, exactly the distinction nl.json draws between a falling cabinet and a replaced PM. Crude rate: 2 events / 52 years = 0.0385/yr. UNIT CHECK (C4.4): weight -0.5 at the t=0 durability of 78 gives exp(-0.5*(78-50)/50)=0.7558, so the declared baseline is rated UP to 0.051 to draw ~0.0385/yr. Verify against simcli hazard-rates. CASCADE EXEMPT.

events.name: Malta ends its PESCO opt-out
events.provenance: docs/research/E6-MALTA-BRIEF-2026-08-25.md §3. Malta is the SOLE EU member of 27 outside PESCO, opted out at its 2017 launch citing constitutional-neutrality concerns, and reaffirmed 'no reason to change the status quo' in 2026 reporting -- against a rhetorical shift (PM Abela, early 2025: Malta should 'reconsider how it traditionally interprets' neutrality) and a near-doubled defence budget (~EUR42m 2014 to ~EUR100m projected 2026). NOT a constitutional-amendment event -- PESCO membership does not require touching Article 1(3), exactly as it does not for Austria or Ireland, both PESCO members while constitutionally neutral -- so this prices the POLICY move only. DELIBERATELY BOUNDED WELL BELOW ch.cooperation-deepens (declared 0.055/yr, drawing ~0.051/yr): Malta's posture starts at 30 against Switzerland's 44, and this pack's own EU-defence exclusion (SAFE) marks it further from the 'quasi-aligned neutral' end than any of the roster's other three modelled neutrals. UNIT CHECK: weight +0.5 at the t=0 posture of 30 gives exp(0.5*(30-50)/50)=0.8187, so the declared baseline is rated UP to 0.02 to draw ~0.0164/yr -- a ~15.3% cumulative chance across the horizon, deliberately conservative and the number in this pack most likely to get quoted elsewhere. Verify against simcli hazard-rates. CASCADE EXEMPT.

impulses.note: Sized above cy.corruption-scandal's -6 (a peripheral resignation): this is the marquee case itself, and either a guilty verdict (renewed state-responsibility scrutiny) or an acquittal (public outrage, renewed press-freedom criticism) plausibly spikes pressure -- the pack does not attempt to model the verdict's direction, only that reaching one is itself high-salience.

events.name: A verdict is reached in the Fenech assassination trial
events.provenance: docs/research/E6-MALTA-BRIEF-2026-08-25.md §5. Yorgen Fenech's jury trial for the alleged October 2017 assassination of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia began 1 July 2026 and was still underway as of 24 August 2026 (day 43+), with a verdict 'reportedly expected imminently' -- no fixed date found, so this is NOT calendar-authored despite being near-certain soon. UNGATED: no factor modifier, matching us.json's identical 3.0/yr convention for a fast, near-certain one-shot with no natural gating dial -- at 3.0/yr the monthly firing probability is 1-exp(-0.25)=22.1%, giving ~63% within 4 months and ~95% within a year of t=0, which matches 'expected imminently' without asserting a specific month. ONESHOT: a verdict, once reached, is consumed. CASCADE EXEMPT: a domestic verdict is not an interstate escalation.

events.name: Canadian general election
events.provenance: E7-CANADA-BRIEF §2: the Canada Elections Act's fixed-date provision sets a general election for the third Monday of October, four years after the previous polling day -- 2029-10-15 from 2025-04-28, regardless of the later floor-crossing majority consolidation, which changed the government's composition but not the Parliament's own election date. The following fixed date is 2033-10. CALENDAR-AUTHORED (D6.1) at both dates, matching the E6 fix (cz/sk/mt each needed a second scheduled date to avoid leaving half the 120-month horizon's ordinary elections unmodelled). RECORDED APPROXIMATION: the PM retains the power to advise an earlier dissolution, so the modelled dates are the fixed latest dates rather than modal ones, the same gap uk.json names for its own election event. CASCADE EXEMPT because a scheduled domestic election is not an escalation shock.

NEAR-TERM rally-round-the-flag assumption, argued rather than asserted: an active bilateral trade crisis with a clearly external adversary modestly firms up an incumbent's standing in the short run, so a strained relationship (low value) modestly REDUCES this hazard. The counter-argument -- that sustained economic pain from tariffs erodes a government over time rather than strengthening it -- is not modelled; this modifier is a same-direction snapshot effect, not a claim about the crisis's eventual multi-year political cost, which is a named limitation.

events.name: Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect
events.provenance: E7-CANADA-BRIEF §3: US-Canada trade talks collapsed 2026-08-22, three days before this brief; the US applied a 50% tariff on ~$20bn of Canadian exports (~5.5% of the total); Carney announced Canadian retaliation 'dollar for dollar' on US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, paper and electronics starting 2026-09-08 -- eight days into this model's own t=0 month, live news at authoring time rather than backstory. NOT an escalation-cascade trigger: a bilateral tariff dispute between two allied, NATO-member economies is categorically different from the interstate military/security crises the W0 cascade exists to represent, and every other roster pack's domestic-and-bilateral-economic events (uk.general-election, ie's Taoiseach rotation) are exempt on the same reasoning. events.name: First fatal Russia-NATO incident
events.provenance: RU-NATO-FLASHPOINTS §6.3 stage 3: P(first fatal Russia-NATO incident) 8-20%/yr — deaths on either side from a direct interaction (manned-aircraft shoot-down, sabotage fatalities, naval collision), which has not occurred in four years of incidents. EFFECTIVE 0.10/yr AT t=0, NOT the 0.14 midpoint, because one of the brief's three fatal routes is already an event in this pack: candidate event 4, 'NATO shoots down a manned Russian military aircraft, 2-6%/yr', is inside `nonmunition-engagement` by that event's own citation. Rating this one at the full band would count that route twice, and double-counting raises war probability, so it is the direction that must not be left to a footnote. Residual = stage 3 minus event 4 = 6-14%/yr for the routes nothing else carries (sabotage fatalities, naval collision, a one-way munition killing NATO personnel), at the 10% midpoint. Subtracting the two published ranges endpoint-wise is naive — they are not independent and the brief never intended them to be differenced — so the range is indicative and the midpoint is the authored quantity. A second overlap is NOT de-rated because the brief gives no rate to subtract: `russian-fire-on-nato` (limb b) could also be fatal, though neither of its two historical cases was. Baseline de-rated to 0.0657 so that exp(0.8 x 15/50) x exp(0.5 x 18/50) x 0.0657 = 1.27125 x 1.19722 x 0.0657 = 0.100 at the authored hybrid_pressure of 65 and confrontation of 68. Sides are §6.3 stage 4 and nothing else: 'P(reciprocal exchange | fatal incident) 5-15%' at the 10% midpoint. RECURRENCE: the brief prices the FIRST fatal incident; it says nothing about the second, which the broken threshold could make likelier or the resulting sobriety rarer. `oneShot: false` at a constant rate is the neutral choice between them and is stated rather than assumed. Both modifiers fall as the Ukraine war winds down — nato.hybrid_pressure through its ru.war_intensity coupling — which is the gating the brief asks for ('gate: airspace incident rate x ROE assertiveness x hybrid intensity') without a hard gate that would make the hazard vanish at a threshold. WHAT THIS REPLACES: the same event rated identically but split 88 contained / 10.8 fatal / 1.2 fatal-and-reciprocated, which delivered 2.2%/yr of fatal incidents against the 8-20% it cited — the rate was stage 3's and the split was stage 2's. Renamed off `baltic-incident` because the class is not Baltic (sabotage anywhere in Europe, naval collision) and a name that misdescribes its class is the defect §8.1 cost two rounds to. W1 could not author the reciprocal branch at all — a side could not trigger a transition — and approximated it with a standalone `incident-spiral` event gated on confrontation >= 72; that event was removed in W3 because keeping both double-counted the route to armed conflict (measured: ru-nato.conflict-2030 10.5% -> 14.4% against a 4-12% band). KNOWN AND NOT FIXED HERE: (i) `requiresRegimes` is still the base rung only, so the fatal-incident hazard vanishes during a crisis, which is backwards — pre-existing, and widening it adds a second route into the clash rung that needs its own measurement; (ii) the model's crisis -> limited-clash conversion is 28/88 = 31.8% against the brief's 5-20% for 'sustained combat | reciprocal exchange', but the transition is generic across all four routes into crisis while the brief's number is specific to this one, so they are not the same conditional and retuning the transition to it would be wrong.

sides.note: the historical outcome of every fatal incident so far: Turkey/Su-24 2015 (economic retaliation, normalized in ~8 months), Khasham 2018, Przewodow 2022

events.name: NATO destroys a reusable Russian platform
events.provenance: ENGAGEMENT-THRESHOLD §3-§5, limb (a): NATO destroying by weapons fire a Russian-attributed platform that is NOT a one-way munition — a crewed aircraft or a reusable UAV of the Orlan-10/Orion/Bayraktar class. EFFECTIVE 0.08/yr: baseline de-rated to 0.069 so that exp(0.4 x 18/50) x 0.069 = 0.08 at the authored confrontation of 68. This limb has occurred ZERO times: no NATO member has ever downed a Russian reusable platform over NATO territory, and the one engagement of an attributed-Russian Orlan-10 (Oresund, Feb 2026) was jamming, which the market excludes twice over. Rate is therefore FLASHPOINTS §6.3 rung 4's manned-aircraft 2-6%/yr plus a reusable-UAV term that has no published rate but is politically far cheaper than firing on a crewed jet, under the 8 Jul 2026 SACEUR air-defence ROE. NOT GATED on ru.war_intensity: the drivers are ISR tempo and ROE, which survive a ceasefire — unlike the MUNITION class, whose EW-strayed-drone driver disappears when the war ends and which this pack carries in the confrontation level rather than as an event.

sides.note: the Cold War record: the USSR downed ~40 US aircraft with ~200 aircrew killed 1950-1970 and none escalated to sustained combat

events.name: Russian forces employ a weapon against a NATO platform
events.provenance: ENGAGEMENT-THRESHOLD §2-§5, limb (b), the SYMMETRIC limb — added at the owner's direction after W3 recorded that the pack could only ever generate NATO firing while the entire historical qualifying record sits on this side. The two known cases are Russian: a Su-27 releasing a missile near an RAF RC-135 over the Black Sea (29 Sep 2022) and a SAM engagement near a USAF MQ-9 over Syria (Nov 2022). Both are outside NATO territory, which the market's text permits — it imposes no geographic restriction — and the owner's scope decision is to count them. Two events in 4.48 years = 0.45/yr at the top of the range, 0.22/yr at one event; EFFECTIVE 0.17/yr AT t=0. Both cases fell in the war's opening year and none has recurred since, so the rate is authored below the raw 2-in-4.48 MLE rather than at it. Limb (a) 0.08 + limb (b) 0.17 = 0.25/yr, the total the single combined event carried before the split, so this re-attributes mechanism without moving the aggregate. DE-RATING, for BOTH modifiers — the first cut of this constant divided out only the confrontation one and shipped 0.155/yr under a label saying 0.17, which the W3 adversarial review caught: the engine applies every modifier as exp(w x (value-50)/50), so the baseline is 0.17 / (exp(0.4 x 18/50) x exp(0.3 x (35-50)/50)) = 0.17 / (1.15488 x 0.91393) = 0.1611. Note that ru.nuclear_signaling is initial 35, attractor 32 and is bound to no indicator, so its modifier is a permanent SUPPRESSOR that drifts from x0.914 to x0.898 as the factor reverts: 0.17/yr is the rate at the authored state, not a decade average. The realised decade rate is higher regardless, because confrontation drifts up and the cascade doubles hazards while armed.

sides.note: the historical outcome: Russia called the Sep-2022 RC-135 missile release a malfunction and it went no further

factors.provenance: PK brief §1.1/§1.4: 27A (Senate 64-0, NA 234-4) — CDF tri-service command, life immunity, Federal Constitutional Court; FH 2026: 'the military exerts enormous influence... and enjoys impunity'. Near the ceiling because the amendment CONSTITUTIONALIZED what was informal.

factors.name: Civilian governing-coalition strength
factors.provenance: PK brief §1.2: 244/336 on paper, one seat above majority without PPP; cooperation frozen 19 Aug 2026, third dispute in three months; Senate falls to 38/96 without PPP.

factors.name: Opposition street mobilization
factors.provenance: PK brief §1.3: nationwide PTI protests at Khan's third prison anniversary + the KP government (PTI ~93/145), capped by the leader's isolation (23-hr solitary, 31 years of standing sentences) and the post-Nov-2024 crackdown. Khan events shock it.

factors.name: Macroeconomic stress
factors.provenance: PK brief §4: reserves $22.5bn (Aug 2026), S&P B upgrade, growth 3.7% — the 2024-26 stabilization — against inflation re-accelerating (9.2% Jul 2026 vs 5-7% target) and IMF dependence. §4.3: BoP/inflation crisis precedes every modern transition (1969, 1977, 1999, 2022-23).

factors.name: Insurgency intensity (TTP, Baloch, border)
factors.provenance: PK brief §3: 2026 deaths annualizing ~4,780 (+40% over the worst year in a decade); two fronts plus the Afghanistan border war rounds. Internal-security load, NOT the India-facing terror channel — that conduit is in.major-terror-attack impulsing the dyad directly.

factors.name: External patron support
factors.provenance: PK brief §5.2: IMF 3-for-3 on EFF reviews (~$4.8bn disbursed), Saudi/China alignment, Mecca trilateral pact Aug 2026 (W-verified in the dyad brief). Cushions economic stress; imf-derailment cuts it.

factors.name: Nationalist-right vote intention (Reform UK)
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.1: Reform UK ~24.8-25% in the August 2026 polling average (britpolls), against Labour ~24.6-25% and the Conservatives ~19.6-20%. SCALE, uniform across all four D8 packs: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 25% = 57.5, authored 58. The attractor sits slightly below the initial because a mid-parliament insurgent peak three years from a general election is not a fixed point; the reversion is deliberately slow (0.015/mo) because Reform's share has been durable rather than a spike.

factors.name: Capacity to legislate and survive the parliamentary party
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.1: Labour holds 404 seats, a government majority of ~159 and a working majority of ~167 — the largest durability endowment of the four packs, and the fact that matters most for a mid-term exit hazard. Initial 68 also carries Burnham's arrival premium (net approval ~+15.2% in August 2026 against Starmer's -23.8% on departure); the attractor at 58 is the honeymoon decaying toward a normal mid-term government, not a crisis.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §3. SCALE, uniform across the four packs: 50 = 2.5% of GDP on core defence, 20 points per percentage point. The UK sits near 2.5% and is committed under the Hague Investment Plan to a credible incremental path to 3.5% core (= 70 on this scale) with a 2029 review. CHARACTERISED, not fetched: the brief has the UK as the third-largest NATO spender in absolute terms but I did not fetch a current UK GDP percentage, so the initial is the announced 2.5%-class figure and is the weakest-sourced number in this pack. The attractor at 62 (3.1%) encodes the pledged path arriving only partly by 2036, not the full 3.5%.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b override-table convention. The UK is an E3 nuclear power outside the EU whose entire post-1949 defence posture is alliance-first; it is placed highest of the four. No fetched index backs this number — it is a judgement, and it is a REPORTING-grade input here rather than a load-bearing one: it modifies no hazard and feeds one small coupling.

factors.name: Nationalist-right vote intention (AfD)
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.2: AfD FIRST at ~27-27.8% in August 2026 (PolitPro, Statista), against CDU/CSU ~21.2-23%. SCALE, uniform across the four D8 packs: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 27.3% = 61. The near-flat attractor encodes a trajectory that has risen steadily since the February 2025 election (AfD 152 seats, second) rather than a spike; the state elections in month 0 (Saxony-Anhalt 2026-09-06, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 2026-09-20, AfD polling 36-37% in MV) are cited as evidence for the level, not modelled as events (§4.3, named v1 gap).

factors.name: Coalition cohesion and capacity to legislate
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.2: a CDU/CSU-SPD coalition with a Bundestag majority — durable by arithmetic — but under sustained pressure from internal disputes and falling chancellor approval, which the coalition's own reform package (tax relief, pension change, deregulation) was explicitly framed to answer. Authored at the neutral 50: majority arithmetic and internal strain in balance. This is the pack's most judgement-laden initial and it is deliberately the least extreme of the four.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.2/§3: €117.2bn in 2026 rising to €162bn by 2029, about 3.2% of GDP (3.5% counting broader defence-related items). SCALE: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 3.2% = 64. The attractor at 72 (3.6%) is the funded 2029 path continuing; Germany is the closest of the four to the Hague core-defence floor and the only one whose published multi-year plan reaches it.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b override-table convention. Germany funds the largest European defence budget but has the strongest domestic constituency for restraint and the deepest historical inhibition on force employment, so it is placed below the UK and Sweden and near France. No fetched index backs this number.

factors.name: Nationalist-right vote intention (Rassemblement National)
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.3: Bardella at 32% in the first round (Odoxa-Mascaret, May 2026), nearly double Edouard Philippe at 17%, and winning the run-off in every tested scenario; late-2025 Odoxa polling had him at 35-37%. SCALE, uniform across the four D8 packs: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 32% = 68. This is the HIGHEST nationalist initial of the four packs and the one with the most consequence, because it drives a presidential branch rather than a coalition branch. The attractor is set marginally below the initial: 32% is down from 35-37% six months earlier, so the trajectory is flat-to-easing rather than rising.

factors.name: Capacity to pass a budget and survive censure
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.3: the LOWEST initial in the four packs, and it is a description rather than a forecast. Since the 2024 snap dissolution the Assembly has been hung; four prime ministers served between 2024 and 2025; Lecornu survived censure 'by a handful of votes' in October 2025 and carried the 2026 budget only by invoking Article 49.3, with adoption confirmed in February 2026 after two no-confidence motions failed. A government that can pass a budget ONLY by a mechanism that bypasses the vote is the definition of low durability. The attractor at 32 encodes partial normalisation after the 2027 elections without assuming it.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.3/§3: €68.5bn in 2026, about 2.25% of GDP, raised despite wider deficit pressure. SCALE: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 2.25% = 45 — the LOWEST of the four and the furthest from the Hague 3.5% core-defence floor. The attractor at 58 (2.9%) encodes a rising but deficit-constrained path; France is the pack where fiscal pressure and the alliance commitment pull hardest against each other.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. France is an independent nuclear power with a strategic-autonomy tradition that is Europeanist rather than Atlanticist: high willingness to underwrite EUROPEAN collective defence, lower attachment to the Atlantic framing than the UK or Sweden. Placed just above Germany. No fetched index backs this number.

factors.name: Nationalist-right vote intention (Sweden Democrats)
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.4: SD stable at ~18-20%, described by the source as the dominant structural feature of Swedish politics. SCALE, uniform across the four D8 packs: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 19.3% = 49. This is the LOWEST nationalist initial of the four — and the observation worth carrying is that it is lowest in the country where the nationalist right has the most actual power, because SD already supplies the governing majority under the Tido Agreement without holding a ministry. Vote share and governing influence are different quantities and this pack models the first.

factors.name: Capacity to pass a budget and hold the confidence arrangement
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.4: a three-party MINORITY government (M, KD, L) dependent on Sweden Democrat confidence-and-supply, three weeks from an election its bloc is losing in the polls (governing bloc ~42-46% against the red-green ~52-55%). Below the neutral 50 for the minority arithmetic and the governing fatigue the source names; above France's 22 because the Tido arrangement has actually held for a full term and passed four budgets.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.4/§3: +SEK 26.6bn in the 2026 budget, an 18% increase taking military spending to 2.8% of GDP, with a stated intent to reach the 3.5% core-defence target by 2030. SCALE: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 2.8% = 56. The attractor at 70 is exactly the 3.5% floor and the reversion is the FASTEST of the four packs (0.012/mo) because Sweden is the only one of the four with a published date for arriving there — 2030, five years before the alliance deadline.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. Sweden abandoned two centuries of non-alignment to join NATO in 2024, is a Baltic front-line state, and is the only one of the four whose accession is recent enough that the decision itself is evidence of the disposition. Placed just below the UK. No fetched index backs this number.

factors.name: PiS vote intention (largest single nationalist-right list)
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §5: PolitPro poll average, 23 Aug 2026 — PiS 22.4%, its lowest standing in years, tracked here as the single largest nationalist-right list per the established convention (a pack tracks one party, matching se.json's SD-only precedent). Poland's nationalist-right vote is UNUSUALLY fragmented across four lists (PiS 22.4%, Konfederacja 14.4%, Konfederacja Korony Polskiej 10.1%, Rozwoj Plus 6.5% — summed ~53.4%, but openly hostile to each other, not a coherent bloc); the fragmentation itself is encoded in the election-outcome transition's provenance rather than in this factor, which stays a single-party read for cross-pack comparability. SCALE, uniform across the D8/E1 packs: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 22.4% = 54.

factors.name: Tusk coalition's capacity to hold together and win re-election
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §3: a four-party coalition (KO+PSL+Poland 2050+Lewica) with only 9-12 seats of headroom (240-243/460 against a 231 threshold), which survived two tested crises in 2026 (the Feb 2026 Poland 2050/Centrum split, the 30 Apr 2026 Hennig-Kloska no-confidence vote) without losing a floor vote — hence above Sweden's 40 (a minority government with no comparable survived floor test). But PolitPro's 23 Aug 2026 seat projection gives the incumbent coalition only 42.8% of seats if an election were held today, well short of a majority, and PSL/Poland 2050 are individually BELOW the 5% threshold and depend on running jointly with KO — a governing-fatigue pattern the attractor (38, below the initial) is set to reflect: surviving to 2027 is more likely than winning it.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §4, read directly off NATO's own 'Defence Investment of NATO Countries (2014-2026)' PDF (3 Jul 2026), Table 3: Poland's core defence expenditure at 4.68% of GDP for 2026 (estimate). SCALE, uniform across the D8/E1 packs: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 4.68% = 94. Government communications cite a higher national-definition figure (~4.8%, with a repeated 5%-by-2030 aspiration); the NATO-harmonised figure is adopted for cross-polity comparability, per this pack's own flagged composition-dependence note. Attractor set to the ceiling (100 = 5.0%) reflecting the stated 2030 aspiration, already the highest initial of any Eastern Flank pack — NATO's July 2026 estimate projects Poland to be OVERTAKEN by all three Baltic states specifically in 2026 (see ee/lv/lt.json), inverting Poland's own 'NATO's #1 spender' self-image.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. Poland hosts NATO's largest eastern-flank US presence (~8,000 troops, V Corps (Forward) HQ at Poznan, an operational ballistic-missile-defence site), ran a March 2025 mass voluntary military-training programme targeting 100,000 volunteers/year by 2027, and EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §1 records that Tusk and Nawrocki's New Year addresses converged on defence investment as a shared priority even amid an otherwise adversarial cohabitation. Set as the highest atlanticism of the five E1 packs: unlike Finland (nationalist strength genuinely orthogonal to NATO alignment) or Hungary/Slovakia-style skepticism elsewhere in the roster, Poland's defence commitment is the one dial its two warring executives do not contest.

factors.name: Dual constitutional-legitimacy dispute (government vs. Constitutional Tribunal)
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §7, the brief's own flagged single most important domestic risk factor and explicitly recommended as its own dial: since Dec 2023 the Tusk government has refused to publish Constitutional Tribunal rulings or nominate judges to vacant seats (4 of 15 unfilled or contested), on the grounds the Tribunal itself is unlawfully constituted; the CJEU ruled 24 Mar 2026 this breaks EU law; the Tribunal has reciprocally struck down the government's own flagship KRS judicial-reform bill (20 Nov 2025); the dispute was still live as of 14 Aug 2026 (Tusk seeking to install an ally as a Tribunal judge). LOW = deep, unresolved dual-legitimacy dispute (the t=0 state); a two-thirds Sejm majority plus absolute Senate majority is required to resolve it structurally and no bloc holds one, hence the SLOW reversion and a modest attractor (35, not a return to full normalcy) rather than a fast-resolving durability shock. Explicitly INDEPENDENT of the president-PM cohabitation dial: the brief's own argument is that a future unified government of either bloc would still inherit this condition.

factors.name: Finns Party (PS) vote intention
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §5: PS at 14.6% (Verian/HS, 19 Aug 2026), the top of a robust 14-15% current band after collapsing below 8% in the 13 Apr 2025 municipal elections (from 14.5% in 2021) and recovering through 2026 -- a real trough-and-recovery, not noise. SCALE: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 14.6% = 42. DISTINCTIVE WARNING from the source brief: PS is Finland's governing coalition's finance-ministry partner, not an opposition insurgent, and is explicitly NOT NATO-skeptic or Russia-accommodating -- unlike AfD/RN/Reform elsewhere in this roster, a rising PS does not predict a less-Atlanticist Finland. Attractor set marginally above initial (43) reflecting the 2026 recovery trend continuing modestly, well below its 20.1% 2023 election peak (raw 50).

factors.name: Orpo coalition's capacity to hold together and win re-election
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §3: a four-party coalition (NCP+PS+RKP+KD) with a comfortable 108/200 majority, no seats lost mid-term, and one survived near-crisis (Sept 2025's Keskisarja 'population replacement' remarks disrupted the 2026-2029 budget-framework talks and pushed the government 'close to collapse' per Bloomberg, but no discipline followed and the budget passed) -- hence a majority-government initial above Sweden's 40. But NCP itself, the anchor party, polled 16.5% on 19 Aug 2026, its lowest in over five years, against SDP leading every 2026 poll by 6-9 points; the attractor (46, below the initial) reflects a high-confidence expectation of losing the 2027 election to an SDP-led alternative -- ordinary democratic-alternation risk, the source brief's own framing, not coalition-implosion risk.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §4: SIPRI's cross-polity-comparable core-defence figure, 2.8% of GDP (2025 fact sheet, released 27 Apr 2026), adopted over two adjacent-but-different 2026 figures the brief explicitly warns not to average (the MoD's own 2.5% budget-branch proposal; Defence Minister Hakkanen's wider 2.4% 'defence- and security-related' category, which explicitly does NOT count toward the 3.5% core target). SCALE: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 2.8% = 56. Stated forward commitment is 3% by 2029 (raw 60, the attractor) -- lower ambition and a full year later than Sweden's 3.5%-by-2030 pledge. Reversion set SLOWER than Sweden's (0.008 vs 0.012): the brief's own flagged §7 finding is that public debt at 89.7% of GDP (Q1 2026), a 0.2% 2025 growth rate and 10.0% unemployment (Statistics Finland LFS, Jun 2026) are a real fiscal constraint on funding the ramp, distinct from any party's foreign-policy stance.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. Placed above Sweden's 66: Finland has the alliance's longest NATO-Russia border (~1,340km, more than doubling NATO's pre-accession total on joining), withdrew from the Ottawa landmine convention specifically to permit border re-mining (effective Jan 2026), has hosted a US rotational-access DCA since Sept 2024 covering 15 facilities, and became host nation for NATO's ninth forward-presence formation, Forward Land Forces Finland, activated 6 Jun 2026. Near-universal cross-party consensus: SDP, the likely 2027 government, is the party that led Finland's own 2023 NATO accession under PM Marin and is at least as hawkish as NCP on defence spending -- so, unlike government_durability, this factor is not expected to move much on the 2027 election result.

factors.name: EKRE vote intention (hard-right populist)
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §5: PolitPro trend to 23 Aug 2026, EKRE 13.9%. Tracked over the higher-polling Isamaa (22.3-25.2%) because the source dossier explicitly characterises EKRE as 'hard-right populist, Euroskeptic' -- the party genuinely comparable to AfD/RN/PiS elsewhere in this roster -- while Isamaa is Christian-democratic/national-conservative and mainstream-opposition, a different category. SCALE: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 13.9% = 41. (NG1a CORRECTION, 2026-08-25: this read 'so 13.9% = 46', which is 50 - (20-13.9)/1.5 -- DIVIDED where the convention multiplies. The correct value is 50 - 6.1*1.5 = 41. A different slip from lv's in the same block.)

factors.name: Michal coalition's capacity to hold a floor majority
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §3: on 9-10 Aug 2026 (two weeks before this pack's epoch) one MP defected from each coalition party in successive days, dropping the government to 50 of 101 seats -- one short of an absolute majority, and the SECOND coalition rupture in 18 months after SDE's expulsion in March 2025. A no-confidence vote needs 51 of all members so the government is not automatically toppled, but its position for the autumn budget and for the concurrent 2 Sep 2026 presidential vote is materially weakened. Set below every other Eastern Flank pack's initial (Sweden's 40, Poland's 43): this is the only E1 government that has ALREADY lost its floor majority before any election.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §4: the Estonian government locked in a baseline of at least 5% of GDP from 2026 (18 Mar 2025 decision), holding through 2027-2029; the 2026 budget is EUR2.4bn / 5.4% of GDP, up 42% from 2025 (Estonian Ministry of Defence, kaitseministeerium.ee). SCALE, uniform across the D8/E1 packs: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 5.4% = 108.
