This is the first Eastern Flank pack whose raw value exceeds the default 0-100 range -- MAXIMUM raised to 120 (6.0% of GDP) to leave headroom above the already-locked-in 5.4% floor rather than clipping the initial value against the ceiling. Reversion set SLOWEST of the five E1 packs: Estonia already exceeds the alliance's 2035 target nine years early and has publicly pushed for an even higher NATO-wide figure, so there is little further near-term movement to model.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. Estonia is a first-line Article-5 tripwire state hosting a UK-led enhanced Forward Presence at Tapa, requested Article 4 consultations ONCE after the 2025-09-19 MiG-31 airspace violation (three armed aircraft, ~12 minutes), the North Atlantic Council meeting 2025-09-23 (NG1b VERIFIED 2026-08-26: this read 'twice within ten days'. Source: nato.int official text, 2025-09-23), and is the alliance's most publicly hawkish member on the 5%-of-GDP figure (§4). Placed below Poland (82) given Estonia's currently-fragile government has less institutional bandwidth to act on that disposition, but above Finland/Sweden given the sharper, more immediate border-incident record (Narva incursions rising from an 18-incident to a 96-incident baseline).

factors.name: Keskerakond (Centre Party) vote intention
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §5, the DISTINCTIVELY BALTIC dynamic the source dossier proposes as a candidate factor: Keskerakond, historically the vehicle for Russian-speaking voters, polls 21.2-21.8% (PolitPro, 23 Aug 2026) -- Estonia's second-largest party, and proportionally the largest such bloc of the three Baltic states (Estonia's Russian-speaking population is 20.2% national, 87.7% in Narva; Latvia's analogous party polls 2.5%, Lithuania's 3.89% -- see ee/lv/lt.json's coverage declarations for why only Estonia carries this factor). SCALE, distinct from nationalist_strength's convention since this tracks a mainstream governing-eligible party rather than a populist fringe: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 21.5% = 71 (midpoint of the cited range).

factors.name: Sovereign Power (SV) vote intention
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §5: SKDS poll, 15 Jul 2026 -- Sovereign Power (SV, anti-establishment/nationalist, founded 2022, led by Julija Stepanenko) at 17.1%, the largest of THREE distinct ethnic-Latvian nationalist/populist lists (SV 17.1%, Latvia First/LPV 14.8%, National Alliance/NA -- now a governing coalition partner -- 8.7%; combined ~40%). Tracked as the single largest, matching the roster's one-party convention; the fragmentation itself (three hostile lists rather than one bloc) is recorded in the election-outcome transition's own provenance. SCALE: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 17.1% = 46. (NG1a CORRECTION, 2026-08-25: this read 'so 17.1% = 76' and the factor was stored at 76, which the pack's own display scale converts to 37.3% -- the raw percentage multiplied instead of its deviation from the 20% base. 17.1% is 2.9 points BELOW 20, so it is 50 - 2.9*1.5 = 46.)

factors.name: Kulbergs caretaker government's capacity to hold until, and past, the election
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §3: PM Kulbergs's four-party government, in office since 28 May 2026, is explicitly characterised by outside analysis (OSW) as a CARETAKER administration ahead of the 3 Oct 2026 election -- the lowest initial of any Eastern Flank pack, below even Estonia's already-minority 30, reflecting that Latvia's government has not merely lost a majority but has openly abandoned governing-for-the-term in favour of managing to the election. The proximate cause: a 7 May 2026 Ukrainian-drone strike on a Rezekne oil depot triggered the Defence Minister's resignation and the Progressives' withdrawal of support, felling PM Silina's government within a week. Ten parties cluster near or below the 5% threshold in current polling, including a SITTING coalition partner (ZZS, 4.2%, below threshold) -- the attractor (28) reflects that this fragmentation persists past the election rather than resolving it.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §4: the Latvian Ministry of Defence's own published series -- 2024 3.3%, 2025 3.80%, 2026 4.73% of GDP (EUR2,157,966,637), against the Finance Ministry's 10 Mar 2026 GDP forecast -- 'continuing the targeted move toward 5% of GDP' (mod.gov.lv). SCALE: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 4.73% = 95. Latvia is the ONLY one of the three Baltic states not yet at or above 5% for 2026, trailing Estonia (5.4%) and Lithuania (5.38%) despite similar rhetorical commitment; attractor set to the ceiling (100 = 5.0%) reflecting the stated trajectory, with the slowest-but-one reversion of the five E1 packs given the greater distance still to close.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. Latvia hosts a Canadian-led multinational brigade (~3,500 troops) and absorbed THREE dated kinetic incidents in 2026 alone (7 May Rezekne, 8 Jun Latgale, 14 Aug Balvi -- all drone shoot-downs or strikes, the last just ten days before this pack's epoch), a materially higher incident tempo than any other E1 pack. Placed comparably to Estonia (78) rather than lower despite the government crisis: the source brief's own framing is that the hybrid-incident record has driven governing INSTABILITY, not reduced Atlanticist disposition -- the Rezekne strike toppled a government precisely because the public reaction demanded MORE defence accountability, not less alignment.

factors.name: Nemuno Ausra (Dawn of Nemunas) vote intention
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §5: PolitPro trend to 23 Aug 2026, Nemuno Ausra (populist, expelled from government Jun 2026) at 11.3-12%, tracked as the largest single nationalist-populist list -- ahead of the newer, more explicitly nationalist National Alliance (NS, ~4-5%). Lithuania's nationalist-right is the smallest and most fragmented of the five E1 packs by this measure. SCALE: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 11.7% (midpoint of the cited range) = 38.

factors.name: Sinkevicius coalition's capacity to hold together and win re-election
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §3: three Prime Ministers in thirteen months (Paluckas resigned 31 Jul 2025 amid a corruption/fine scandal after a presidential ultimatum; Ruginiene's government fell Jun 2026 when LSDP expelled Nemuno Ausra over a former leader's Holocaust-minimisation fine), each transition WITHIN the LSDP-anchored bloc rather than a loss to the opposition. The reconstituted coalition (LSDP+LVZS+DSVL) is smaller and more exposed -- 75/141 seats, down from the original 86-seat coalition. Current polling: the three coalition parties combined poll ~28-29%, barely ahead of the single opposition party TS-LKD at 22.9% -- hence an initial near Poland's (43) but slightly lower, reflecting the demonstrated turnover pattern even though the bloc itself has not yet lost power.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §4: the Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence's own release confirms the Seimas approved a record EUR4.79bn / 5.38% of GDP defence budget for 2026 -- the HIGHEST defence-spending ratio in NATO (kam.lt). SCALE, uniform across the D8/E1 packs: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 5.38% = 108 -- exceeding the default 0-100 range, MAXIMUM raised to 120 matching ee.json's same accommodation. Political leadership across government and opposition agreed in Jan 2025 to hold spending at an average 5-6% of GDP through 2030 (attractor 112 = 5.6%), with no planned tax increases -- the most durable, genuinely cross-partisan commitment of any E1 pack, hence the slowest reversion in the roster.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. Set as the HIGHEST atlanticism of the five E1 packs: Lithuania sits at the Suwalki Gap (the sole land corridor between the Baltic states and the rest of NATO, assumed a first target in any conflict), hosts Germany's largest permanent overseas basing commitment since WWII (the 45th Panzer Brigade at Rukla, reaching full operational capability of ~4,800 troops in 2027), and has taken NATO's single most assertive rules-of-engagement stance -- authorising peacetime shoot-downs of intruding drones, a step none of the other four E1 states have taken. The Jan 2025 cross-partisan 5-6%-of-GDP defence pact (see defence_effort) reinforces this: commitment here survives even the demonstrated coalition churn.

factors.name: Fidesz vote intention (largest nationalist-right party, now in opposition)
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.1/§4: PolitPro aggregate 23 Aug 2026, Fidesz-KDNP 23.6% -- a 15-point collapse from its 38.6% list vote in April, and the party is now in OPPOSITION. SCALE, uniform across the D8/E1/E2 packs: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 23.6% = 55. DECLARED CHOICE, per the brief §4: the roster convention is the largest single nationalist-right party, so Fidesz alone; Fidesz + Mi Hazank (7.6%) would read 31.2% = 67, twelve points higher. The bloc reading is the rejected alternative. SEPARATELY worth carrying: Hungary's nationalist right took 44.2% of the list vote for 29% of the seats, because a mixed-member majoritarian system met a fully consolidated opposition -- a pack reading this factor off SEATS would overstate the collapse by ~15 points.

factors.name: Tisza government's capacity to hold its majority and its amendment power
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.1: the most durable configuration in the entire roster. A SINGLE party holding 141 of 199 seats -- no coalition partner who can withdraw, no confidence-and-supply dependency, 3.5 years to the next election -- and a governing party whose support has RISEN 12.7 points since its own election (Tisza 65.9%). Highest initial of any pack in the model. The attractor (72, below the initial) reflects that 65.9% is a ceiling rather than a floor and the first concrete grievances are already visible (the end of the interest-rate cap, energy subsidies, medicine VAT) against a 5.2%-of-GDP deficit and a promised defence ramp. The number that matters is not the 41-seat majority cushion but the EIGHT-seat cushion above the 133-seat constitutional threshold: eight defections would end the amendment power without endangering the government, which is why this factor gates the supermajority state and not the government's survival.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2, read off NATO's own 'Defence Investment of NATO Countries (2014-2026)' fact sheet (3 Jul 2026), Table 3: Hungary at 2.09% of GDP for 2026e. SCALE: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 2.09% = 42. HUNGARY IS ONE OF THE VERY FEW ALLIES WHOSE CORE RATIO HAS FALLEN since its trend peak -- 1.84% (2022) to 2.21% (2024) to 2.06% (2025e) to 2.09% (2026e), i.e. flat-to-falling, and 1.41 points BELOW the Hague core floor. The lowest defence_effort initial of any pack in the model. Attractor 55 (2.75%) rather than the stated 5%-by-2035 Ankara commitment, and the reversion is the SLOWEST in the roster, for a reason the brief states: the commitment is corroborated-not-primary (not found in a Hungarian government or NATO primary document), and it runs against a 5.2%-of-GDP deficit with 1.6-2.3% growth. Pricing the stated target as the attractor would model an announcement rather than a trajectory.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention, and the single factor in this pack most changed by the April 2026 election. Hungary spent a decade as the alliance's and the EU's most obstructive member; within four months of the change of government it lifted the Ukraine EU-accession veto (3 Jun 2026), agreed the release of EUR16.4bn in frozen funds, joined the EPPO, and committed at Ankara to a defence ramp. Placed at 58 -- above the neutral 50 and rising, but well below the Eastern Flank packs (74-84) for two documented reasons: Magyar explicitly does NOT support fast-tracking Ukrainian accession, putting it at 10-15 years and floating a Hungarian referendum at the end of it; and the Russian energy relationship is structurally intact whatever the politics (a 2035 oil phase-out, eight years later than the EU's own target; ~60% of gas via TurkStream; Paks II under construction on a Russian state loan, reactors due 2033 and 2035 -- both inside this horizon). The politics turned; the dependencies did not.

factors.name: Fratelli d'Italia vote intention (largest nationalist-right party, governing)
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.2/§4: PolitPro aggregate 23 Aug 2026, Fratelli d'Italia 27.0%. SCALE: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 27.0% = 61. The number worth carrying is not the level but the STABILITY: FdI polls 27.0% against its 26.0% at the 2022 election -- a governing party four years in with no erosion at all, which is unusual anywhere in this roster and is the opposite of the incumbency decay fi.json and ee.json price. DECLARED CHOICE: FdI alone, per the roster convention. The nationalist-right BLOC reads ~33% including the Lega (6.0%) or ~39.5% including Futuro Nazionale (6.5%), and the bloc reading is the rejected alternative. Italy is the only pack where a THIRD nationalist-right party sits outside the coalition and attacks it from the right; see the election-outcome transition.

factors.name: Meloni coalition's capacity to hold together and win re-election
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.2/§3.1: a four-party coalition with cushions of +36 in the Chamber and +16 in the Senate, unchanged in composition since October 2022, having survived the thing that felled its nearest precedent -- Meloni lost the 22-23 March 2026 constitutional referendum 53.2% to 46.8% and did NOT resign, where Renzi resigned within days of losing his in 2016. Set high (68) accordingly, second only to Hungary's supermajority. The attractor (58) reflects real and dated erosion the initial does not: the Lega has halved to 6.0%, Vannacci's Futuro Nazionale took eight deputies out of the coalition and withdrew support on 31 Mar 2026, and the annual Ukraine-aid decree is now a coalition stress test with a named dissenter. The 2027 election, not a mid-term collapse, is what this factor is really about.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2, read off NATO's own fact sheet (3 Jul 2026), Table 3: Italy at 2.10% of GDP for 2026e. SCALE: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 2.10% = 42 -- tied with Hungary for the lowest in the model. THE DEFINITIONAL CHOICE, declared: Rome's own headline figure is 2.8%, a BROAD defence-and-security number Meloni presented at Ankara; the NATO-harmonised core figure is adopted for cross-polity comparability, and the two must not be mixed. Italy's whole compliance story is one discontinuity -- 1.52% (2024) to 2.09% (2025), +38.5% real in a single year, then +1.01% in 2026 -- so it cleared the old 2% floor and stopped. Attractor 58 (2.9%) reflects Crosetto's stated +0.15-0.2 points/yr path rather than the 3.5% destination, because the path is capped by a binding and dated fiscal constraint: Italy's 2025 deficit came in at 3.1% of GDP, exit from the excessive-deficit procedure is expected in 2027 rather than 2026, and Italy declined to activate the national escape clause for 2026.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. Italy has sent twelve military aid packages worth over EUR3bn to Ukraine since 2022, signed a bilateral security agreement in 2024, and extended military transfers through 2026 by decree in December 2025. It was also the only G7 member ever to join the Belt and Road Initiative and the first country ever to leave it (non-renewal notified December 2023), replacing it with much harder golden-power screening. Placed at 68 -- solidly Atlanticist, below Poland (82) and the Baltics, because the commitment is renewed by ANNUAL DECREE and each renewal is a coalition stress test with a named dissenter: the December 2025 decree passed only after weeks of dispute and a Lega abstention threat, and Salvini argued further aid would fuel corruption rather than end the war. The next renewal falls due inside this horizon at roughly month 4.

factors.name: Vox vote intention
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.3: PolitPro trend 23 Aug 2026, Vox 17.5% (SocioMetrica 6 Aug 17.0%, NC Report 4 Aug 18.0%). SCALE: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 17.5% = 46. Vox is up 5.1 points on its 2023 result, the largest gain of any Spanish party, and the attractor is set marginally above the initial for a dated reason: post-Ceuta polling (the 30-31 July 2026 border crisis, three weeks before this pack's epoch) put PP+Vox at 200-206 seats and the combined left below 35%, among its worst recorded results. Vox is not in national government and is not a plausible entrant before the 2027 election, but it is back in FOUR regional PP coalitions including Andalusia since July 2026, having walked out of all of them in 2024.

factors.name: Sanchez government's capacity to survive to the scheduled election
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.3/§3.2. This factor measures SURVIVAL, not legislative capacity -- Spain is the pack where those two come apart hardest, and conflating them is the error the brief warns against. Survival is genuinely likely: a Spanish motion of censure is CONSTRUCTIVE, requiring 176 votes AND a named alternative prime minister, and PP+Vox=170, PP+Vox+UPN+CC=172 -- four short, with the missing votes held by parties (PNV, Junts) that will not install Feijoo. So the initial sits below neutral but not low. What pulls the attractor down is the judicial track the brief flags as Spain's single most important risk: nine cases now reach the governing party's core, including the PM's wife ordered to stand trial and his former organisation secretary facing 24 years, and the realistic mid-term exit path is Sanchez choosing to go on a COURT date rather than a parliamentary one. There is precedent for the near-miss: his five-day public reflection on resigning, April 2024.

factors.name: Capacity to pass a budget and win floor votes
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.3/§3.2, and the factor this pack exists to carry: SPAIN'S INSTABILITY IS LEGISLATIVE, NOT EXECUTIVE. The last budget approved by the Cortes is the PGE 2023, rolled over under Art. 134.4 into 2024, 2025 and 2026 -- three consecutive constitutional rollovers. The 2026 spending ceiling was voted down 178-164 on 27 November 2025 and the stability path twice more in July 2026. In 2026 the Congress has approved 15 government initiatives and rejected 6, a 28.6% floor-defeat rate, with Junts voting with PP and Vox on every defeat since it formally broke with the PSOE on 27 October 2025. Government parties hold 147 of 350 against a 176 majority; the investiture bloc was 179 and no longer exists. Set at 22 -- the lowest of any durability-family factor in the roster, below Latvia's caretaker government -- because a government that cannot pass a budget for a fourth consecutive year is at the floor of what 'governing' means, while still being very likely to survive.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2, from Spain's own July 2026 report 'Spain in NATO': 2% of GDP consolidated in 2025 and 2026. SCALE: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 2.0% = 40 -- the lowest in the model. THE DEFINING FACT: Spain was the ONLY NATO member to refuse the Hague 5% commitment (June 2025), agreeing a bilateral understanding at 2.1% instead, and it has NO 3.5% path. The attractor is 42 (2.1%) -- the only attractor in the roster that sits BELOW the alliance's core floor, and it is authored that way deliberately rather than smoothed toward the alliance target, because pricing a trajectory Spain has explicitly refused would model a wish. The reversion is the slowest in the model for the same reason. This position survived direct pressure: at Ankara (7-8 July 2026) Trump ordered trade measures against Spain over it, and SPAIN CONCEDED NOTHING -- the order was withdrawn within a day and Moncloa's line was that there is 'no additional payment'. Treat 'Spain caved' reporting as wrong; it retro-fits an April 2025 plan onto a July 2026 event. FLAGGED: Spain's own '0.9% in 2018' baseline is not reconcilable with NATO's series and is on a narrower national basis; do not mix it with NATO-basis percentages.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention, and the hardest judgement in this pack because the evidence genuinely points both ways. AGAINST: the 5% refusal, and Spain's refusal of US base access at Rota and Moron for the Iran war from its 28 February 2026 onset, followed by closing Spanish airspace to US strike aircraft on 30 March 2026 -- 'No to the breakdown of international law'. FOR: Spain is, as of June 2026, the ally with the LARGEST NUMBER OF TROOPS DEPLOYED outside its own territory on NATO's eastern flank, holds the maritime component of the Allied Reaction Force and the Multinational Brigade in Slovakia, has raised Ukraine aid every year to ~EUR3.8-4bn cumulative, and is a PURL contributor. Placed at 52 -- just above neutral, and the LOWEST atlanticism in the roster -- because the refusals are about American operations and headline spending targets while the contributions are about NATO's own missions, and a single dial cannot separate them. This is the factor a future reader should attack first.

factors.name: PVV vote intention
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.4/§4: Ipsos I&O July 2026, PVV 11.3% (~17 seats). SCALE: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 11.3% = 37. Wilders has gone from largest party and coalition kingmaker to fourth or fifth in two years: 37 seats (2023) to 26 (Oct 2025) to 19 after seven MPs left on 20 January 2026, the proximate cause being his refusal to admit members to a party of which he remains the sole formal member. DECLARED CHOICE, and the largest such gap in the roster: the nationalist-right BLOC (PVV + JA21 + FvD, ~29%) would read ~66 on this scale -- roughly THIRTY POINTS higher, more than most parameters in any pack. The roster convention (largest single party) is followed and the bloc reading is the rejected alternative. The bloc is not shrinking; it is fragmenting upward, which is a different fact and one this factor cannot express.

factors.name: Jetten cabinet's capacity to survive as a cabinet
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.4: the LOWEST initial in the entire roster, below Latvia's caretaker government (22). A minority cabinet ten seats short of a majority, 22 of 75 in the Eerste Kamer, and -- uniquely since 1918 -- with NO confidence-and-supply agreement, so every bill needs an ad-hoc majority assembled from scratch across a seventeen-party chamber. It faces the 2027 budget on Prinsjesdag, 15 September 2026, in month 0, with the two opposition parties it needs demanding OPPOSITE things: PRO wants EUR6.5bn of social-security cuts reversed and funded by wealth and corporate taxes, JA21 wants welfare cut further and the defence levy scrapped. Its three parties have fallen from 66 seats to 57 in July polling and 47 in an August poll. An August 2026 poll found 78% of Dutch voters expect the cabinet to collapse, 42% before the end of 2026. The attractor is set ABOVE the initial (28) because 20 is a crisis reading, not a steady state -- a Dutch cabinet that survives its first budget has passed its hardest test.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2: 2.59% of GDP on the NATO basis for 2025, up from 1.4% in 2022 and 2.0% in 2024 (the first time the Netherlands met the old 2% standard since the early 1990s). SCALE: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 2.59% = 52. The ministry's own budget line reads ~2.2%; the ~0.4-point gap is definitional and the two must not be mixed. Attractor 70 -- EXACTLY the Hague 3.5% core floor, the same value se.json uses -- and the FASTEST reversion of the E2 packs, because the Netherlands has the strongest commitment in this block: it adopted the full 5%-by-2035 target on 13 June 2025, BEFORE the Hague summit, and the Jetten coalition proposes to put the 3.5% core figure INTO STATUTE, a long-term legal commitment rather than an annual budget line. Spain and the Netherlands are near-opposites on this axis -- comparable current spending, totally divergent commitments -- and the two packs are authored to show it.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. The highest of the four E2 packs and comparable to the Baltics: EUR9.1bn in military assistance allocated with EUR11.6bn further earmarked, EUR1bn to PURL, a complete Patriot system with interceptors, and a Jetten coalition proposing an EU 'Five Eyes' equivalent, 40% joint European procurement, and -- a real break with Dutch precedent -- joining French-led talks on European nuclear deterrence. The attractor is set marginally BELOW the initial for a dated reason: in July 2026 the Defence Minister said the Netherlands had reached the limit of what it can give from its own stocks, and while Jetten framed that as a call for other allies to step up rather than a Dutch drawdown, a stated stock limit is a real ceiling on the most visible form of the commitment.

factors.name: Vlaams Belang vote intention (national)
factors.provenance: E3-BENELUX-BRIEF §B4: PolitPro aggregate 23 Aug 2026, Vlaams Belang 16.0% NATIONAL. SCALE, uniform across the D8/E1/E2/E3 packs: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 16.0% = 44. THREE DECLARATIONS, and this pack needs more of them than any other in the roster. (1) NATIONAL, not Flemish: VB reads 26.6% in Flanders alone, which would be ~60 on this scale -- but Belgium's chamber is national and every other pack in the roster reads a national share, so the national figure is adopted and the Flemish one recorded. (2) VB ALONE, not the bloc: VB + N-VA reads 34.7% nationally, ~72 on this scale, a 28-point gap identical in shape and size to the Dutch PVV declaration in E2 §4. (3) AND THE SHARPEST ONE -- N-VA MUST NOT BE POOLED WITH VB. N-VA is Flemish-nationalist and confederalist in programme but governing, mainstream, and supplies the Prime Minister; a bloc reading would classify the sitting head of government as nationalist-right, which is a category error rather than a wider reading. HOUSE SPREAD, flagged: Ipsos and De Stemming disagree by ~6.6 points on VB in Flanders with overlapping March 2026 fieldwork, which is ~10 points on this dial -- a declarable choice, not a rounding issue.

factors.name: Arizona coalition's capacity to hold and to legislate
factors.provenance: E3-BENELUX-BRIEF §B1/§B5: the five-party Arizona coalition (N-VA+MR+Les Engages+Vooruit+CD&V) under Bart De Wever, sworn in 3 February 2025 after a 239-day formation, holding 80 of 150 against a 76 majority -- a cushion of FOUR, the thinnest in the roster, and it has never held the 81 the coalition agreement implies because one member left the N-VA group the day before the government was sworn in. Set below neutral for that margin and for a fiscal position that is the government's actual stress: 20 hours of talks produced the November 2025 budget against nationwide strikes, and the March 2026 monitoring committee then required EUR4.9bn of further savings by 2029 with the deficit at 3.8% of GDP. De Wever has publicly threatened resignation during budget rounds. None of it has moved the seat count, which is why the initial is 42 rather than lower -- and why this factor is named for holding AND legislating, since the coalition's promised seventh state reform needs 100 votes it cannot assemble (see the coverage note on state-disintegration).

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: E3-BENELUX-BRIEF §B3, from NATO's own Defence Expenditure of NATO Countries (2014-2026) fact sheet, 7 July 2026: Belgium at 2.00% of GDP for both 2025e and 2026e. SCALE: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 2.00% = 40. THE HISTORY AND THE TREND POINT OPPOSITE WAYS AND BOTH ARE TRUE: Belgium was the SINGLE LOWEST core-defence spender in the entire alliance in 2024 at 1.27%, below Luxembourg, Slovenia, Albania, Canada and Spain -- and its 2025 real increase of +58.52% was the alliance's SECOND LARGEST, behind only Luxembourg. THE ATTRACTOR EQUALS THE INITIAL, WHICH IS DELIBERATE AND IS THE POINT: Defence Minister Francken stated on 8 July 2026 that Belgium 'will maintain 2 per cent defence spending until 2029', with the Hague 3.5% acknowledged and a roadmap promised but no dated path. Belgium has a declared PLATEAU, not a ramp, and the flattest reversion in the roster encodes it. Contrast lu.json, whose identical starting point carries a declared +0.1-points-per-year ramp -- same axis as Spain against the Netherlands in E2, one tier down.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. Belgium is a NATO founder member and hosts both NATO headquarters and SHAPE, and it signed the Hague Investment Plan with the other thirty allies. Placed at 62 -- solidly committed and unremarkable, below the Netherlands' 76 and Italy's 68 -- because the commitment is institutional and geographic rather than fiscal: Belgium was the alliance's lowest spender as recently as 2024 and has now declared a plateau at the old 2% floor rather than a path to the new one. Hosting the alliance and funding it are different quantities and this factor reads the second. Unlike at.json and ch.json in this same block, the roster-standard factor name is kept here without qualification: Belgium is a full member and 'willingness to underwrite collective defence' asks it a question it can answer.

factors.name: ADR vote intention
factors.provenance: E3-BENELUX-BRIEF §L4: Ilres, 24 April 2026 -- ADR 11.4%, up 2.1 points on its 9.27% in the October 2023 election. SCALE, uniform across the D8/E1/E2/E3 packs: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 11.4% = 37. THE ROSTER'S CLEAREST CASE OF A NATIONALIST RIGHT THAT IS GROWING BUT STRUCTURALLY MINOR, and the one pack in this block with NO bloc-vs-party ambiguity at all: unlike Belgium, where N-VA sits adjacent to Vlaams Belang and supplies the prime minister, no larger nationalist party sits beside the ADR and the governing CSV is unambiguously Christian-democratic mainstream. The attractor is set marginally above the initial because the ADR is rising against a CSV that has shed 7.4 points since its own election. VINTAGE FLAGGED: April 2026 is the most recent verified voting-intention set -- the July 2026 Politmonitor wave reports government approval but no voting intentions.

factors.name: CSV-DP coalition's capacity to hold
factors.provenance: E3-BENELUX-BRIEF §L1: a TWO-party coalition (CSV+DP) under Luc Frieden, sworn in 17 November 2023 after a 40-day formation -- against Belgium's 239 in the same year, which is the cleanest available illustration of the two systems' difference. It holds 35 of 60 against a 31 majority: a cushion of four, numerically identical to Belgium's, in a chamber two and a half times smaller and with three fewer partners. Set well above neutral for that: two parties, a comfortable proportional margin, one uneventful ministerial reshuffle in December 2025, and an Ilres reading of 49% approving the government's work against 36% disapproving. The attractor sits modestly below the initial on one specific signal -- Frieden himself does not appear in the top ten most popular politicians while his deputy and two opposition figures do, which is a governing-fatigue indicator rather than a coalition-arithmetic one.

factors.name: Core defence spend against the Hague 3.5% floor
factors.provenance: E3-BENELUX-BRIEF §L3, from NATO's own fact sheet (7 July 2026): Luxembourg at 2.03% of GDP for 2026e. SCALE: 50 = 2.5% core, 20 points per percentage point, so 2.03% = 41. THE DENOMINATOR IS THE FINDING, and it is a larger definitional trap than Italy's 2.8%-vs-2.10% in E2: Luxembourg's NATO obligation is measured against GROSS NATIONAL INCOME rather than GDP, an explicit NATO-sanctioned exception granted because its GDP per capita is far above the alliance average, and STATEC records that this makes its required spending 'about 35% lower than it would be if calculated using GDP'. The Luxembourg government's own release states the Hague commitment as '5% of GDP (or GNI in Luxembourg's case)'. THE NATO-HARMONISED GDP FIGURE IS ADOPTED for cross-pack comparability and the GNI series is recorded as the rejected alternative; a pack reading the GNI numbers would sit ~2 points higher and would not be comparable with any other pack in the roster. THE ATTRACTOR ENCODES A DECLARED RAMP: Defence Minister Backes, 20 May 2026, set out +0.1 points of GNI a year -- 2.1% (2027), 2.2% (2028), 2.3% (2029) -- explicitly stopping at 2029 because NATO reviews the trajectory then and Luxembourg holds elections in 2028. Contrast be.json's identical starting point and FLAT attractor: same axis as Spain against the Netherlands in E2, one tier down. Luxembourg's 2025 real increase of +60.66% was the LARGEST of any ally.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. Placed slightly above Belgium's 62 despite a near-identical GDP ratio, on the strength of the derivative rather than the level: Luxembourg posted the alliance's largest single-year real increase in 2025 (+60.66%), carries a dated year-by-year ramp to 2029, and devotes 51.77% of core spending to equipment -- a very small force buying capability rather than manpower, with military personnel of about 1,000. Per head it outspends Belgium by more than half again ($1,707 against $1,093 in 2026e). A NATO founder member with no ambiguity about the commitment; the roster-standard factor name is kept without qualification, unlike at.json and ch.json in this same block.

factors.name: FPO vote intention
factors.provenance: E3-NEUTRALS-BRIEF §A5: PolitPro trend 23 Aug 2026, FPO 37.6% -- up 8.8 points on its 28.85% win in the September 2024 election. SCALE, uniform across the D8/E1/E2/E3 packs: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 37.6% = 76. THE HIGHEST NATIONALIST-RIGHT READING IN THE ROSTER, clear of Romania's 74 and well above France's 68 (NG1a, 2026-08-25: this read "above Latvia's 76 by a hair" -- lv was stored at 76 by a unit error and is now 46, so the comparison was between at's correct 37.6% and lv's INTENDED 17.1% under the same number. B1 §4's correspondence class: one value, two referents). Six individual 2026 polls span 36-39% with no trend inside that range, so the level is well measured and flat rather than rising. Kickl leads the Kanzlerfrage by more than the other three party leaders combined. The contrast that matters for authoring: Austria's nationalist right is at a historic high and ACCELERATING (+8.8 since its own election), where Switzerland's is at a historic high and STATIC (+0.1) -- see ch.json's same factor, and do not give the two a shared drift term.

factors.name: Stocker three-party coalition's capacity to hold
factors.provenance: E3-NEUTRALS-BRIEF §A1: the first three-party coalition in Austria since 1949 (OVP+SPO+NEOS, 110 of 183, a +18 cushion), formed only on the SECOND attempt after the FPO won the 2024 election and two separate negotiations collapsed -- five months and two failures between an election and a government. Set below neutral for that formation record and for a live August 2026 crisis over drought aid and the climate law that Chancellor Stocker had to take into the Chancellery personally; it settled on 21 August 2026, three days before this pack's epoch, with tensions resuming immediately over interpretation. Above Spain's 44... equal to it, in fact, and for the opposite reason: Spain's government cannot be removed but cannot legislate, Austria's can legislate but is three parties wide with the largest party outside it polling 37.6%. The attractor sits below the initial because the three coalition parties now sum to ~43.9% against the FPO's 37.6% alone.

factors.name: Defence spend as a share of GDP
factors.provenance: E3-NEUTRALS-BRIEF §A3. SCALE retained for cross-pack comparability (50 = 2.5% of GDP, 20 points per percentage point) but THE HAGUE REFERENCE IS DROPPED: Austria is not a NATO member and appears nowhere in the Hague framework, so unlike es.json -- which declined a floor it was under -- this is a floor Austria was never under. The factor reads a raw GDP share here and the pack says so. DECLARED READING, since two circulate and differ by ~0.3pp (= 6 points on this scale): the Austrian-inclusive ~1.19% of 'relevant GDP' for 2027-28 from the Defence Ministry's own budget documents is adopted over the ~1.0% World Bank basis, so 1.19% = 24. Attractor 40 = 2.0%, Austria's OWN target (2% by 2032 under Aufbauplan OBH 2032+), NOT an alliance figure. The reversion is among the slowest in the roster because the target is measurably failing: the Landesverteidigungsbericht 2026/2027 records a EUR12.6bn shortfall through 2031, and Parliament's own Budgetdienst told the 10 July 2026 floor debate that 2% by 2032 'cannot be reached with current financial planning'. Austria activated the EU's national escape clause in February 2026 -- up to 1.5% of GDP of fiscal room, conditional on defence -- and is not using it, so the gap is a choice rather than a constraint.

factors.name: Participation in European security structures (non-alliance)
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. THIS FACTOR REPLACES `atlanticism`, AND THE RENAME IS THE POINT. For a constitutionally neutral state, 'willingness to underwrite collective defence' reads near zero and reads it for a reason the number conceals -- a legal prohibition, not a preference -- which is the B1 §4 / W4.5 correspondence class exactly: near-identical factor names, a different question underneath. What Austria actually does is participate deeply WITHOUT alliance: Art. 23j B-VG admits CFSP and EU military operations, ten PESCO projects (coordinating one), eleven EU/NATO/UN missions, over 200 troops in Bosnia, NATO Partnership for Peace since 1995, and membership of the European Sky Shield Initiative that the current government explicitly kept against FPO objections. Placed at 58 -- above neutral and rising slowly -- with the ceiling held down by the single most model-relevant neutrality number the brief found: 90% of Austrians want EU military support FOR Austria while 13% support Austria reciprocating under Art. 42(7). That 90/13 asymmetry is not a preference about alliances; it is a free-riding preference, and it is what caps this factor.

factors.name: SVP/UDC vote intention
factors.provenance: E3-NEUTRALS-BRIEF §S5: PolitPro trend, SVP/UDC 28.0%. SCALE, uniform across the D8/E1/E2/E3 packs: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 28.0% = 62. TWO THINGS MAKE THIS A DIFFERENT OBJECT FROM EVERY OTHER nationalist_strength IN THE ROSTER. First, THE SVP IS IN GOVERNMENT -- two of the seven Federal Council seats under the magic formula -- while simultaneously sponsoring the neutrality initiative the Federal Council is campaigning against; it is not an opposition insurgency and must not be modelled as one. Second, and this is why the reversion is the slowest in the block: the SVP's national share has moved +0.1 POINTS SINCE 2023 while Austria's FPO has moved +8.8. Switzerland's nationalist right is at a historic high and STATIC; Austria's is at a historic high and ACCELERATING. Giving the two a shared drift term would be wrong. VINTAGE FLAGGED HONESTLY: the trend line is dated 23 August 2026 but its most recent individual poll is November 2025 -- Swiss national voting-intention polls are infrequent between elections. Treat this as 28-30% last measured November 2025, not as an August 2026 reading; Sotomo had it at 30.4% in September 2025, the first Swiss party past 30% since proportional representation arrived in 1919.

factors.name: Capacity to carry policy past a referendum
factors.provenance: THIS FACTOR REPLACES `government_durability`, AND THE REPLACEMENT IS THIS PACK'S CENTRAL CLAIM. E3-NEUTRALS-BRIEF §S6: the Federal Council cannot be removed -- no confidence vote, no recall, no dissolution -- so government survival is structurally 1.0 and is not a quantity. What CAN fail, on a fixed calendar roughly four times a year, is the government's policy. The base rates are hard: popular initiatives pass 24 of 213 times since 1891 (11.3%), and of the ~6% of parliamentary decisions ever challenged by optional referendum, roughly 36-42% are rejected by voters. Set at 55 -- above neutral, because the government wins most contests it enters -- and calibrated so that the referendum events below draw near their historical rates. THE E2 §3.2 PARALLEL IS EXACT: the Netherlands separates cabinet fall from PM exit and models the cabinet because that is where the instability lives; Switzerland separates government survival (1.0) from policy survival (~0.6-0.65 per challenged law) and models the policy. A pack mapping Swiss instability onto leader exit would predict ZERO where the real quantity is a third of contested legislation.

factors.name: Defence spend as a share of GDP
factors.provenance: E3-NEUTRALS-BRIEF §S3. SCALE retained for cross-pack comparability (50 = 2.5% of GDP, 20 points per percentage point) but THE HAGUE REFERENCE IS DROPPED ENTIRELY, as in at.json: Switzerland is in neither NATO nor the EU, so no external framework applies at all and its number is wholly domestic. The 2026 army budget of CHF 7bn is roughly 0.8% of GDP, so 0.8% = 16 -- THE LOWEST DEFENCE READING IN THE MODEL, against 0.66% on the VBS's own 2024 accounting and 1.33% as recently as 1990. Attractor 30 = 1.0%, Switzerland's OWN target, and the date is 2032 rather than the widely-cited 2030: parliament adopted 1%-by-2030 motions in May 2022, then extended the deadline to 2032 while keeping the level, and official VBS pages still carrying the 2030 title should not be cited for the target year. THE ATTRACTOR IS GATED ON A POPULAR VOTE, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS PACK: the 1% path is not financed, and the Federal Council's August 2026 Botschaft proposes a temporary earmarked VAT increase (+0.5 points from 2028 for twelve years, feeding a debt-capable defence fund) that is a CONSTITUTIONAL amendment under Art. 130 BV and therefore requires a mandatory referendum with a double majority. That vote is planned for summer 2027 and is authored below as ch.defence-funding-vote.

factors.name: Participation in European security structures (non-alliance)
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. REPLACES `atlanticism` for the same reason at.json does, and the two neutrals' shared rename is the block's clearest correspondence finding: 'willingness to underwrite collective defence' reads near zero for both, for structurally DIFFERENT reasons the single number would conceal. Placed BELOW Austria's 58, and the gap is the substantive judgement. Switzerland aligns with EU sanctions but incompletely and with a widening lag -- it completed the 19th package in February 2026, implemented the 20th only partially in May 2026, and declined to list seven third-country companies in what analysts called a deliberate political choice. Its December 2025 War Materiel Act relaxation permits supply to 25 Western countries but still explicitly does NOT permit deliveries to Ukraine. Against that: 56% public support for NATO cooperation, membership of the European Sky Shield Initiative alongside Austria, and a Security Policy Strategy 2026 whose own text concedes that surrounding EU and NATO states 'expect Switzerland to contribute more to European security'. The attractor sits barely above the initial because the direction of travel is real but slow, and because the 27 September 2026 vote below could freeze it constitutionally.

factors.name: Chega vote intention
factors.provenance: E4-PORTUGAL-IRELAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A4: PolitPro trend 9 August 2026, Chega 24.3%. SCALE, uniform across the D8/E1/E2/E3/E4 packs: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 24.3% = 56. Chega's trajectory is the fastest in the roster -- 1.3% (2019), 7.2% (2022), 18.1% (2024), 22.8% (2025) -- and the 2025 election made it the OFFICIAL OPPOSITION: it tied PS on vote share and took two more seats, so for the first time in Portuguese democratic history neither PS nor PSD is one of the two largest parties. Attractor set two points above the initial for that trajectory, with a slow reversion because six years of monotone rise is a trend rather than noise. PORTUGAL IS THE ROSTER'S CLEANEST CASE FOR THE LARGEST-PARTY CONVENTION, precisely because the convention makes no difference here: the other Portuguese nationalist vehicles (ADN, Ergue-te, Nova Direita) took under one percent between them in 2025 and returned no seats, so the bloc reading differs from this one by about a point -- against the Netherlands' 30, Denmark's 10 and Hungary's 11. See the rejected alternative in reference class pt.chega-ceiling for the number that IS worth 14 points.

factors.name: AD minority government's capacity to hold
factors.provenance: E4-PORTUGAL-IRELAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A1, §A5. AD (PSD+CDS-PP) holds 91 of 230 against a majority of 116 -- TWENTY-FIVE SHORT, the widest gap of any governing formation in the roster. Set slightly below neutral rather than low, because the structural fact is not weakness but OPTIONALITY: the XXV Government has TWO different majorities available and used both inside one year. A right majority with Chega (91+60 = 151) carried the nationality law 152-64 on 1 April 2026; a centre majority by PS abstention carried the 2026 State Budget on 27 November 2025, with Chega voting AGAINST. Neither partner alone can bring the government down and neither alone is needed to pass everything. The actual failure mode is the one Montenegro named publicly in July 2026 -- PS and Chega voting TOGETHER against the government on spending, from opposite directions -- which is not what a minority-government durability dial usually encodes, and the pack says so rather than letting the number imply the usual thing. Attractor two points below the initial: AD has fallen ~7 points since the election while Chega has risen.

factors.name: Defence spend as a share of GDP
factors.provenance: E4-PORTUGAL-IRELAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A3. SCALE uniform across the roster: 50 = 2.5% of GDP core, 20 points per percentage point. DECLARED READING: NATO's own Defence Investment of NATO Countries (2014-2026) fact sheet of 3 July 2026, Table 3, gives Portugal 2.10% core for 2026e, so 2.10% = 42. THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE IS THE LARGEST DEFINITIONAL GAP IN THE MODEL, 20 POINTS: at the Ankara summit (7-8 July 2026) Montenegro announced 3.1% of GDP for 2026, which decomposes as 2.1% core (~EUR6.7bn) plus 1.0% (~EUR2.5bn) of dual-use energy, telecommunications and transport projects counted under the Hague framework's defence-and-security-related pillar. That reads 62 on this scale. NATO's Table 3 is adopted because defence_effort is defined cross-pack on the CORE measure and Table 3 is what every other pack in this roster reads; taking Lisbon's number for Portugal alone would make it incomparable with Italy's or Spain's. For scale, E2 recorded Italy's equivalent gap (NATO 2.10 against Rome's broad 2.8) at 14 points. Portugal cleared the old 2% floor in 2025, twelve years late, and stopped -- the same discontinuity-then-plateau shape E2 §2 recorded for Italy, arrived at one year later. Attractor 50 = 2.5%, slow reversion, because the plateau is the observed behaviour and nothing in the 2026 budget changes it. FLAG: the 2.1/1.0 decomposition is from Portuguese business press, consistent across two independent write-ups, and I did not find it in a primary MoD or Finance Ministry document.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. Portugal carries the roster-standard atlanticism rather than E3's european_security_integration, and the distinction from ie.json in this same block is the point: Portugal is a NATO FOUNDER MEMBER (1949) with no neutrality tradition and no constitutional fence of any kind on alliance commitment, so 'willingness to underwrite collective defence' has a plain referent here. Placed above neutral rather than high, for two measured reasons: the core spend cleared 2% only in 2025 and has plateaued (see defence_effort), and Portugal's alliance value has historically been GEOGRAPHIC -- Atlantic basing, principally Lajes Field on Terceira -- rather than expeditionary. The second of those is the one this model cannot draw: see this pack's notes. Flat attractor because nothing in the 2026 budget or the Ankara commitments moves the underlying posture.

factors.name: Largest nationalist-right vote intention
factors.provenance: E4-PORTUGAL-IRELAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B9: Ireland Thinks / Sunday Independent, fieldwork 31 July 2026 -- Independent Ireland 7% and Aontu 7%, TIED. SCALE uniform across the roster: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 7% = 31. IRELAND IS THE ONLY POLITY IN THE ROSTER WITH NO IDENTIFIABLE LARGEST NATIONALIST-RIGHT PARTY, and the convention still resolves it: take the largest single vehicle. The bloc reading (14%) is 41, a 10-point declaration, the same size as Denmark's and a third of the Netherlands'. THE HONEST NOTE, and it is why this factor carries a caveat no other pack's does: neither number is measuring the thing. In the presidential election of 24 October 2025, 213,738 ballots -- 12.9% of all votes cast, against 1.23% in 2018 -- were SPOILED, on an organised 'Spoil The Vote' campaign launched by eight right-of-centre figures on the grounds that the two-candidate ballot excluded conservative voices. A record in Irish electoral history by an order of magnitude. So the same electorate that gave a left independent 63.36% simultaneously produced a 12.9% organised spoil. A dial read off a party's vote share measures the VEHICLE in a system where the vehicle has repeatedly failed to exist, while the demand it would carry shows up in ballot spoiling, in the independent bloc's 13.2%, and in the April 2026 fuel protests that nearly broke the government. This is the Danish vehicle-vs-policy caveat in a third form -- vehicle vs DEMAND -- and 31 is declared with it rather than as an unqualified reading.

factors.name: FF-FG coalition's capacity to hold
factors.provenance: E4-PORTUGAL-IRELAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B6. Fianna Fail 48 + Fine Gael 38 + supporting independents; Martin elected Taoiseach 95-76 on 23 January 2025 against a majority of 88 of 174 (or 87 of 173 excluding the Ceann Comhairle, who votes only to break a tie -- both figures circulate and this pack means the latter). Set just below neutral, and the reason is a measurement rather than a mood: THE GOVERNMENT HAS ALREADY BEEN TESTED ONCE. During the 2026 Irish fuel protests, junior minister Michael Healy-Rae resigned mid-debate on 14 April 2026 saying the government had 'let the people of Ireland down', his brother Danny voted against, and the government survived the confidence motion 92-78 -- FIVE above the threshold. That is the first crack in the coalition and it leaves a working cushion of five. Attractor two points lower: the two government parties total 36% in the July 2026 polling against 45.7% at the election, a 10-point loss, while no single opposition party is above 20%.

factors.name: Defence spend as a share of GDP
factors.provenance: E4-PORTUGAL-IRELAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B8. SCALE retained for cross-pack comparability (50 = 2.5% of GDP, 20 points per percentage point) but THE NATO REFERENCE IS DROPPED ENTIRELY: Ireland is not a member and appears in no NATO table, so this is not a floor it has declined (es.json) nor one it was never under while adjacent to the alliance (at.json, ch.json) -- there is no alliance framework here at all. Source is the European Defence Agency's Defence Data 2025-2026: Ireland 0.2% of GDP against an EU average of 2.2% rising to 2.4%, with 23 of 27 member states at or above 2%. 0.2% = 4, THE LOWEST IN THE MODEL AND A QUARTER OF SWITZERLAND'S 16, which was E3's floor. DECLARED READING: Irish GDP is inflated by multinational profit attribution, so GNI*/GNP is the standard corrective and gives 0.3% = 6; the two are two points apart and the pack takes the GDP basis because that is the denominator every other pack in this roster uses. Attractor 8 (~0.4%) rather than higher, and the reason is that the constraint is not the budget: the 2026 Defence Vote Group allocation is a record EUR1.49bn, up 11% on 2025 and 35% since 2022, but total Defence Forces strength was 7,767 in 2026 against an establishment of 9,739 and an LOA2 target of 11,500 by 2028 -- roughly 2,000 below its own establishment and 3,700 below its stated target, with the Naval Service (807 personnel) at times able to deploy a single patrol vessel. A defence_effort of 4 here is not merely a low budget; it is a force that cannot currently man the ships it owns. FLAG: the EUR1.49bn 2026 allocation and the EUR1.5bn-by-2028 LOA2 target are in different price bases and must not be read as 'target already met'.

factors.name: Participation in European security structures (non-alliance)
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention. THIS FACTOR REPLACES `atlanticism`, following at.json and ch.json -- AND IRELAND INVERTS BOTH OF THEM, which is the finding this provenance exists to record. Austria's neutrality is CONSTITUTIONAL and fences the ALLIANCE question (Neutrality Act 1955, constitutional rank, 122 of 183 to repeal) while its CSDP participation is deep and unfenced. Switzerland has no constitutional definition of neutrality at all. Ireland's neutrality is POLICY -- it has never been enshrined, and four attempts to enshrine it failed -- so NOTHING constitutional bars NATO accession; what IS constitutionally fenced is EU common defence, by Art. 29.4.9 ('The State shall not adopt a decision taken by the European Council to establish a common defence... where that common defence would include the State'), inserted by the Twenty-Eighth Amendment in 2009 after the first Lisbon referendum failed. SO FOR IRELAND THE RENAMED FACTOR NAMES THE QUANTITY WITH A CONSTITUTIONAL CEILING AND THE REJECTED `atlanticism` NAMES THE ONE THAT IS MERELY POLICY -- the exact inverse of Austria. The rename is kept for comparability (all three neutrals read low on the same dial) and the inversion is declared here, because this is B1 §4's correspondence class for a third time and THE FIRST TIME IT APPEARS AS AN INVERSION RATHER THAN A DIFFERENCE: three low numbers produced by three different mechanisms, two of them on opposite axes. Placed at 52 and rising: six PESCO projects as a full member (including Critical Seabed Infrastructure Protection, 2023-2035, which matters because Ireland sits on the transatlantic cable corridor) plus observer status on seventeen more; the EU Council Presidency from 1 July to 31 December 2026 -- month 4 -- with security and defence a stated priority; and the triple lock reform in flight (see ie.triple-lock-reform), whose stated trigger is that Ireland had to WITHDRAW from Operation IRINI when the Security Council's mandate lapsed.

factors.name: Dansk Folkeparti vote intention
factors.provenance: E4-DENMARK-GREENLAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A4: PolitPro trend 23 August 2026, DF 12.2%. SCALE uniform across the roster: 50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point, so 12.2% = 38. DF is GROWING AFTER ITS ELECTION, not before it: 9.10% and 16 seats on 24 March 2026 -- the single largest gain of that election, +11 -- and 12.2% five months later. The bloc reading is a 10-point declaration: DF+DD = 17.9% (48), DF+DD+Borgernes = 18.6%. The roster convention takes the largest single party, so 38, and the fragmentation is real but NARROWING -- Danmarksdemokraterne peaked in 2022 and is receding (5.75% to 5.7%), Borgernes Parti is fading fast (2.13% to 0.7%). THE CAVEAT THIS PACK MUST CARRY, and it is the Danish form of the B1 §4 correspondence class: Danish immigration policy has been executed by a SOCIAL DEMOCRATIC government since 2019, and DF's 2022 collapse to five seats is usually attributed to that appropriation. So a dial read off DF's vote share measures THE VEHICLE, not THE POLICY, and the two have moved in opposite directions for seven years. Compare ie.json in this same block, where the mismatch is vehicle vs DEMAND. (This paragraph's causal claim is a characterisation from standard commentary; I found no quantitative instrument for it.)

factors.name: Frederiksen III minority coalition's capacity to hold
factors.provenance: E4-DENMARK-GREENLAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A1. Socialdemokratiet 38 + Green Left 20 + Moderaterne 14 + Radikale Venstre 10 = 82 of 179 against a majority of 90 -- EIGHT SHORT -- relying on Enhedslisten (11) and Alternativet (5) from outside, which reaches 98. Set below neutral for the eight-seat gap and for the election that produced it: Socialdemokratiet's 21.84% is ITS WORST RESULT SINCE 1903, down 12 seats, and it remains by far the largest party. Not set lower, because the confidence-and-supply partners are to the government's LEFT and have nowhere else to go -- the alternative to this government is a right bloc including DF at 16 seats. Attractor a point below the initial: PolitPro's August 2026 seat projection puts the incumbent coalition at 44.7% of seats, still short of 90.

factors.name: Defence spend as a share of GDP
factors.provenance: E4-DENMARK-GREENLAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A3. SCALE uniform across the roster: 50 = 2.5% of GDP core, 20 points per percentage point. DECLARED READING: NATO's Defence Investment of NATO Countries (2014-2026) fact sheet of 3 July 2026, Table 3, gives Denmark 3.49% core for 2026e, so 3.49% = 70. THE HIGHEST IN THIS ROSTER OUTSIDE THE EASTERN FLANK, and DENMARK IS THE LARGEST RISER IN NATO THAT IS NOT ON THAT FLANK: 2022 to 2026e it multiplies its core share by 2.55x, second only to Luxembourg's 3.56x, and gains +2.12 points, fifth-largest absolute gain behind only Estonia, Lithuania, Latvia and Poland. The reason is Greenland and the Arctic, not the eastern flank. THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE IS 0.01 OF A POINT AWAY AND STILL DECIDES A VERDICT CLASS: Denmark's own Ministry of Defence and Danish trade press state flatly that Denmark REACHES 3.5% in 2026, while NATO's Table 3 says 3.49% -- and NATO's accompanying news item counts exactly five allies expected to meet the 3.5% guideline in 2026, which by its own numbers are Lithuania, Estonia, Latvia, Poland and Greece. Denmark is sixth, one hundredth of a point outside. So 'Denmark meets the Hague core floor nine years early' is true on Copenhagen's arithmetic and false on NATO's. Table 3 is adopted because every other pack in this roster reads it. The gap's mechanism is identifiable: Denmark counts its Ukraine Fund toward the figure (up DKK 3.8bn in 2026 to DKK 14.0bn total), and that uplift carries the last fraction of a point -- while Denmark is simultaneously CUTTING military aid to Ukraine, DKK 9.4bn in 2026 against 16.5bn in 2025. The dial rises while the transfer falls. Attractor 74 (3.7%) on the stated path of 3.5% core sustained plus 1.5% defence-and-security-related by 2030, i.e. the full Hague 5% five years early.

factors.name: Willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per the C4.0b convention, and THE ONLY FACTOR IN THIS ROSTER WHOSE ATTRACTOR SITS EIGHT POINTS BELOW ITS INITIAL. Denmark answers the alliance question maximally on paper: a NATO founder member since 1949, and since the referendum of 1 June 2022 -- 66.9% yes, 33.1% no, turnout 65.8% -- a full participant in EU CSDP, having held the defence opt-out alone in the EU since the 1993 Edinburgh Agreement. That is the initial. The FALLING attractor is the Greenland crisis and it is measured, not inferred: on 19 January 2026 the Danish Defence Intelligence Service listed THE UNITED STATES as a potential national security threat for the first time in its history, and Premier Nielsen said a military conflict could not be ruled out. 'Willingness to underwrite collective defence' has a plain referent for Denmark -- unlike at, ch and ie in this roster, which is why this pack keeps atlanticism rather than european_security_integration -- but the alliance whose defence Denmark underwrites now contains the state its own intelligence service names as a threat to it. The attractor encodes that erosion; the reversion is the fastest of any atlanticism dial in the roster because the movement is recent and one-directional. THIS IS NOT COUPLED to us.json, per Programme E's no-couplings rule -- see this pack's notes on what that rule now costs.

factors.name: AUR vote intention
factors.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A4. THE ROSTER'S SECOND-HIGHEST nationalist_strength, behind Austria's 76. (NG1a, 2026-08-25: this claimed the HIGHEST, BY 18 POINTS -- measured against Portugal's 56, i.e. against the E5 block alone, while at (76) and fr (68) were already higher. lv also read 76 until NG1a corrected a unit error to 46.) AUR alone on the PolitPro trend of 23 August 2026 reads 35.7%, which is 73.6 on the roster scale (50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point); take 74. The bloc reading (AUR + SOS + Velichie-equivalent POT = 39.7%) is 79.6 and is recorded as the same-question rejected alternative -- a SIX-POINT declaration, the roster's second-smallest after Portugal's, because the vehicle has absorbed its rivals rather than shared with them: AUR gained 17.8 points since the December 2024 election while SOS and POT lost 9.7 between them and now poll 2.8% and 1.2%. The nationalist right here CONSOLIDATED into one vehicle; Denmark's fragmented and Bulgaria's migrated. ATTRACTOR HELD FLAT AT 74 DELIBERATELY. The measured trajectory is steeply up (18.01% at the election, 35.7% eighteen months later) and encoding that slope as an attractor would be authoring a forecast rather than a level; the noise is set high (1.2, the roster's joint-highest) instead, because this is a dial that has genuinely moved 27 points in eighteen months and a pack that let it sit still would be understating what it can do. THE CORRESPONDENCE HAZARD, DECLARED NOT FIXED, and it is the third of the E-programme's four distinct forms: this dial measures the POST-ABSORPTION PARTY, and the largest single measurement of the underlying demand was ANNULLED. Calin Georgescu polled ~5% and took 22.94% on 24 November 2024; the election was voided; he was barred from the re-run; AUR then absorbed most of that electorate. The model has no representation for a candidate, so the pre-absorption number is unexpressible here. See the ro.aur-ceiling reference class for the head-to-head measurement, which is a DIFFERENT quantity and must not be adopted as a level.

factors.name: Capacity of a Romanian government to hold office
factors.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A1, §C13. THE ROSTER'S LOWEST INITIAL, and it is a description rather than a judgement: at t=0 Romania has no fully-empowered government at all. Bolojan's cabinet resigned by operation of Art. 110(2) on 5 May 2026 and exercises only Art. 110(4) caretaker functions; two designations have failed; there is no PM-designate. 18 sits below the Netherlands' 20 and France's 22 because those two describe governments that exist. THE ATTRACTOR IS THE LOAD-BEARING NUMBER, not the initial: 38 is where a formed Romanian government sits, and it is set below the neutral 50 because Romania's mid-term departure rate (0.331/yr) is the roster's second-highest. Reversion 0.020 is the roster's fastest for this dial, which is the pack saying that Romanian formation failures END -- the previous records are 51 and 48 days -- even though the current one has run 119. NOT A DIAL FOR THE PARLIAMENT'S SURVIVAL: see this pack's notes. A low value here raises ro.pm-exit and ro.formation-failure and does NOT raise any dissolution hazard, because in Romania the two are constitutionally decoupled.

factors.name: Romanian defence spending
factors.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A3. NATO, Defence Investment of NATO Countries (2014-2026), 3 July 2026, Table 3 -- core defence expenditure as a share of real GDP: 2026e 2.43%, which is 48.6 on the roster scale (50 = 2.5%, 20 points per percentage point); take 49. E5.15's ROSTER FINDING APPLIES HERE AND THIS PACK IS ON THE RIGHT SIDE OF IT: only seven of the twenty packs committed before this block cite NATO Table 3, and ten NATO members cite national budget documents instead, so a reader comparing Germany's 64 against this 49 is comparing Berlin's accounting against NATO's. All five E5 packs take Table 3. THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, worth 7 points: Romania's Ministry of National Defence requested 57bn lei in direct allocations for 2026, stated as 2.81% of GDP -> 56, PLUS 112bn lei in COMMITMENT APPROPRIATIONS for F-35 and Abrams. A request is not an outturn and forward commitments are not annual spend; the 112bn figure is exactly the number that gets quoted as if it were. THE SHAPE CONTRADICTS THE OBVIOUS STORY and the provenance says so rather than fitting a trend: Romania was ABOVE 2% in 2020 and then fell for three consecutive years to 1.61% in 2023 -- the year of the largest Russian escalation -- before rising 35.95% in 2024 and 10.71% in 2026e. It is the only eastern-flank ally whose share declined through 2021-2023. Attractor 54 (2.70%) continues the 2024-2026 direction without carrying a Hague 5% path, which nothing in NATO's own table supports.

factors.name: Romanian willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A3. High, and the shooting has started. In 2026 to mid-August Romania recorded 23 Russian drone airspace violations against 18 in all of 2022-2025 combined, 27 drones or fragments on its territory against 16 in all of 2025, and 54 Russian attacks near its frontier against 28 in 2025; the FIRST interception in Romanian history was in July 2026, followed by two more inside two days, all by Romanian F-16s, and on 20 August 2026 Romania destroyed an explosive drone near the Neptun Deep Black Sea gas project. President Dan has called the breaches intolerable. Romania operates 33 F-16s, eighteen of them bought from the Netherlands for EUR 1 in November 2025, and hosts the European F-16 Training Centre at Fetesti. ATTRACTOR SET BELOW THE INITIAL, at 70, and the reason is the only honest one available: AUR polls 35.7% and is projected 135 of 330 seats, and four national elections fall inside this horizon. That is a drag on the dial and the pack should say so rather than hold it flat. NO COUPLING IS AUTHORED into nato or ru-nato, for a fifth block, and this is the strongest coupling case Programme E has found -- the first with a measured monthly rate behind it. Recorded and not acted on.

factors.name: Integrity of the constitutional-electoral order
factors.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A5, and the roster's SECOND pack to carry a fifth factor beyond the tier-2 four, after pl.json -- which exists for exactly this shape of question. LOW = DEEP CRISIS. THE SCALE IS INVERTED AND IT IS INHERITED DELIBERATELY: pl.constitutional_crisis reads 28 for a live dual-legitimacy standoff, and if this pack scaled the other way the two numbers would not be comparable, which is the whole point of putting the same name on both. THE NAMING HAZARD IS RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED HERE -- a factor named for a crisis and scaled as its inverse is a trap for a reader, and correcting it means re-scaling pl too, which is a decision about existing content and belongs in its own block. WHY 34 AND NOT POLAND'S 28: Romania's sequence was more violent to the electoral order than Poland's is -- CCR Ruling 32/2024 annulled an ENTIRE presidential process unanimously on 6 December 2024 under Art. 146(f), with no appeal; the Central Electoral Bureau barred the leading candidate 10-4 on 9 March 2025 and the CCR upheld it 9-0; President Iohannis resigned on 10 February 2025 rather than face a third suspension vote -- but it is EPISODIC where Poland's is STRUCTURAL. Romania's institutions acted and a valid, higher-turnout (64.72%) election produced a decisive result five months later; Poland's standoff needs a two-thirds Sejm majority nobody holds and cannot resolve at all. So Romania sits above Poland and reverts faster (0.010 against 0.006) toward an attractor of 46 -- near-normal, NOT normal, because Art. 146(f) stands unamended and unappealable and a live 119-day formation failure is the other half of what this dial reads. THE 2024-25 SEQUENCE IS AUTHORED AS REALIZED INITIAL CONDITIONS, NEVER AS A FORWARD-LOOKING PROBABILITY -- see this pack's contested-succession coverage row for the reference-class argument that decided it.

factors.name: Revival (Vazrazhdane) vote intention
factors.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B10. THE ROSTER'S LOWEST nationalist_strength, below Ireland's 31 -- in a country whose government is the most Russia-accommodating in the roster and holds an absolute majority. THAT IS NOT AN ERROR AND IT MUST NOT BE FIXED BY INFLATING THE DIAL. Revival on the PolitPro trend of 23 August 2026 reads 4.7%, which is 27.0 on the roster scale (50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point); take 27. Its collapse is the largest in the roster: 13.78% and 38 seats at its June 2024 peak, 4.19% and 12 seats on 19 April 2026, a loss of 60% of its parliamentary strength; MECh (3.23%) and Velichie (3.10%) both fell under the 4% threshold and lost all 21 of their seats between them, so the nationalist right's entire parliamentary presence fell from 81 seats to 12. The nationalist BLOC's 10.59% -> 36 is recorded as the same-question rejected alternative, a 9-point declaration. THE FINDING IS CARRIED ON atlanticism INSTEAD, AND THIS IS DELIBERATE, on E3's precedent that when a factor name's referent has shifted the answer is to name the right quantity rather than distort the wrong one: OSW measured that 12% of Progressive Bulgaria's vote came from nationalist parties, so the alignment did not evaporate, it MIGRATED -- to a party of the nationalist LEFT. Progressive Bulgaria's 45.8% would read 88.7 and is typed ADJACENT-QUESTION and excluded from this class's spread; merging it would produce a 62-point number, twice the roster's largest same-question gap, and would be B3 §2's pooling error exactly. THE FOURTH DISTINCT FORM of the vehicle-vs-referent hazard the E-programme has recorded, and the sharpest: dk measures the vehicle not the policy, ie the vehicle not the demand, ro the post-absorption party not the pre-absorption candidate, and bg the nationalist RIGHT when the alignment sits on the nationalist LEFT. AND THE SINGLE LARGEST PARTIAL EXPLANATION IS A REALIZED EVENT, AUTHORED AS INITIAL CONDITIONS AND NEVER AS A FORWARD-LOOKING PROBABILITY: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026 at BGN 1.95583 per EUR 1, the ERM II central rate, as the 21st member of the euro area — the Council approved the final legal acts on 8 July 2025, the European Parliament voted 531 for / 69 against / 79 abstentions, and the changeover completed by 31 January 2026. Revival owned the opposing side and had collected over 600,000 signatures against adoption. The ECB's own assessment (9 April 2026) puts the changeover's inflationary impact at 0.3-0.4 percentage points and records that HICP inflation FELL from 3.5% in December 2025 to 2.3% in January and 2.1% in February — so the predicted price spike did not happen, and the party that had campaigned on it lost 60% of its seats four months later. RECORDED AS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A MEASUREMENT: no source found quantifies the causal share. Dual price display in lev and euro was mandatory from August 2025 to August 2026, ending essentially at this model's start month.

factors.name: Capacity of a Bulgarian government to hold office
factors.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B7, §B8.5, §C14. THE PACK'S LARGEST DELIBERATE TENSION, authored as a trajectory rather than settled by moving a rate. At t=0 Bulgaria has its FIRST OUTRIGHT SINGLE-PARTY MAJORITY SINCE 1997: Progressive Bulgaria holds 131 of 240 against a 121 threshold, a cushion of +10, four months old, polling 45.8% against its 44.59% result, with the BSP wiped out of parliament entirely and the opposition split three ways at 15/14/6. 64 is the roster's fourth-highest initial and it describes that. THE ATTRACTOR AT 44 IS WHERE THE HISTORY LIVES: eighteen elections in 35.86 years, only four of seventeen intervals reaching an effective full term, and a 2021-2026 burst at 1.389 elections per year. A pack that carried 64 flat would assert that the single-party majority is the new Bulgarian normal on four months of evidence; a pack that started at 44 would assert that it is already gone. The reversion of 0.012 crosses most of that distance inside the horizon, which is the honest statement: the majority is real now and the roster's most volatile parliamentary record has not been repealed. NOTE WHAT THIS DIAL GATES: bg.pm-exit, and through it EVERY early election in this pack, because Bulgaria has no discretionary dissolution mechanism at all.

factors.name: Bulgarian defence spending
factors.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B9. NATO, Defence Investment of NATO Countries (2014-2026), 3 July 2026, Table 3: 2026e 2.22% of real GDP, which is 44.4 on the roster scale (50 = 2.5%, 20 points per percentage point); take 44. All five E5 packs take Table 3, which is E5.15's roster finding acted on for the new content and not for the existing roster. THE 2019 SPIKE IS A TRAP AND THE PROVENANCE NAMES IT RATHER THAN FITTING A TREND THROUGH IT: Bulgaria's share reads 3.15% in 2019 -- 63 on this scale, higher than Denmark's 2026 figure -- and 1.59% the year after. That is not a policy, it is the up-front payment for eight F-16 Block 70 aircraft contracted in 2019 and paid in a single budget year, and any pack citing 'Bulgaria's peak' or regressing 2014-2026 would be citing a procurement instalment. Attractor 50 (2.50%) continues the measured 2023-2026 direction (+24.81%, +2.66%, +13.65%, +6.80% real) without carrying a path to the Hague guideline. EXPLICITLY NOT RECORDED AS A REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, and the distinction matters: Radev's manifesto promised defence modernisation at 5% of GDP, which would read 100, but a manifesto aspiration with no budget line is not a competing MEASUREMENT of the same quantity -- it is a political statement, and it sits in this pack's machine provenance instead. Bulgaria and Romania are 0.21 points of GDP apart, the closest pair in the block, which is worth saying because their security postures are not close at all.

factors.name: Bulgarian willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: E5-ROMANIA-BULGARIA-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B7, §B10. THE ROSTER'S LOWEST atlanticism AMONG NATO MEMBERS -- 12 points below Spain's 52 and 34 below Romania's 74 -- AND IT IS WHERE THIS PACK'S NATIONALIST FINDING LIVES. Read it beside bg.nationalist_strength's 27: THE TWO NUMBERS DESCRIBE THE SAME ELECTORATE. Bulgaria's Euro-Atlantic scepticism has not disappeared with Revival's collapse; it has moved inside the governing party, which holds 131 of 240. Prime Minister Radev's recorded positions: sanctions on Moscow 'bring no concrete benefits'; he opposed the Bulgaria-Ukraine security cooperation agreement; he advocates normalising relations with Moscow and resuming Russian energy imports. NOT LOWER, and the counterweights are why: he backs continued EU and NATO membership, said during the campaign he would not seek to block the EU's support mechanisms for Ukraine while declining Bulgarian participation, and Bulgaria hosts NATO Air Policing, took delivery of eight F-16 Block 70 by late 2025, contracted 183 Strykers, and transferred enough 155mm ammunition to Ukraine to need stockpile replenishment. ECFR's characterisation -- he 'will probably sound like Viktor Orban when it comes to foreign policy but act more like Robert Fico' -- is recorded as a characterisation and not as a measurement, as is OSW's assessment that the Russia rhetoric served mainly domestic purposes. NO COUPLING is authored into nato or ru-nato, for a fifth block.

factors.name: Greek Solution vote intention
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A4. Greek Solution (Velopoulos) on the PolitPro trend of 23 August 2026 reads 8.2%, which is 32.3 on the roster scale (50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point); take 32. THE ROSTER'S FIRST CASE WHERE THE LARGEST-PARTY CONVENTION HAS A ROTATING REFERENT, and the convention REPORTS MOVEMENT THAT DID NOT OCCUR. Between June 2023 and July 2026 the Greek nationalist-right bloc moved from 12.82% to 12.6% -- it did not move at all -- while the largest-party reading moved from 27 to 32, because the IDENTITY of the largest party changed: the Spartans took 4.68% and 12 seats in 2023 and have ceased to exist as a parliamentary group, while Greek Solution nearly doubled inside a bloc of constant size. That is B1 §4's correspondence class in a form no earlier pack produced -- not a familiar name over a shifted question, but a RULE whose subject changes identity between measurements while the underlying quantity is flat. The three-party bloc (EL 8.2 + FL 3.4 + NIKI 1.0 = 12.6%) reads 39 and is recorded as the same-question rejected alternative; note that the argument for 39 here is NOT that the bloc is bigger -- it is only 7 points bigger, smaller than Denmark's 10 or Hungary's 11 -- but that the bloc is the quantity with a STABLE REFERENT, which is a better argument than any previous pack's bloc alternative and the one a future reader needs. NOT INCLUDED, and flagged as a coding judgement rather than a fetched classification: Course of Freedom (Konstantopoulou, 3.2-5.5%), anti-systemic and sovereigntist but left-populist in origin, which standard classifications place on the left; including it would take the bloc to ~17% and 45.
