NOT AUTHORED, and the largest single uncertainty on the Greek right inside the horizon: Antonis Samaras has not launched a party but is preparing one, and April 2026 SCENARIO polling put a Samaras vehicle at 12% -- a hypothetical, not a vote intention, and it must not be treated as one.

factors.name: Capacity of a Greek government to hold office
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A1, §A2. THE CHAMBER IS NOTHING LIKE THE ELECTION AND THE INITIAL IS PRICED ON THE CHAMBER. June 2023 gave New Democracy 158 of 300 against a majority of 151; the current composition is ND 156, PASOK-KINAL 33, KKE 21, Greek Solution 11, Syriza 10, Niki 8, Course of Freedom 5, and FIFTY-THREE INDEPENDENTS -- the highest such share in the Third Republic. Syriza has lost 37 of its 47 seats to defection and polls 1.1-2.0%, below the 3% threshold. ND's cushion over 151 is FIVE. 46 is therefore just under neutral: a working single-party majority, but a thin and eroding one. THE ATTRACTOR SITS BELOW IT, at 42, and the reason is arithmetic rather than mood: on July 2026 polling ND at ~30% takes roughly 118 of 300 with the bonus (Metron Analysis projected 120 on 30 June), so the modal outcome of the scheduled 2027 election is a hung parliament -- and under Article 37 a hung parliament is three three-day mandates, a judicial caretaker and a second election. NOTE WHAT THIS DIAL DOES AND DOES NOT GATE: it drives gr.pm-exit and gr.early-dissolution, and it does NOT drive the caretaker branch of election-outcome directly -- that branch carries its own factor weight, because a hung parliament is produced by the arithmetic of an election rather than by the outgoing government's condition.

factors.name: Greek defence spending
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A3. NATO, Defence Investment of NATO Countries (2014-2026), 3 July 2026, Table 3: 2026e 3.65% of real GDP -> 73 on the roster scale (50 = 2.5%, 20 points per percentage point). FIFTH IN THE ROSTER, above Denmark's 70 and Germany's 64. Sorting Table 3's 2026e column descending gives exactly five allies at or above 3.5% -- Lithuania 5.33, Estonia 5.10, Latvia 4.92, Poland 4.68, Greece 3.65 -- so Greece is the only one of the five that is not on the eastern flank, and it holds fifth place by 0.16 points over Denmark. THE ATTRACTOR SITS BELOW THE INITIAL AND NO OTHER PACK IN THAT TOP FIVE DOES THAT. Greece's series is not monotone: 3.66% (2021), 3.89% (2022), then a 27.28% REAL FALL to 2.77% in 2023, flat at ~2.78% for three years, and +33.17% in 2026e. Table 8a explains it -- equipment as a share of core spending runs 42.29% (2022), 25.15% (2023), 37.65% (2026e) -- so the share tracks DELIVERY SCHEDULES, not policy, where Poland's, Estonia's and Lithuania's rise monotonically because theirs are structural. 62 is the 2019-2026e mean (3.10%), the plateau the spike sits on. THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE FOR THE INITIAL, worth 11 to 17 points: the thirteen-year mean of 2.82% -> 56, or the 2019-2026e mean -> 62. Not adopted as the INITIAL because every other pack in this roster reads its current-year Table 3 value and a Greece-only mean would be incomparable -- the same reasoning pt.json used to take 2.10 over 3.1 -- but adopted as the ATTRACTOR, which is where a lumpy series belongs. THE PROGRAMME BEHIND IT, all inside the horizon: Agenda 2030, EUR 25-28bn over twelve years with at least 25% to Greek industry, centred on Achilles Shield (Rafael Spyder and David's Sling, IAI Barak MX); 20 F-35As signed 25 July 2024 out of an approved FMS of up to 40 at EUR 8.6bn, deliveries beginning 2028, first four aircraft held in the US until 2030, fleet operational 2033 -- months 17 to 88. E5.15's roster finding applies: all five E5 packs take Table 3, ten of the twenty earlier packs do not.

factors.name: Greek willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A3, §A5. High and flat. Greece spends 3.65% of GDP on core defence, fifth in the alliance, and -- on a figure NATO does not print, derived from Table 7 against population reconstructed from Table 5 divided by Table 6 -- HAS THE MOST SOLDIERS PER HEAD OF ANY ALLY. It drew on the EU's SAFE facility in the first wave (Commission approval 15 January 2026). NOT HIGHER, and the reason is the one this pack carries on its own factor: Greek alliance behaviour is conditioned on a bilateral relationship the model cannot represent -- Greece vetoed Turkish participation in SAFE and states an explicit condition for lifting it. That is gr.accommodation_posture, and a reader should look there rather than reading this dial as the whole of Greek alliance policy. NO COUPLING is authored into nato or ru-nato, for a fifth block.

factors.name: Greek willingness to trade alliance goods for Turkish concessions
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A7.4, §A7.5, and E-PLAN §E5.12. THE FIFTH FACTOR, and it exists because of what this pack CANNOT carry rather than what it can. HIGH = MORE WILLING TO ACCOMMODATE; the scale is NOT inverted (contrast ro.constitutional_crisis, which inherits pl.json's inversion and says so). THE t=0 READING IS AN ACT, NOT AN OPINION: the EU's Security Action for Europe facility is EUR 150bn of low-interest defence procurement loans; 19 member states drew on the first wave, Greece among them; TURKEY APPLIED AND WAS EXCLUDED on veto threats from Greece and Cyprus, and Greece's stated condition for lifting its veto is that Turkey revoke the 1995 casus belli resolution. 22 is a hard line with a named, specific reversal condition. THE ATTRACTOR SITS ABOVE IT, at 30, because the diplomatic track is warming and dated -- the High-Level Cooperation Council is annual and the next round is due -- while the military tempo runs the other way. WHY THIS FACTOR AND NOT A BILATERAL TENSION DIAL, which is the question a reader will ask: airspace violations, EEZ delimitation, mock dogfights and the casus belli are JOINT PRODUCTS of two states' behaviour, and putting them on gr alone would be a factor whose value is set mostly by Turkish decisions -- B1 §4's correspondence failure exactly, and the thing the scenario vocabulary's own rejection of external-armed-conflict forbids operationally ('a polity flag referencing dyad content makes the pack unloadable'). A VETO IS AN ACT OF THE VETOING STATE, so this factor has a Greek predicate throughout, and its two consequences in this pack -- gr.safe-veto-lifted and gr.maritime-zone-extension -- are Greek acts too. See this pack's state-disintegration coverage row for the typed absence.

factors.name: Most vote intention
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B11, governed by reference class hr.nationalist-vehicle. Most (Bridge) on the PolitPro trend of 23 August 2026 reads 9.9%, which is 35.1 on the roster scale (50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point); take 35. THE RANKING HAS INVERTED SINCE THE ELECTION and that is the finding: the Homeland Movement (DP) took 9.56% and 14 seats in April 2024, entered government in May 2024 with three ministries, and now polls 3.6% with a 2% probability of clearing the threshold -- a loss of roughly 62% of its vote -- while Most has gained about 24% in opposition and is projected 18 seats. BOTH ALTERNATIVES ARE RECORDED, DP's 25 and the bloc's 40, because this is a CLASSIFICATION question before it is an aggregation question: if DP is the referent hr reads 25 and becomes the roster's floor; if Most is, it reads 35 and sits mid-table. THE FINDING CARRIED HERE IS DENMARK'S CAVEAT WITH THE SIGN REVERSED. Denmark's nationalist right collapsed while a Social Democratic government executed its policy -- vehicle down, policy up, and the dial measured the wrong one. CROATIA'S COLLAPSED WHILE IT WAS IN GOVERNMENT EXECUTING ITS OWN POLICY. DP holds demographic development and agriculture, it got what it asked for, and it has lost two thirds of its support doing so. A dial read off DP measures THE COST OF OFFICE, not the strength of the demand -- and the demand is visibly intact, because it moved next door to Most. A POLLING CAUTION THAT APPLIES TO EVERY NUMBER IN THIS PACK: PolitPro's trend normalises undecideds and raw pollsters do not, so the two differ by several points across the board (Ipsos, 31 July 2026, n=997: HDZ 27.4, SDP 18.8, Mozemo 13.3, Most 9.0; Promocija plus, 5 July, n=1,300: HDZ 27.0, SDP 21.5, Mozemo 12.2, Most 7.7). Most's raw readings of 7.7-9.0% would give 32-34 rather than 35; the trend value is taken for consistency with every other pack in the roster, and the raw range is recorded here so a reader can see the width.

factors.name: Capacity of a Croatian government to hold office
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B8, §B10. ABOVE NEUTRAL, and the record rather than the arithmetic is why. The Plenkovic III cabinet took office 17 May 2024 on HDZ 61 + DP 14 = 75 against a majority of 76, with a working number of 78 including supporting minority and small-party members -- one seat short on paper, comfortably over in practice. A no-confidence motion in December 2024 FAILED 64 to 76. Ministerial churn has been heavy (Health dismissed November 2024, Agriculture resigned January 2025, Finance out January 2026, Labour February 2026) AND THE GOVERNMENT HAS NOT MOVED -- which is the Croatian pattern: eight of nine parliaments since 1992 ran their term. 56 records that. THE ATTRACTOR SITS SLIGHTLY BELOW IT, at 52, because the coalition partner carrying 14 of its 75 seats is polling below the threshold, so the arithmetic that produced this government is not available to reproduce it. NOTE WHAT REMOVAL ACTUALLY REQUIRES, because it is a third thing distinct from both roster precedents: Article 113 is NOT Spain's or Slovenia's constructive vote -- no named successor is required to remove a government -- and NOT Portugal's bare motion either, which sends the question straight to the country. It is a THIRTY-DAY REPLACEMENT WINDOW FOLLOWED BY AUTOMATIC DISSOLUTION: the chamber may remove a Prime Minister without a successor and then has one month to produce one, failing which 'the President of the Republic shall immediately dissolve Parliament and simultaneously call a parliamentary election'.

factors.name: Croatian defence spending
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B9. NATO, Defence Investment of NATO Countries (2014-2026), 3 July 2026, Table 3: 2026e 2.03% of real GDP -> 40.6 on the roster scale (50 = 2.5%, 20 points per percentage point); take 41, level with Luxembourg and just above Belgium and Spain at 40. THE ATTRACTOR SITS BELOW THE INITIAL AND THE REASON IS IN THE SERIES, NOT IN A JUDGEMENT: Croatia's 2026e share FALLS, 2.07 to 2.03. Only four allies decline year on year in the 2026 estimate -- Finland (-0.10), Croatia (-0.04), North Macedonia (-0.01) and Slovakia (-0.01) -- and Croatia's real spending still RISES +1.01%; the share falls because GDP rises faster. Croatia is the only ally in the roster whose defence_effort attractor has a defensible argument for sitting below its initial on the published series alone. IT IS ALSO THE ALLIANCE'S FOURTH-SLOWEST RISER SINCE 2014: Table 4 gives 2014-2026e real growth of +65.28%, ahead of only the United States (+13.77%), France (+39.43%) and the United Kingdom (+41.71%) -- and those three started from 3.71, 1.82 and 2.13 while Croatia started from 1.81 and has gained 0.22 points of GDP in twelve years, against Denmark's 2.34. AND THE MANPOWER RUNS THE OTHER WAY, WHICH THIS DIAL CANNOT EXPRESS AND SO NAMES: the Sabor amended the Defence Act on 24 October 2025 and MANDATORY BASIC MILITARY TRAINING BEGAN 9 MARCH 2026 -- men aged 19-29, two months, ~4,000 conscripts a year in five cohorts, EUR 1,100 net monthly, curriculum covering cyber, first aid and drone operation, first cohort completed 9 May 2026, the first Croatian conscription since 2008. Table 7 already shows it: personnel 13.5k (2024) -> 13.6k (2025e) -> 14.3k (2026e), the first increase in a decade of decline, while Table 8a shows equipment falling from 34.31% of core spending in 2025e to 23.41% in 2026e as personnel rises to 54.14%. SO CROATIA'S POSTURE IS: MONEY FLAT, MANPOWER RISING, OUT-OF-AREA CONTRIBUTION VETOED BY THE HEAD OF STATE -- three axes pointing three ways. A force-generation factor is the named v1.1 item; this pack does not author one, because a second defence dial in one pack and not in the other twenty-three would be incomparable, which is the same argument that keeps defence_effort on NATO's Table 3.

factors.name: Croatian willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B8, and E-PLAN §E5.13. PRICED ON THE STATE'S BEHAVIOUR, NOT THE GOVERNMENT'S POSITION, and that is the whole point of the number. Plenkovic's HDZ government is an ordinary Atlanticist EPP administration and on its position alone Croatia would read in the 60s with Belgium and Portugal. IT DOES NOT, BECAUSE CROATIA DOES NOT PARTICIPATE IN NSATU -- NATO's Security Assistance and Training for Ukraine command at Wiesbaden -- since President Milanovic, as commander-in-chief, refused to release a handful of staff officers: 'While I am president and the commander in chief, Croatian soldiers, officers and NCOs will not take part in activities that would draw Croatia into a war.' Plenkovic's response was that the President is 'further isolating Croatia on the international scene and destroying its credibility as a NATO member'. THE VETO IS OPERATIVE, NOT RHETORICAL: overriding it needs two-thirds of the Sabor, 101 of 151, against a coalition of 78, and it binds SPECIFICALLY ON OUT-OF-AREA CONTRIBUTION, which is the largest part of what atlanticism means in this roster. Several ambassadorial appointments are vacant for the same reason. 48 is a NATO member that sits out the alliance's Ukraine mission. THE REVERSION IS THE ROSTER'S SLOWEST FOR THIS DIAL, 0.004, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE MACHINERY RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT ABOUT CROATIAN OPINION: hr.presidential-term-ends delivers a +12 impulse at month ~41 and the schema has no way to move an ATTRACTOR, only a value, so a fast reversion would erase the scheduled change within a year of its arriving. At 0.004/month the impulse decays to roughly +9 by the horizon's end, which is the pack asserting that the constraint's removal is durable but not permanent. THE SCHEMA ITEM LEFT BEHIND (v1.1): an event can impulse a factor's VALUE and cannot re-point its ATTRACTOR, so a scheduled structural change has to be authored as a shock plus a slow reversion. This is the first pack in the roster to need that and it is the first to say so.

factors.name: Resni.ca vote intention
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §C16, governed by reference class si.nationalist-vehicle. THE ROSTER'S LARGEST SINGLE FACTOR DISCRETION -- 37 POINTS -- AND THE CHOICE IS DECLARED IN FULL. Resni.ca (Stevanovic) on the PolitPro trend of August 2026 reads 3.5%, which is 25.3 on the roster scale (50 = 20% national vote intention, 1.5 points per percentage point); take 25. SDS reads 27.9% and would be 62. The question is entirely a classification question about SDS and the two most relevant sources disagree flatly: Wikipedia gives its ideology as national conservatism, nationalism and right-wing populism, position centre-right to right-wing; PolitPro classifies it as CHRISTIAN DEMOCRATIC and reserves 'Right-Populist' for Resni.ca alone. SDS is a full member of the European People's Party and sits in the EPP group, which is the strongest argument for the mainstream reading; the S&D group has formally called on the EPP to expel it, which is the strongest argument against. 25 IS TAKEN FOR COMPARABILITY AND FOR NO OTHER REASON: every other pack in this roster reads a party OUTSIDE the mainstream centre-right -- pt reads Chega and not PSD, dk reads DF and not Venstre, at reads FPO and not OVP, hu reads the nationalist right in opposition and not Tisza -- and reading SDS would put a GOVERNING EPP PARTY into a column that everywhere else holds anti-establishment challengers, so a reader comparing 62 against Portugal's 56 would conclude Slovenia's challenger right is stronger than Chega's, which is false in every sense that matters. THE HONEST COST IS STATED HERE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: at 25 si becomes the roster's floor, below Ireland's 31 and below Bulgaria's 27, and Slovenia plainly does not have less nationalist-right politics than Ireland. THE THIRD OPTION IS REJECTED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN SILENTLY: a Slovenia-specific composite would be uncomparable by construction, which is the whole thing the convention prevents. AND ONE MEASUREMENT ARGUES THE OTHER WAY AND IS RECORDED: SNS took 2.1-2.3% and no seats, Resni.ca won five seats in March and has since FALLEN BELOW THE THRESHOLD, and Demokrati (Logar, founded January 2025) is a centre-right split from SDS at 4.8%. Slovenia's challenger right is small, fragmented and falling while its national-conservative right is the largest party in the country and in government. The dial cannot express both.

factors.name: Capacity of a Slovenian government to hold office
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §C13, §C14, and E-PLAN §E5.14. SET ABOVE WHAT THE SEAT ARITHMETIC IMPLIES, DELIBERATELY, AND THE REASON IS ARTICLE 116. The government is SDS 28 + NSi 7 + Demokrati 6 + SLS 1 + FOKUS 1 = 43 of 90, THREE SHORT of the 46 majority, governing on confidence and supply from Resni.ca's 5 and the two national-minority deputies for a working 50 -- which the cabinet confirmation vote of 49 very nearly reproduced. On seats alone that is a fragile minority government and would read in the low 40s. IT IS NOT, BECAUSE A SLOVENIAN GOVERNMENT CAN ONLY BE REMOVED BY NAMING ITS REPLACEMENT: Article 116's constructive vote requires the opposition to assemble 46 votes for ONE NAMED ALTERNATIVE, and the opposition here spans Svoboda, SD, Levica/Vesna and arguably Resni.ca. Both removals in the record (1992 and 2013) did exactly that, and both required a bloc that had already agreed on a person. This is Spain's shape, not Croatia's or Portugal's. 52 records the constructive vote; the attractor at 48 records the live fact that RESNI.CA -- the party the government depends on for its majority -- HAS FALLEN BELOW THE THRESHOLD, which is a durability fact rather than a curiosity.

factors.name: Slovenian defence spending
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §C15. THE ROSTER'S STEEPEST SINGLE TRAJECTORY -- 32 TO 70 -- AND BOTH ENDS COME FROM THE SAME PRIMARY SOURCE, which is what makes it authorable rather than a guess. NATO, Defence Investment of NATO Countries (2014-2026), 3 July 2026, Table 3: 2026e 1.61% of real GDP -> 32.2 on the roster scale (50 = 2.5%, 20 points per percentage point). SLOVENIA IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE 31 ALLIES REPORTING A CORE SHARE THAT IS BELOW 2.00%, and the gap to second-lowest is larger than the entire spread of the next six: Slovenia 1.61, then Belgium 2.00, Spain 2.00, Czechia 2.01, Slovakia 2.02, Croatia 2.03, Luxembourg 2.03. Against the roster it sits eight points below the lowest ally in the model (be and es at 40) and eight points above neutral Austria's 24. AND EVERY SLOVENIAN ROW IN EVERY TABLE CARRIES AN ASTERISK WHOSE FOOTNOTE IS THE MOST POLITICALLY EXPLICIT THING IN THE DOCUMENT: 'These are the actual figures at the moment of the inauguration of the new government of the Republic of Slovenia on 04 June 2026. The new Slovenian government is committed to a credible implementation of the commitments jointly agreed at the Hague Summit. Therefore, the current financial projections from 2026 onwards will be reviewed and reprogrammed. A credible national plan to exceed 2% of GDP on core expenditure in the current year, and reach 3.5% of GDP by 2035, will be indicated after the Ankara Summit and finalised with concrete steps in the following months.' So the attractor of 70 is 3.5%, NATO's own record of this government's own commitment, and the alliance itself has flagged the published series as stale by reason of a change of government. No other pack in the roster has that. RECORDED IN PROVENANCE AND DELIBERATELY NOT AUTHORED, because it is the strongest evidence that the trajectory is contested: after the Hague summit of 24 June 2025, LEVICA -- then a governing party -- proposed a consultative referendum on raising military spending to 3% of GDP AND IT PASSED THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY ON JANSA'S OPPOSITION VOTES, not the government's; Golob countered by proposing a SECOND CONSULTATIVE REFERENDUM ON NATO MEMBERSHIP ITSELF; BOTH WERE CANCELLED ON 19 JULY 2025 BY A VOTE OF 44 TO 7. Slovenia came within one parliamentary vote of holding a consultative referendum on NATO membership, in 2025. Table 8a supports the structural picture: infrastructure 5.47% of core spending in 2026e, among the highest in the alliance, against equipment 27.80% and personnel 46.12%, with personnel falling 6.8k (2014) to 5.9k (2026e) -- one of only a handful of allies whose headcount has shrunk.

factors.name: Slovenian willingness to underwrite collective defence
factors.provenance: E5-AEGEAN-ADRIATIC-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §C15. MID-TABLE AND RISING, and the pair of numbers on this pack is the interesting part: Slovenia is the alliance's lowest spender AND has an incoming government committed in NATO's own footnote to 3.5% by 2035. Jansa's SDS is unambiguously Atlanticist and pro-Ukraine and has been for two decades, which is why 54 sits above the Spanish and Irish 52 despite the spending; the attractor at 58 follows the commitment. NOT HIGHER, and the evidence against is dated and specific: in July 2025 the National Assembly passed a consultative referendum on capping military spending at 3% (on the then-opposition's votes), the then-Prime Minister countered with a referendum on NATO membership itself, and BOTH were cancelled 44-7 -- so the country came within one parliamentary vote of a public vote on membership fourteen months before t=0. NO COUPLING is authored into nato, for a fifth block.

factors.name: Government durability
factors.provenance: docs/research/E6-CZECHIA-BRIEF-2026-08-25.md §4. Set moderately above neutral: the ANO+SPD+Motoriste coalition won its mandatory investiture 108-91 (15 Jan 2026) and SURVIVED a no-confidence motion 84-99 against a 101-vote threshold (4 Feb 2026) with room to spare, and August 2026 polling projects a LARGER coalition seat share (~57%) than the 2025 election actually delivered (54%) -- the coalition's floor-vote record is intact and its polling position has IMPROVED, exactly the pattern this project's convention (E4's Ireland paragraph) reads as durable rather than fragile. The attractor sits below the initial for two DATED, ongoing drags this factor does not separately carry as their own dials: the Pavel/Macinka standoff (see president_government_conflict) and the EU's suspension of some subsidy reimbursements pending clarification of Babis's blind-trust arrangement (see babis-conflict-of-interest-episode). Set BELOW Italy's 68/58 (it.json) because Czechia's overall cabinet-turnover rate (16 transitions/33.7y = 0.475/yr) is itself higher than Italy's Second Republic reputation would suggest, even though sitting-government floor-vote LOSSES are rare (1/33.7y, see government-collapse).

factors.name: EU/NATO alignment posture
factors.provenance: docs/research/E6-CZECHIA-BRIEF-2026-08-25.md §6.1. NAMED DELIBERATELY DIFFERENTLY FROM european_security_integration, the roster's neutral-polity factor -- Czechia is a full NATO member with no constitutional neutrality clause, so this dial tracks COMMITMENT STRENGTH within the alliance, not whether to join one. Set well below neutral: the 2026 defence budget (~155bn CZK, ~1.7% of GDP) passed 104-87 BELOW NATO's 2% target, with PM Babis stating the government is 'certainly not' on a path to raise it and President Pavel publicly rebuking the Chamber over it; the number of countries funding the Czech-led Ukraine ammunition initiative has roughly HALVED, ~18 to 9, since Babis returned to office; and Babis publicly rejected further Czech aid to Ukraine and Czech guarantees for EU loans to Ukraine (13 December 2025). Press framing of this as V4/Orban-Fico realignment is NOTED but not adopted as a modelled fact -- only the independently sourced budget and funder-count figures set the level. NO COUPLING into nato's aggregate dials this block, per programme rule.

factors.name: President-government institutional conflict
factors.provenance: docs/research/E6-CZECHIA-BRIEF-2026-08-25.md §6.2. THE PACK'S CENTRAL, GENUINELY NOVEL DIAL -- see the notes field for why no earlier roster pack carries this mechanism. Set elevated at t=0 (the standoff was still active as of the most recent source, March 2026) with the attractor set below the initial: the specific Turek disputes are dated flashpoints plausibly cooling even if the underlying structural asymmetry -- a popularly elected president who personally defeated the sitting PM in 2023 -- persists for the whole term. This factor feeds president-refuses-appointment below; it does NOT feed the government-falls transition, because Pavel's veto power over individual ministers is narrower than, and constitutionally separate from, the Chamber's own no-confidence mechanism.

factors.name: Government durability
factors.provenance: docs/research/E6-SLOVAKIA-BRIEF-2026-08-25.md §3-4. Set just above neutral: the coalition has been TESTED and held every time -- it survived an ~8-week minority period (24 Jan-19 Mar 2025) without a lost vote, then won a legislated, mechanically triggered confidence vote 78-54 (18 June 2026), a comfortable 24-vote margin once actually forced. The attractor sits below the initial for the structural fragility texture the initial does not carry alone: SNS lost its official parliamentary-group status in October 2024 (three MPs broke away), two more MPs were expelled from Hlas in January 2025, and SNS itself now polls at 4% -- BELOW its own 5% survival threshold. On the historical base rate, 3 of 11 completed PM terms since 1993 ended in a lost floor vote (~27%) and a further 2 in a same-coalition resignation (~18%), against 6 of 11 (~55%) ending in an ordinary election loss.

factors.name: Judicial independence and rule-of-law posture
factors.provenance: docs/research/E6-SLOVAKIA-BRIEF-2026-08-25.md §5. See the notes field for why this is set explicitly below a comparable Czech reading. Set low and drifting lower: the 2024 fast-tracked criminal-code reform cut corruption/economic-crime sentences, shortened limitations periods and dissolved the Special Prosecutor's Office (European Parliament passed a concern resolution, January 2024; a European Commission rule-of-law chapter dated 17 July 2026 exists, not read in depth this block); the public broadcaster RTVS was abolished and replaced by STVR under leadership effectively controlled by the culture minister/parliamentary majority; Fico has labelled major outlets 'enemy media' and sued journalists; the PM has been criticised for 'monitoring' judges who ruled against allies.

factors.name: Russia-Ukraine alignment posture
factors.provenance: docs/research/E6-SLOVAKIA-BRIEF-2026-08-25.md §6.1. Set below neutral but WITH ELEVATED NOISE AND FAST REVERSION rather than pinned low, because the record is genuinely oscillating rather than fixed: Fico (with Orban) blocked the EU's 18th sanctions package and vetoed opening Ukraine's EU accession talks in mid-2025, then reconciled with Zelensky at a September 2025 Uzhhorod meeting and said he would support Ukraine's EU accession (leaving Hungary the sole holdout) -- then the Druzhba pipeline dispute recurred in early 2026 (transit disrupted 27 Jan-23 Apr after Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, with Fico linking a EUR90bn Ukraine funding package and a 20th sanctions package to restoring transit). Modelled as a recurring, RESOLVABLE flare tied to concrete transactional asks, not a fixed posture -- see druzhba-linkage-flare.

factors.name: Public approval of the sitting President
factors.provenance: Noverna/Politis poll, 16 March 2026, n=1,020: approve 28%, disapprove 56% -- a FURTHER deterioration from the September 2025 reading of 40% positive / 56% negative (the disapprove side held flat; the erosion is on the approve side). Worst-rated policy area is water management at ~69% negative; only digital transformation reads net-positive (46/38). Attractor set above the initial reading rather than at it: Christodoulides is 3 years into a 5-year first term with no removal mechanism before February 2028 and both invoked-zero-times removal clauses (high treason, moral turpitude) require a 75%-House-approved prosecution motion, so the office has no channel for the number to keep falling toward -- it either recovers some ground into the run-up to the 2028 election (the modal pattern for an incumbent seeking one more term) or the President does not stand again, which the factor does not need to distinguish.

factors.name: House of Representatives fragmentation
factors.provenance: 24 May 2026 election: the largest party (DISY) holds 17 of 56 elected seats (30.4%), six parties cleared the 3.6% threshold, EDEK/DIPA/the Ecologists (11 seats combined after 2021) lost their ENTIRE representation, and ELAM DOUBLED its seats to become the third-largest party. President and House are elected on separate tracks and Cyprus's last two presidents (2023, and Christodoulides was the first to do so) have won without either major party's backing, so governing requires shifting issue-by-issue majorities across a House with no party above a third of seats. High and structural rather than a crisis reading -- this is the system's ordinary operating point, not a spike.

factors.name: Momentum toward a Cyprus-problem settlement
factors.provenance: Elevated from a near-zero historical baseline by ONE genuine structural break: Tufan Erhurman's 62.8%-35.8% landslide over pro-partition incumbent Ersin Tatar in the 19 October 2025 Northern Cypriot presidential election, and UN Secretary-General Guterres's 27-29 July 2026 visit -- his FIRST since Ban Ki-moon in 2010 -- calling 2026 a 'critical year' and announcing a new 5+1 preparatory process. Attractor set BELOW the elevated initial value rather than above it, on the reference class this factor's own reversion argues against optimism outrunning: four serious negotiating attempts over 52 years (2004 Annan, 2008-12 Christofias-Talat, 2017 Crans-Montana, this 2026 process), ZERO ratified settlements, and no full-format conference is even scheduled as of this pack's t=0 -- only preparatory diplomacy. Cypriot public reporting (Neos Kosmos, July 2026) shows scepticism toward the renewed push, and Turkey retains the practical veto over what Erhurman can actually concede.

factors.name: Great Sea Interconnector progress
factors.provenance: A EUR1.9bn subsea electricity cable (Cyprus 63%/~EUR786m, Greece 37%/~EUR460m, EU committing EUR657m) intended to end Cyprus's total electrical isolation from the EU grid. Originally due online 2024, now delayed past 2029-2030. Turkey disputes the underlying EEZ claims the route depends on, forced 2024 survey delays with naval deployments, is pursuing a rival cable to Northern Cyprus (rejected by the European TSO network, 15 April 2026), and is advancing an expansive 'Blue Homeland' maritime doctrine toward domestic law (parliamentary consideration pushed to October 2026). Greece and Cyprus asked the EIB in April 2026 to reassess viability; as of 19 August 2026 'no conclusion has been reached on whether financing will be considered' (Euronews). Initial set above the attractor on real committed financing (the EU's EUR657m is not contingent on the EIB review); attractor below it on the stated multi-year delay and the unresolved Turkish obstruction this factor is named for tracking.

factors.name: Government durability
factors.provenance: 7 individuals across 8 PM stints since the 1974 republic (Fenech Adami served twice), average tenure ~6.5-6.9 years, and NO PM has EVER been removed by a floor no-confidence vote in that ~52-year record -- every exit is an election loss or voluntary resignation (Mintoff 1984, Muscat 2020). Rated near the roster's most durable pole, on the same register as Ireland's fixed-term stability, but by a DIFFERENT mechanism: Malta's two-corrective-mechanism electoral system (Article 52 proportionality correction, Article 52A gender correction) is specifically engineered to guarantee the top vote-getter a working single-party majority, so Malta has never once needed coalition formation, unlike most of this roster's parliamentary packs.

factors.name: European security-integration posture
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, per the C4.0b convention, following at/ch/ie's shared factor name for cross-polity comparability -- AND MALTA IS A FOURTH DIFFERENT REFERENT UNDER THE SAME NAME (B1 Section 4's lesson, a fourth time). Set LOWEST of the four modelled neutrals: Malta is the SOLE EU member of 27 outside PESCO, opted out at PESCO's 2017 launch citing constitutional-neutrality concerns and reaffirming 'no reason to change the status quo' as of 2026 reporting; it is also EXCLUDED from the EU's SAFE defence-funding programme, unlike Austria, Ireland and Cyprus. Priced as a POLICY-DRIFT/POSTURE dial, deliberately NOT the constitutional text itself: defence spending has nearly doubled over a decade (~EUR42m 2014 to ~EUR100m projected 2026, European Parliament data), driven by stated subsea-cable/cyber-infrastructure concerns rather than territorial defence or alliance-integration appetite, which is what keeps the initial reading low rather than static at zero.

factors.name: Corruption and rule-of-law pressure
factors.provenance: A 2021 public inquiry into the October 2017 assassination of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia found the Maltese STATE ITSELF bore responsibility, citing a state-created 'atmosphere of impunity.' Alleged mastermind Yorgen Fenech's jury trial began 1 July 2026 and was still underway as of 24 August 2026 (day 43+), with a verdict reportedly expected imminently -- the pack's t=0 sits inside this trial's own final stretch. Separately, international press-freedom bodies (RSF, IPI, PEN International, ECPMF) have repeatedly criticized the government for inaction on the inquiry's own media-reform recommendations, pressure renewed as recently as April 2026. The EU's 29 April 2025 ECJ ruling striking down Malta's 'golden passport' citizenship-by-investment scheme (Malta was the LAST EU state running one, after Cyprus 2020 and Bulgaria 2022 scrapped theirs) is treated as a SETTLED t=0 condition, not a live driver of this factor -- it is already resolved, only its fiscal-replacement question remains open and is not separately modelled here.

factors.name: Capacity to legislate and survive the parliamentary party
factors.provenance: E7-CANADA-BRIEF §1: a Liberal majority (171/343 at t=0, 174 when it was assembled) reached 2026-04-13, five months before t=0, via five floor-crossings plus a clean sweep of three by-elections -- the first time a Canadian PM has reached a majority this way rather than at a general election. August 2026 polling shows a consistent double-digit Liberal lead across pollsters (Liaison Strategies 9-13pts; Leger 12pts; Research Co. 20pts), with one tracker (Liaison Strategies) reporting Carney approval near 60%. Initial 72 carries this consolidation-and-polling premium, higher than uk.json's Burnham-arrival initial of 68 because the polling margin is larger and the majority itself is newly proven rather than merely inherited; the attractor at 60 is the same 'honeymoon decaying toward a normal mid-term government' shape uk.json uses, not a claim that today's lead is a fixed point three years from the first scheduled election. NG1d: the INITIAL of 72 was priced on the 174/343 reading and has NOT been re-derived against 171-with-6-vacant. It is left where it is deliberately rather than nudged: a durability dial is priced from a reference class plus judgement, and moving it to match a seat count nobody re-argued would be the silent retune the calibration doctrine forbids. What has changed is the ARGUMENT behind it — a working majority of four is thinner than a nominal majority of two — and commons-standings' ifChanged already names this dial as in the blast radius. Re-deriving it is a named successor, not this block's business.

factors.name: State of the US-Canada trade relationship
factors.provenance: ANALYST-ASSESSED at the epoch, labelled as such per uk.json's atlanticism/defence_effort convention -- no index of 'US-Canada relationship quality' was fetched, because none exists to fetch. E7-CANADA-BRIEF §3: talks collapsed 2026-08-22, the US applied 50% tariffs on ~5.5% of Canadian exports, and Canadian retaliation is scheduled for 2026-09-08 (authored separately as ca.retaliatory-tariffs-implemented so this factor's initial value is not double-counting the same fact against that event's own impulse). Initial 28 reads as a serious, bilateral rupture between treaty allies rather than a full diplomatic breakdown -- CUSMA-compliant goods retain exemptions and no military or alliance dimension is in play. The attractor at 45 assumes a partial, slow recovery over the horizon (trade disputes between economically interdependent neighbours have historically de-escalated, e.g. the pre-collapse CUSMA-compliance exemptions this same dispute already carried) without asserting a full return to a neutral relationship.

The Mecca trilateral pact (Aug 2026) adds a Gulf/Turkey channel with the OPPOSITE sign, which is why 60 and not 70. Crisis states pull it up: the off-ramp engages when the phone rings.
