C3 §1.3: a contest resolved by the winning faction taking overt control

states.name: Labour majority government
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): Burnham's Labour government, 404 seats, majority ~159. EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.1.

states.name: Conservative-led majority government
states.provenance: A single-party or Conservative-led majority after a general election. Reachable only through uk.election-outcome.

states.name: Reform-led majority government
states.provenance: Reform UK forming a government with a Commons majority. The brief's §2.1 polling puts this within reach on a uniform swing; FPTP makes the seat translation the dominant uncertainty, which is why the election transition carries a large hung-parliament branch rather than reading the vote share off directly.

states.name: Hung parliament
states.provenance: No single party with a Commons majority — minority government or confidence-and-supply. 2010 and 2017 are the post-war referents; a four-way ~25/25/20/11 vote split makes it a live outcome rather than a tail.

destinations.provenance: Incumbency plus a 159-seat cushion, discounted by the insurgent's strength. Governed by reference class uk.mid-term-exit's sibling judgement about era: the weights let a Labour government that has held its durability re-win, and one that has not, lose.

EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.1: Reform led or tied the August 2026 average. The heaviest factor weight in the pack, because this destination is the one the modelled nationalist trajectory is actually about.
The Conservatives at ~20% are third; the negative weight encodes that Reform's strength comes substantially at their expense rather than independently.

The seat-translation branch. With four parties above 10% a hung parliament is the modal FPTP outcome of a fragmented vote, and it carries no factor weight because it is driven by the geography of the split rather than by any modelled quantity — an honest flat weight rather than a fabricated dependence.

states.name: CDU/CSU-SPD coalition
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): the Merz government formed after the 2025-02-23 snap election, CDU/CSU 208 seats. EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.2.

states.name: CDU/CSU-led coalition without the SPD
states.provenance: A CDU/CSU-led majority with the Greens and/or FDP instead of the SPD. Reachable only through de.election-outcome.

states.name: Coalition including the AfD
states.provenance: A federal government in which the AfD participates. Requires breaking the cross-party commitment the CDU has restated explicitly ('the CDU won't be destroyed by the far right'), so it is a formation discontinuity with no post-war precedent — which is why its weight is driven hardest by nationalist_strength and why its SEVERITY is nevertheless equal to the other majority configurations (see presentation).

states.name: Minority government
states.provenance: A chancellor elected without a Bundestag majority, governing issue by issue. Rare federally but the standing alternative when the firewall removes coalition options.

states.name: Prolonged government-formation crisis
states.provenance: No government formed within the normal window; the outgoing cabinet continues in a caretaker capacity. 2017 is the referent — 171 days, the post-war record, after the Jamaica talks collapsed.

destinations.provenance: The modal outcome if the AfD's rise stalls: CDU/CSU leads with a partner other than the SPD. Discounted as nationalist_strength rises, because AfD seats are the arithmetic that removes this option.
Continuation of the t=0 configuration. Rewarded by durability, discounted by the insurgent's strength for the same arithmetic reason as centre-right.

The heaviest factor weight in the pack. The base weight is deliberately low — no post-war precedent, and an explicit standing commitment against it — while the factor weight is the largest, so the branch is driven by the modelled AfD trajectory rather than by an authored prior. Governed by reference class de.coalition-formation.

The firewall's arithmetic consequence: excluding a party polling 27% while refusing its participation leaves the remaining parties needing a majority from a shrinking remainder, and a minority chancellor is one of the two ways that resolves.
The other way it resolves: no government at all within the normal window. Governed by reference class de.coalition-formation, which declares why the adopted rate is double the post-war base rate.

states.name: Hung Assembly, government by Article 49.3
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): the condition since the June 2024 dissolution. A centrist president, no Assembly majority, a prime minister governing by 49.3 and surviving censure. EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.3.

states.name: Centrist or centre-right presidency with an Assembly majority
states.provenance: The Fifth Republic's designed configuration — the fait majoritaire, where the presidential election is followed weeks later by a legislative election that delivers the winner a majority.

states.name: Nationalist presidency with an Assembly majority
states.provenance: An RN president whose June legislative election delivers a working majority. Reachable only through fr.presidential-outcome. The brief's §2.3 polling makes this the single highest-consequence branch in the four D8 packs.

states.name: Left presidency with an Assembly majority
states.provenance: The mirror branch. Priced low but not at zero: the 2024 legislative election was won by the left-wing NFP alliance on seats, so the coalition exists even where the presidential polling is weak.

states.name: Cohabitation
states.provenance: President and Assembly majority from opposing blocs, with the prime minister drawn from the Assembly. Three post-war episodes (1986, 1993, 1997), all of which ran their full term — which is why its severity sits below the hung Assembly rather than above it: cohabitation is a functioning if constrained configuration, whereas a hung Assembly is not.

states.name: Caretaker crisis
states.provenance: A government censured or resigned with no successor able to command the Assembly. The nearest realised approach is the sequence of 2024-25 prime ministerial collapses; the state is the tail beyond them.

destinations.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.3: Bardella leads the first round at 32% and wins the run-off in every scenario Odoxa tested. Governed by reference class fr.presidential-outcome, which declares why a run-off lead is NOT converted into a run-off probability one-for-one.

A president elected without the legislative election delivering a majority. Weighted upward by nationalist strength because the RN's presidential reach currently exceeds its legislative reach — its 2024 first-round alliance share converted into far fewer seats than its votes implied, which is exactly the configuration that produces cohabitation.

The republican-front branch: a centrist or centre-right candidate consolidating the anti-RN vote in the run-off, as in 2002, 2017 and 2022. Discounted hard as nationalist_strength rises, which is the mechanism the front depends on weakening.

The status quo persists: a president without an Assembly majority and without a hostile one either. Flat-weighted — this branch is about the legislative election's fragmentation rather than about any modelled quantity, and a fabricated dependence would be worse than an honest constant.
Priced low against the presidential polling but non-zero on the 2024 legislative precedent.
An election that resolves nothing. Deliberately a tail: elections in the Fifth Republic have always produced a government eventually, and the 2024-25 sequence produced four.

transitions.name: Presidential election and the legislative election that follows it

states.name: Tido minority government
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): the Kristersson government — M, KD and L in cabinet, Sweden Democrats supplying confidence and supply from outside under the Tido Agreement. EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.4.

states.name: Social Democrat-led government
states.provenance: A Social Democrat-led government, almost certainly a minority one on Left/Centre/Green support — the standard Swedish configuration, held for most of the post-war period. The red-green bloc leads the polls at 52-55% with the Social Democrats the largest single party at ~33%.

states.name: Right-bloc majority government
states.provenance: The right bloc with an outright Riksdag majority, with or without SD in cabinet. Priced low: outright majorities are rare but NOT unknown -- the Reinfeldt Alliance held 178 of 349 in 2006-2010 (M 97 + C 29 + FP 28 + KD 24). (NG1b VERIFIED 2026-08-26: this read 'no Swedish government has commanded a single-party or tight-bloc majority since 1979', which is false. Source: historik.val.se 2006 final result.)

states.name: Government-formation crisis
states.provenance: No government formed within the normal window after an inconclusive election. 2018 is the referent and it is recent and severe: 134 days, TWO failed prime-ministerial votes on Speaker's proposals (Kristersson 2018-11-14, rejected 154-195; Lofven 2018-12-14, rejected), the longest formation in Swedish history. (NG1b VERIFIED 2026-08-26: this read 'four failed'. The Riksdag's own protocols record three Speaker's proposals, the third of which -- Lofven, 2019-01-18 -- PASSED 115/153/77 under negative parliamentarism, a proposal falling only if 175+ vote no. The separate 2018-09-25 ballot was the post-election retention vote on the sitting PM, a different instrument. 'Four failed' is also structurally impossible: the Regeringsformen allows four attempts and four failures MANDATE an extraordinary election within three months, which Sweden did not hold. Source: riksdagen.se protocol 2018/19:39.)

destinations.provenance: EUROPEAN-MEMBERS-BRIEF §2.4: the red-green bloc leads at 52-55% against the governing bloc's 42-46%, with the Social Democrats the largest single party at ~33%. Governed by reference class se.election-outcome, which declares why a bloc polling lead three weeks out is not converted one-for-one.

Continuation of the t=0 arrangement. Swedish bloc polling has historically tightened into election day, and the 2022 election was won by this bloc by a single-seat margin against polls that had it behind.

The 2018 branch. Flat-weighted because formation failure in Sweden turns on the arithmetic of a fragmented eight-party Riksdag and the blocs' mutual vetoes, not on either bloc's strength — 2018's crisis followed an election in which the two blocs finished within 0.4 points of each other. Governed by reference class se.election-outcome.

Deliberately a tail: outright majorities are rare -- the last was the Reinfeldt Alliance's 178 of 349 in 2006-2010, not 1979 as this string previously claimed (NG1b VERIFIED 2026-08-26, historik.val.se) -- and the branch exists so the configuration is expressible rather than because it is likely.

states.name: Tusk-led KO-anchored coalition
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): KO+PSL+Poland 2050+Lewica, 240-243/460 seats. EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §1/§3.

states.name: PiS/Konfederacja-anchored government
states.provenance: A PiS-led or PiS+Konfederacja-anchored coalition takes office post-election. Does not require the four fragmented right lists to formally unify (they are openly hostile per EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §5) — only that a right-anchored coalition forms, which their combined ~53.4% vote intention makes the modal single outcome even under fragmentation.

states.name: Government-formation crisis
states.provenance: No governing coalition assembled within the normal post-election window. Elevated relative to Sweden's equivalent tail: the 23 Aug 2026 seat projection has SIX lists clearing the threshold (KO, PiS, Konfederacja, Konfederacja Korony Polskiej, Lewica, Rozwoj Plus) against Sweden's eight-party but two-bloc system.

destinations.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §3/§5: the incumbent coalition polls only 42.8% of seats today against a fragmented-but-larger combined right vote (~53.4%). Modal outcome given the polling deficit, though translating fragmented vote share into a governing coalition is itself uncertain — see the formation-crisis branch.

Continuation, whether or not PSL/Poland 2050 individually clear the 5% threshold (both currently sub-threshold and structurally dependent on a joint KO-anchored list, per EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §3). 14+ months remain to the scheduled election from this pack's epoch; incumbency retains real recovery capacity.

Flat-weighted, matching se.json's equivalent branch: formation difficulty here turns on the arithmetic of six lists clearing threshold, not on either bloc's strength. Set higher than Sweden's 15 given Poland's more fragmented field (six lists vs. Sweden's two-bloc eight-party system).

states.name: Orpo-led NCP-anchored coalition
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): NCP+Finns Party+RKP+KD, 108/200 seats. EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §1.

states.name: Social Democrat-led government
states.provenance: SDP has led every located 2026 poll by 6-9 points (23-24% vs NCP's 16.5-18.3%) since at least June 2026. EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §3.

states.name: Government-formation delay
states.provenance: A thin tail, priced well below Sweden's equivalent (2018's 134-day crisis) or Poland's: the research did not surface a comparable Finnish formation-crisis precedent, and Finland's post-election coalition talks have historically resolved within weeks even across an eight-party Eduskunta.

destinations.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §3: SDP's consistent 6-9 point 2026 polling lead over the NCP-anchored coalition.

Continuation. A stronger PS partially offsets NCP's own weak polling within the incumbent coalition -- the distinctive Finnish dynamic where the nationalist-right partner's strength supports rather than threatens the sitting government, per this pack's own nationalist_strength provenance.
Flat-weighted and thin, below Sweden's 15 and well below Poland's 20 -- see the state's own provenance.

states.name: Michal-led Reform/Eesti 200 coalition
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): Reform+Eesti 200, 50/101 seats after two Aug 2026 defections. EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §1/§3.

states.name: Isamaa-anchored government
states.provenance: Isamaa leads all located 2026 polling (22.3-25.2%) despite being in opposition. Represents any Isamaa-anchored coalition, not a specific partner combination.

states.name: Government-formation crisis
states.provenance: Estonia's party system is now SIX-way fragmented at material polling levels (Isamaa, Keskerakond, SDE, EKRE, Reform, Parempoolsed) -- more fragmented than Poland's six-list Sejm by vote-share dispersion, not just list count -- so priced at the same elevated level as Poland's equivalent tail rather than Finland's thin one.

destinations.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §3/§5: the governing parties have collapsed to a combined ~14% (Reform 12.4-13.0%, Eesti 200 1.6%) against Isamaa's outright lead.
Set below Finland/Poland's equivalent continuation weight: this is the only E1 pack whose government has already lost its floor majority before any election, six months out from the 2027-03 deadline.
Flat-weighted and the highest formation-crisis weight of the five E1 packs, matching the state's own provenance on Estonia's six-way fragmentation.

states.name: Kulbergs caretaker government
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): United List+National Alliance+New Unity+ZZS, explicitly caretaker ahead of the Oct 2026 election. EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §1/§3.

states.name: Post-election government
states.provenance: A new governing coalition forms after the 3 Oct 2026 election. Latvia's ten-party fragmentation makes naming a specific successor bloc unsupportable from current evidence -- this state represents ANY coalition that successfully forms, whatever its composition, deliberately not attributed to a named bloc the way Estonia's or Finland's alternation states are.

states.name: Government-formation crisis
states.provenance: Ten parties cluster near or below the 5% threshold, including a sitting coalition partner currently below it -- the single most fragmented party system of the five E1 packs by this measure, and the only one where the outgoing government has already been explicitly labelled a caretaker rather than merely weakened.

destinations.provenance: The modal outcome: SOME coalition forms, even from a fragmented field -- Latvia has never gone past a normal post-election window without eventually seating a government, unlike the more open-ended formation-crisis tail.

Continuation of the caretaker arrangement past the election is possible but unusual -- caretaker governments are, by construction, transitional rather than durable configurations, hence the lowest continuation weight of any E1 pack.

Matches Estonia's elevated tail (30): ten parties near threshold, a demonstrated 2026 precedent of a single hybrid incident felling a government inside a week, and no clear governing bloc emerging from current polling.

states.name: LSDP-anchored coalition
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): LSDP+LVZS+DSVL, 75/141 seats, PM Sinkevicius since 30 Jun 2026. Tracks the CONFIGURATION -- this state persists across an internal PM change (as it already has twice) provided the same bloc governs. EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §1/§3.

states.name: TS-LKD-anchored government
states.provenance: TS-LKD, the sole major opposition party, polls 22.9% against the three-party governing coalition's combined ~28-29% -- close enough that alternation is a genuine, not dominant, possibility at the 2028 election.

states.name: Government-formation crisis
states.provenance: Priced at the same elevated level as Poland's equivalent tail (20): both packs' recent history shows real coalition fragility, though Lithuania's manifests as within-bloc PM churn rather than outright formation failure so far.

destinations.provenance: EASTERN-FLANK-BRIEF §3: TS-LKD's 22.9% against the coalition's combined ~28-29% -- a genuinely close race, not a clear lean either way, roughly two years out from the scheduled election.
Set equal to the alternation weight, reflecting the close current polling -- distinct from Estonia/Finland's clearer leans.
Flat-weighted, matching Poland's equivalent tail.

states.name: Single-party constitutional supermajority
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): Tisza alone on 141 of 199 seats, 8 above the 133-seat constitutional threshold. The ONLY supermajority state in the roster, and the reason this pack's machine is not shaped like the others: Hungary's governing question is not whether a coalition holds but whether the amendment power does. E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.1.

states.name: Governing majority without the amendment power
states.provenance: A government that holds a working majority but has fallen below the 133-seat two-thirds threshold -- the configuration eight defections would produce without endangering the government itself. Also the modal shape of an ordinary Hungarian government: every government from 1990 to 2010 was one.

states.name: Multi-party coalition government
states.provenance: A coalition rather than a single-party government -- the configuration in which all three of Hungary's historical mid-term PM departures occurred (Antall 1993, Medgyessy 2004, Gyurcsany 2009 were all coalition-era). Reachable through an election, not from the t=0 state directly.

destinations.provenance: The modal Hungarian outcome across the whole post-1990 record: a governing majority without the two-thirds. Flat-weighted deliberately -- which bloc wins is not modelled by this pack, only the CONFIGURATION the election produces, and the configuration's distribution is a property of the electoral system rather than of either bloc's strength.

A renewed two-thirds. Not a tail in Hungary the way an outright majority is a tail in Sweden: the mixed-member majoritarian system has delivered a constitutional supermajority in four of the last five elections (Fidesz 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022; Tisza 2026), which is the fact that makes this branch substantial rather than exceptional.
A return to the coalition politics of 1990-2010. Flat-weighted for the same reason as the majority branch.

states.name: Right-anchored coalition government
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): FdI + Lega + Forza Italia + Noi Moderati, 237/400 and 119/205. E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.2.

states.name: Centre-left coalition government
states.provenance: A PD-anchored coalition. The blocs are near-tied in current polling (~46.8% vs ~45.5%), which is what makes this a real branch rather than a tail.

states.name: Technocratic or national-unity government
states.provenance: The distinctively Italian configuration and the reason this pack's machine differs from every other in the roster: a non-partisan cabinet installed by the President when the chamber cannot produce a political majority. Four in the Second Republic alone -- Ciampi 1993, Dini 1995, Monti 2011, Draghi 2021 -- so it is a standing feature of the constitutional order, not an emergency. Reachable from any state.

destinations.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.2/§5: the blocs are near-tied, and the base weight is deliberately NOT read off FdI's stable 27%. Italy elects 147 of 400 deputies by first-past-the-post, where coalition COMPOSITION matters more than vote share, and Futuro Nazionale (6.5%) has said it will contest 2027 independently with Salvini ruling out any alliance -- a classic spoiler that could cost the centre-right dozens of plurality seats while winning none itself. A model pricing this branch off FdI's own polling would systematically overstate it; the brief says so explicitly and this weight is set below the naive read for that reason.
A PD-anchored government, with the fragmented right's FPTP disadvantage as the mechanism rather than a centre-left polling lead, which does not exist.

Flat-weighted, and the highest such branch in the roster at 20: four Second-Republic instances in 32 years is a base rate of roughly one per two elections. Flat because a technocratic government follows from the CHAMBER's inability to produce a majority, not from either bloc's strength.

states.name: PSOE-led minority government
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): PSOE+Sumar on 147 of 350, governing vote by vote since Junts broke on 27 October 2025. E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.3.

states.name: PP-anchored government
states.provenance: A PP government, with or without Vox in cabinet. Current polling gives PP 32.5% (128 seats) and PP+Vox 200-206 seats post-Ceuta -- so this is the modal outcome of the 2027 election, not a tail.

states.name: Government-formation crisis
states.provenance: No government invested within the constitutional window. Spain has a recent and severe precedent: the 2015-2016 impasse ran 315 days across two elections with no government formed, the longest in Spanish democratic history.

destinations.provenance: E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.3: PP 32.5% to PSOE's 26.6%, and PP+Vox at 200-206 seats in post-Ceuta polling against a 176 threshold. The modal branch. Gated on legislative_capacity as well as Vox's strength, because a fourth budget-less year is the government's most legible failure.

Continuation. Not a tail despite the polling deficit: Spanish government formation turns on whether the PP can assemble 176 WITH Vox and the regionalists, and the 2023 election is the direct counter-example -- the PP won the most seats and could not form a government.

Flat-weighted, matching the roster convention that formation failure turns on chamber arithmetic rather than either bloc's strength. Set at 20 rather than Sweden's 15 on the strength of the 2015-2016 precedent and the fact that Spanish investiture requires an absolute majority on the first ballot.

states.name: Minority cabinet without confidence-and-supply
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): D66 + VVD + CDA on 66 of 150, no confidence-and-supply agreement -- the first such cabinet since 1918. E2-MEMBERS-BRIEF §1.4.

states.name: Majority coalition cabinet
states.provenance: The ordinary Dutch configuration: a coalition holding more than 75 of 150 seats with a negotiated agreement. Every Dutch cabinet from 1918 to 2025 except the current one.

states.name: Demissionary (caretaker) cabinet
states.provenance: THE STATE THIS PACK EXISTS TO MODEL. When a Dutch cabinet falls it does not vanish -- it becomes demissionary and governs with restricted authority until a new one is formed. Sixteen cabinets have fallen prematurely since 1945. Critically, entering this state does NOT imply a change of prime minister: Rutte survived three collapses and Balkenende three. THE DWELL IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS ADDED AFTER MEASURING (C4.7 §5's rule: dwell resolution beats waiting for a factor, for a short state). Without it this state's ONLY exit is the scheduled general election, so a cabinet collapsing in late 2026 would sit demissionary until May 2030 -- about 41 months, against a real Dutch mechanism of collapse then early election then formation. Sized from the record the brief carries: 4.7 months from collapse to poll in 2023 and 4.9 in 2025, plus a formation that took 117 days in 2026 and has run longer (the 2021-22 formation took 299 days). 6-13 months brackets that sequence.

destinations.provenance: A collapse has one destination by construction: a fallen Dutch cabinet becomes demissionary and stays so until a new one is formed. Single-destination and flat-weighted -- the probability lives entirely in the triggering event's hazard, not here.

transitions.name: The cabinet falls and becomes demissionary

destinations.provenance: The ordinary Dutch outcome: a negotiated coalition with a Tweede Kamer majority. Flat-weighted, because which parties compose it is not modelled by this pack and the CONFIGURATION's distribution is a property of a seventeen-party chamber rather than of any party's strength.

Deliberately substantial rather than a tail, and this is a judgement worth stating: minority cabinets were vanishingly rare in Dutch history until 2026, but the chamber that produces them -- seventeen parties, the largest holding 26 seats, a fragmenting nationalist right -- is the chamber that will still exist in 2030. Weighting this branch at a Sweden-style 5% would price the 1990s party system.

transitions.name: A new cabinet is formed after an election

states.name: Coalition government
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): the five-party Arizona coalition, 80/150. Belgium has essentially only ever had coalition governments -- no single party has approached a majority in the modern era -- so this state is the ordinary condition rather than one configuration among several. E3-BENELUX-BRIEF §B1.

states.name: Caretaker government during formation
states.provenance: BELGIUM'S CHARACTERISTIC STATE, and the reason this pack's machine is shaped the way it is. When a Belgian government falls or an election produces no coalition, the outgoing cabinet continues in caretaker capacity -- for 541 days in 2010-11 (the federal record), 494 in 2019-20, 284 in 2007-08, 239 in 2024-25. The dwell below is sized from that record rather than from a general prior.

destinations.provenance: Single-destination by construction: a Belgian election or government collapse opens a formation period with the outgoing cabinet in caretaker capacity. The probability lives in the triggering events' hazards, not here.

transitions.name: Election or collapse opens a formation

destinations.provenance: Also single-destination: every Belgian formation has eventually produced a coalition, including the 541-day one. What varies is how long it takes, which the caretaker state's dwell carries, not which state it reaches.

states.name: CSV-led coalition
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): CSV+DP, 35/60, under Luc Frieden. THE MODAL LUXEMBOURG CONFIGURATION BY A LONG MARGIN -- the CSV has held the premiership for 66.6 of the 81.6 post-war years, 81.6%, broken only by Thorn (1974-79) and Bettel (2013-23). E3-BENELUX-BRIEF §L1.

states.name: Coalition without the CSV
states.provenance: The Bettel configuration of 2013-2023 and the Thorn one of 1974-79: a coalition assembled to exclude the largest party. Its most recent instance is instructive -- in 2013 the CSV won the snap election and was excluded anyway.

destinations.provenance: The CSV has led 81.6% of post-war governments. Weighted at 70 rather than 82 because its own polling has fallen 7.4 points since 2023 into a three-way bunch with the DP and LSAP, and because 2013 is the direct counter-example of a CSV plurality that did not govern.

Flat-weighted: which parties assemble the alternative is not modelled, and the CSV's exclusion in 2013 turned on coalition arithmetic among the other parties rather than on any measured quantity this pack carries.

states.name: Three-party coalition
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): OVP+SPO+NEOS, 110/183. The first three-party government since 1949. E3-NEUTRALS-BRIEF §A1.

states.name: Two-party coalition
states.provenance: The ordinary Austrian configuration for most of the Second Republic -- OVP-SPO grand coalitions and OVP-FPO or SPO-FPO pairings alike. Reachable after an election.

states.name: FPO-led government
states.provenance: The FPO won the 2024 election and did not take office: coalition talks under Kickl collapsed in February 2025 over the OVP's terms, not over arithmetic. At 37.6% and leading every 2026 poll it is a real branch, and the pack prices the CONFIGURATION rather than predicting the outcome.

states.name: Caretaker or expert government
states.provenance: A non-partisan or interim cabinet between governments -- the Schallenberg configuration of January-March 2025, and the Bierlein expert government of 2019-20 after the Ibiza affair. Austria reaches this state readily and leaves it within months.

destinations.provenance: The modal Austrian configuration across the Second Republic. Flat-weighted: which two parties pair is not modelled here, and the configuration's distribution is a property of the party system rather than of any bloc's strength.

Gated on FPO strength, which is what distinguishes this branch from the others. Set below the two-party weight despite the FPO's polling lead because 2024 is the direct counter-example: winning the election was not sufficient to take office.

Continuation of the t=0 configuration, or another three-party arrangement. Historically rare -- one instance since 1949 -- but the current one exists precisely because a two-party majority could not be assembled, and the arithmetic that produced it has not changed.

Formation failure. Flat-weighted, and lower than the roster's usual formation-crisis tail because Austria resolves these quickly through an interim chancellor rather than sitting in a prolonged vacancy -- see the state's own dwell.
A caretaker period ends when a coalition is assembled; the two-party form is the modal result.
The 2025 outcome -- the configuration that ended the last caretaker period, and the reason this branch is weighted well above its historical base rate.
The branch that did NOT happen in 2025 despite the FPO having won the preceding election.

transitions.name: A government is formed after a caretaker period

states.name: Discretionary neutrality
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09) and the status quo. The Federal Constitution does NOT define Swiss neutrality -- it appears only as a task assigned to the Federal Assembly and Federal Council in Art. 173(1)(a) and Art. 185(1). Swiss neutrality is a PRACTICE the executive adjusts, not a rule that binds it, which is why sanctions alignment, arms-export rules and Sky Shield participation are all decidable by government and parliament. E3-NEUTRALS-BRIEF §S4.

states.name: Constitutionally entrenched neutrality
states.provenance: The state the Neutrality Initiative would create: neutrality declared perpetual and armed in the constitution, no joining of or cooperation with military alliances except under attack, no participation in third-state conflicts, and a near-total ban on sanctions against warring states except UN Security Council measures. It is ABSORBING by construction -- reversing it would require another constitutional amendment and another double majority, which is a different question on a longer timescale than this horizon.

states.name: Cooperative alignment
states.provenance: The direction the Security Policy Strategy 2026 points and the Neutrality Initiative exists to block: neutrality retained in name while security cooperation with the EU and NATO deepens -- Cassis's 'cooperative neutrality', a term his own Federal Council colleagues struck out of the 2022 neutrality report while the substance survived. Reachable only from the discretionary state, and only if the initiative fails.

destinations.provenance: REJECTION, and the modal outcome. Two August 2026 polls both have it losing -- gfs.bern for SRG 42% yes / 54% no on n>17,000, and 20 Minuten/Tamedia 36% / 62% -- against a long-run initiative pass rate of 11.3%, a double-majority requirement, and rejection recommendations from the Federal Council, the National Council (124-65) and the Council of States (29-10). Weighted at 74 rather than at the 89% the base rate alone implies, because 42% in the SRG wave is not a trivial starting position for an initiative with an organised party behind it.

ACCEPTANCE. Deliberately NOT hard-coded to zero despite the polling and the base rate: this is the one branch that would freeze Swiss sanctions policy and alliance cooperation for the rest of the horizon, and pricing it at nil would be asserting an outcome rather than forecasting one. Gated on SVP strength, the initiative's sponsor.
Single-destination: the drift has one direction. Its probability lives in the triggering event's hazard, which is gated on european_security_integration.

transitions.name: Security cooperation deepens without leaving neutrality

states.name: Minority government
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): AD (PSD+CDS-PP) 91 of 230, 25 short of a majority, governing by alternating majorities. E4-PORTUGAL-IRELAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A1.

states.name: Right coalition with Chega
states.provenance: AD+Chega as a formal coalition: 151 of 230 on the 2025 arithmetic. Not the t=0 configuration -- Montenegro has governed WITH Chega's votes on immigration and nationality while refusing a coalition -- but the configuration the 2025 result makes arithmetically available, and the one Chega's 24.3% polling is bidding for.

states.name: PS-led government
states.provenance: The alternation Portugal ran on from 1995 to 2024. PS leads the August 2026 polling at 28.6% having recovered ~6 points from its worst result since 1987, so this is a live configuration rather than a historical one.

states.name: Caretaker government (gestao)
states.provenance: Portuguese caretaker periods are SHORT and the dwell says so: Art. 172(3) keeps members' terms running to the first sitting of the new Assembly, and the writ must give at least 60 days' notice, so dissolution-to-election has run 60-90 days in every recent case (2021-11-04 dissolution to 2022-01-30 poll; 2025-03-13 to 2025-05-18). E2 §3.2's dwell defect is the reason this is authored rather than left to resolve at the next scheduled election: nl.caretaker-cabinet had no dwell and a late-2026 collapse sat demissionary ~41 months against a real 6-13. Portugal's real window is shorter still.

factorWeights.note: A larger Chega makes a workable centre-right minority harder to assemble, not easier.

destinations.provenance: The modal Portuguese outcome since 2015 and the t=0 configuration. Minority government is the Portuguese norm rather than the exception: it has been the governing form for most of the last decade under both PS and AD.

factorWeights.note: The one branch Chega's share genuinely drives -- it is the only route by which Chega enters government.

destinations.provenance: Weighted up by nationalist_strength and by nothing else, because that is the only quantity that moves it. PSD has refused a formal coalition and has legislated with Chega anyway, so the branch is about arithmetic becoming unavoidable rather than about a change of heart.

factorWeights.note: A larger nationalist right compresses the left's path to a majority.

destinations.provenance: PS leads the August 2026 polling at 28.6%. Base weight below the minority branch because a PS-led government would itself most likely be a minority one -- this branch is about which bloc holds the Prime Ministership, not about whether it commands 116.

Single destination: in Portugal a fallen government goes to the country, not to a re-formation. Art. 195(1) lists what forces resignation (a rejected Programme, a lost confidence motion, a carried no-confidence motion at 116) and there is NO constructive vote of no confidence, so the chamber that removes a government names no successor.

transitions.name: The government loses its majority position

states.name: Fianna Fail-led coalition
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): Micheal Martin (FF) as Taoiseach since 23 January 2025, FF 48 + FG 38 + supporting independents. E4-PORTUGAL-IRELAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §B6.

states.name: Fine Gael-led coalition
states.provenance: The same coalition with the office rotated. Reached on 16 November 2027 by the Programme for Government's own terms, and reachable again after an election. NOT a change of government: the coalition, the Programme and the supporting independents are unchanged; only the officeholder moves.

states.name: Opposition-led government
states.provenance: A government led from outside the FF/FG duopoly -- in practice Sinn Fein, which leads or ties the July 2026 polling at 20-21% and took 39 seats in 2024. Ireland has never had one, which is why this branch's base weight is below the incumbent branches rather than equal to them.

states.name: Caretaker government
states.provenance: Art. 28.11 keeps ministers in office until successors are appointed, and Art. 16.3.2 requires a general election within thirty days of a dissolution -- but Irish GOVERNMENT FORMATION, not the election, is what sets this dwell: 2020 took about five months (February poll, June government), 2024 about two (November poll, January government). E2 §3.2's dwell defect is why this is authored: nl.caretaker-cabinet had no dwell and a late-2026 collapse sat demissionary ~41 months against a real 6-13.

destinations.provenance: Single destination and a certainty, which is the point: this is not a contested outcome and the pack must not price it as one. The mechanism has fired once already, in December 2022 under the 2020 agreement (Martin to Varadkar).

factorWeights.note: A larger nationalist right takes seats from the rural-independent pool FF depends on to reach a majority.

destinations.provenance: FF took 48 seats on 21.86% in 2024 and polls 16% in July 2026, a two-year low. Base weight below the combined FG/opposition branches for that reason.

factorWeights.note: Same channel as FF: the transfer-friendly centre is what the nationalist right erodes.

destinations.provenance: FG polls 18-20% and is level with Sinn Fein. Equal base weight to FF because the two are within polling error of each other and the model should not encode a preference.

factorWeights.note: The incumbents' hold is what stands between the opposition and office; nothing else in this pack moves this branch.

destinations.provenance: Sinn Fein at 20-21% leads or ties, and the two government parties have lost 10 points since the election. Weighted BELOW the two incumbent branches, not above, because Ireland's transfer-based PR-STV system has repeatedly converted an SF plurality of first preferences into fewer seats than the combined centre -- 2024 is the worked example: SF took the second-largest first-preference share and finished third in seats.

A hung result with no formation. Not a rare outcome in Ireland: 2016 took 70 days and 2020 took about five months. Distinct from the other three because it is the absence of a result rather than one of them.

Art. 28.10: the Taoiseach resigns on ceasing to retain a Dail majority UNLESS the President grants a dissolution on his advice. Either branch lands here -- a caretaker government pending formation, or a caretaker government pending an election.

states.name: Minority coalition
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): the Frederiksen III cabinet, sworn in 3 June 2026 -- S+SF+M+RV, 82 of 179, eight short, with confidence and supply from Enhedslisten and Alternativet. E4-DENMARK-GREENLAND-BRIEF-2026-08-24 §A1.

states.name: Cross-bloc coalition
states.provenance: The Frederiksen II configuration (2022-2026): S+V+M, the first cross-bloc majority government since 1978. Denmark reaches this shape when neither bloc can govern alone, and it is a live rather than historical branch -- the 2026 arithmetic makes it available again.

states.name: Right-bloc government
states.provenance: A government of the blue bloc, which on the 2026 seat distribution requires DF's 16. Not reached since 2019, and the configuration DF's growth to 12.2% is bidding for.

states.name: Caretaker government
states.provenance: Danish formation is FAST by European standards and the dwell says so: the 2026 election was held 24 March and the cabinet took office 3 June, about ten weeks over three rounds of talks; 2022 took about six. E2 §3.2's dwell defect is why this is authored -- nl.caretaker-cabinet had no dwell and a late-2026 collapse sat demissionary ~41 months against a real 6-13. Denmark's real window is shorter than the Netherlands' and this state must not inherit a Dutch number.

factorWeights.note: A larger DF compresses the red bloc's path to 90 and pushes toward the other two branches.

destinations.provenance: The modal Danish configuration and the t=0 one. Minority government is the Danish norm rather than the exception -- Denmark has had a majority government for only a handful of years since 1945.

Weighted by nothing, deliberately: a cross-bloc coalition is a formation OUTCOME rather than an electoral preference, and no factor in this pack measures the willingness of the two blocs' leaderships to sit together. Base weight set from the historical frequency -- twice since 1978 -- rather than from a mechanism this pack can express.

factorWeights.note: The one branch DF's share genuinely drives: on the 2026 distribution the blue bloc cannot reach 90 without it.

destinations.provenance: Weighted up by nationalist_strength alone. The 2026 election left the blue bloc short, and DF's 16 seats plus its post-election growth are what would change that.

Single destination. §15 forces a censured minister from office and a censured PM must resign UNLESS he calls an election instead -- and in Denmark he almost always calls the election, which is this pack's headline.

states.name: No invested government
states.provenance: THE t=0 STATE, and the roster's first pack to start in one. Art. 110(4) keeps the censured cabinet carrying out 'only those functions which are necessary for taking care of public business until the members of the new Government are sworn in', which is where Romania has been since 5 May 2026. THE DWELL IS THE HONEST PART AND IT DOES NOT FIT CLEANLY: measured Romanian formation failures are 48 days (Predoiu, May-June 2025), 51 days (Citu as post-censure caretaker, October-November 2021) and the current one at 119 days and running -- so ordinary Romanian formations resolve inside two months and the one the model starts inside is already an outlier at more than double the record. 1-6 months from the model's start puts the current episode's total length at 5-10 months, which over-states the general case and under-states nothing; a dwell sized on the general case (1-2 months) would have asserted that the outlier the model is initialised inside ends immediately. E2 §3.2's dwell defect run the other way: there the risk was a caretaker sitting 41 months against a real 6-13, here it is a general dwell being stretched by one extraordinary occupancy, and the cost is stated rather than hidden. RELEVANT MARKET, recorded and NOT bound as an anchor (E5.9): Polymarket's 'next Romania PM appointed by 31 Dec 2026' reads 80% on $6.7k, and its rules exclude any interim or caretaker Prime Minister from resolution.

states.name: Minority or technocratic government
states.provenance: President Dan's own stated preferred outcome -- he is 'encouraging the emergence of a minority government with a limited mandate' -- and the configuration the liquid market prices: Polymarket's 'party of the next Prime Minister of Romania' reads Independent/Technocrat 59.5% on $59k against PSD 28.35% and AUR 1.0%. That market is a statement about the KIND of government, which is what a machine's states are, and it is the reason this state exists separately from the grand coalition rather than being folded into it.

states.name: Pro-European grand coalition
states.provenance: PSD + PNL + USR + UDMR, the configuration that governed from 23 June 2025 and died on 5 May 2026, and the second such coalition since 2021. It remains arithmetically available on the December 2024 seats (86 + 49 + 40 + 22 = 197 of 331 in the Chamber alone) and its leaders were still meeting President Dan on 20 August 2026. Not the t=0 configuration, and not dead.

states.name: AUR-led government
states.provenance: AUR polls 35.7% and PolitPro projects it 135 of 330 seats, against 63 at the election. NOT a live configuration for the CURRENT formation -- the market prices AUR as the party of the next Prime Minister at 1.0% -- and a live one for the two parliamentary elections inside this horizon (months 27 and 75), which is why it is reachable from election-outcome and effectively not from formation-outcome. Every other party in the chamber has refused to govern with it.

destinations.provenance: The modal exit and the one both the President and the market point at. Art. 103 needs a majority of all deputies and senators (233 of 465) for investiture, and no bloc holds one; a minority or technocratic cabinet tolerated by abstention is what that arithmetic produces.

The PSD-PNL-USR-UDMR arithmetic still clears 233 and its leaders are still negotiating. Weighted below the minority branch because the coalition collapsed over austerity four months ago and the dispute that killed it -- pension and public-wage reform against a 6.2%-of-GDP deficit and an RRF deadline -- is unresolved.

factorWeights.note: The only branch AUR's share drives, and it is the only quantity that moves it.

destinations.provenance: Small and NOT zero, AND THE BASE WEIGHT WAS SET FROM THE MEASURED SHARE RATHER THAN GUESSED AT -- the B3-audit discipline applied at authoring. AUR holds 63 + 28 seats and has tabled a censure motion jointly with the PSD once already; every other party has refused to govern with it; investiture needs 233 of 465 and AUR's own projection is 135 of 330. Polymarket prices the party of the next Prime Minister as AUR at 1.0% on $14k. A first draft used a base weight of 0.08 reading 'about eight percent' and simcli transition-shares returned 12.3%, because the +1.0 factor weight on a nationalist_strength of 74 multiplies it by exp(1.0 x 24/50) = 1.62 while the two pro-European branches carry no factor weight at all. Re-set to 0.010 so the SHARE lands near the market rather than the base weight looking near it.

factorWeights.note: A larger AUR makes a workable minority arrangement harder to assemble, not easier.

destinations.provenance: Romania's post-2020 norm. The Ciolacu II cabinet was invested 240 of 465 on 23 December 2024, seven votes over the line, with the nineteen national-minority deputies inside the majority.

factorWeights.note: The larger the nationalist right, the fewer seats are left for a pro-European coalition to assemble 233 from.

destinations.provenance: The configuration Romania has produced after both of its last two elections. Weighted down hard by nationalist_strength because this branch is arithmetically the one AUR's growth eats: at PolitPro's projected 135 of 330 the remaining parties must find 233 of 465 from what is left.

factorWeights.note: The branch AUR's vote share exists to drive.

destinations.provenance: A live branch at an election in a way it is not inside the current chamber. AUR took 18.01% in December 2024 and polls 35.7%; Simion took 40.96% in the first round of the May 2025 presidential re-run and 46.40% in the runoff. What stands against it is that no other party will coalesce with it and that investiture needs 233 of 465, which is why the base weight sits well below the two pro-European branches even as the factor weight is the largest in the transition. THE BASE WEIGHT WAS SET FROM THE MEASURED SHARE, NOT THE OTHER WAY ROUND: at 0.14 simcli transition-shares returned 21.4% against a hand-computed 14.0%, a 7.4pp gap -- the largest in this pack and the B3-audit error class caught at authoring rather than in a report. Re-set to 0.09 so the drawn share is the roughly 15% this pack intends to claim for an AUR-led government at any single Romanian election.

factorWeights.note: INVERTED SCALE: low constitutional_crisis means a deep crisis, so a NEGATIVE weight makes formation failure MORE likely as the crisis deepens. The sign is the easy thing to get backwards here and it is written out for that reason.
A larger AUR that nobody will govern with is the mechanism by which an election produces no majority.

destinations.provenance: AN ELECTION CAN FAIL TO PRODUCE A GOVERNMENT, and in Romania that is the Art. 89 setup rather than a dead end -- the 60-day clock and the two-rejection count both start here. Base weight sized against the record: ten elections since 1990 have produced a government every time, but the two most recent formations took 22 days and then, after a censure rather than an election, 119 and counting. This branch is a RE-ENTRY into the state the model starts in and it sits in the denominator of every other share in this transition, which is exactly the B3-audit trap; shares checked with simcli transition-shares.

Single destination, and it is the pack's headline as a mechanism. Art. 110(2): the Government resigns on the date Parliament withdraws its confidence; Art. 110(3): 'the provisions of Article 103 shall apply accordingly' -- the President designates again, INSIDE THE SAME PARLIAMENT, with no dissolution and no clock. Twelve times in 36 years, and not once has it produced an election. AND THIS TRANSITION IS FIRED ONLY BY ro.formation-failure, NOT BY ro.pm-exit — the pack's sharpest authoring judgement, recorded here because a transition's own `provenance` does not survive compose(). It is a claim about the monthly timestep: Romania has had NINE acting premierships in 36 years and most lasted DAYS (Predoiu 3, 3 and 48; Bejinariu 7; Athanasiu 9; Cimpeanu 12; Ciuca 16; Dejeu 18), which a monthly model cannot represent and should not pretend to. So an ordinary mid-term departure leaves the configuration standing, and only the rare MATERIAL formation failure — three in 36 years, at 48, 51 and 119+ days — moves the machine.

transitions.name: The government loses office inside the same parliament

states.name: Single-party majority government
states.provenance: THE t=0 STATE and the first of its kind in Bulgaria since 1997. Progressive Bulgaria, sworn in 8 May 2026 under Rumen Radev -- President 2017-2026, and the first Bulgarian government led by a former President -- holds 131 of 240 against a 121 threshold. Its allies in the National Assembly are not needed to pass anything. A SEAT-SHARE DISAGREEMENT RESOLVED BY ARITHMETIC AND RECORDED, because it recurs in every write-up of this election: PB's share is quoted as 43.91% (Wikipedia), 44.6% (Freiheit), 44.7% (OSW) and ~45% (ECFR), and the gap is Bulgaria's formal 'none of the above' ballot option -- 50,733 votes, a valid vote excluded from the seat-allocation denominator. 1,444,920/3,290,889 = 43.91%; 1,444,920/(3,290,889 - 50,733) = 44.59%. The pack takes the seat-denominator column, which is what the 4% threshold is measured against.

states.name: Coalition government
states.provenance: The ordinary Bulgarian governing form and the one every cabinet between 2001 and 2026 took. Reachable from an election and, rarely, directly from a fallen government via the three-mandate sequence succeeding -- which has happened twice in ten mid-term falls, both before 1997 (Popov December 1990, Berov December 1992).

states.name: Minority government
states.provenance: Distinguished from the coalition state because Bulgaria's post-2021 governments have repeatedly governed without a stable 121, and because Art. 89's no-confidence threshold -- more than half of ALL members, not of those voting -- makes the difference material: a minority government survives only while the opposition cannot assemble 121 against it.

states.name: President-appointed caretaker government
states.provenance: A FIRST-CLASS STATE CARRYING NEARLY HALF THE PROBABILITY MASS, not a thin transition -- and the dwell is measured rather than assumed. Bulgaria spent 883 of 1,822 days from 12 May 2021 to 8 May 2026 under a President-appointed caretaker: Yanev 215 days, Donev 308, Glavchev 282, Gyurov 78, mean 221 days = 7.3 months. The 3-10 month dwell brackets all four observations except Gyurov's 78 days, which sits one week under the floor -- stated rather than fitted, because widening to 2-10 would put mass at durations Art. 64(3)'s two-month election window cannot produce for a dissolution that also has to run a three-mandate sequence first. E2 §3.2's Dutch dwell defect is why this is authored at all: nl.caretaker-cabinet had none and would have sat a demissionary cabinet ~41 months against a real 6-13. THE EXIT IS CONSTITUTIONALLY FIXED -- Art. 99(5) requires the President to dissolve and schedule elections -- so resolveVia is election-outcome and there is no other way out. THE APPOINTMENT POWER WAS AMENDED AND THE AMENDMENT SURVIVED BY A TIE, which is worth carrying in the pack rather than only in the brief: the December 2023 amendments restricted the President's choice to a closed list of sitting officeholders (Speaker; BNB Governor or a Deputy Governor; National Audit Office President or Vice-President; Ombudsman or Deputy), and on 26 July 2024 the Constitutional Court STRUCK DOWN the judicial-reform provisions while the caretaker restriction STOOD -- because the Court split evenly and failed to reach a majority against it. One search summary this block read reported that backwards, which is the W4.5 error class exactly. The restriction has been exercised twice and the office chosen differed both times (Glavchev from the Audit Office, Gyurov from the BNB), and Gyurov is now a presidential candidate priced at 21% -- the caretaker post is a political launchpad, which is a second-order consequence nobody appears to have intended. NOT QUOTED: the amended Art. 99's official text. parliament.bg is behind an anti-bot filter, legislationline.org's consolidated PDF 404s and loc.gov 403s; the office list above is a paraphrase reconciled across three secondary sources.

destinations.provenance: The modal Bulgarian outcome and the form every cabinet took between 2001 and 2026. Base weight highest because the 4% threshold and Bulgaria's fragmentation make a majority coalition the ordinary product of an election that works at all.

factorWeights.note: A weaker political environment makes the thin arrangement more likely than the coalition, so this branch is weighted UP as durability falls -- the sign is deliberate and reads the opposite way from the coalition branch.

destinations.provenance: The post-2021 form: several Bulgarian governments in that period governed without a stable 121.

factorWeights.note: The branch a strong political position produces, and the only one whose base weight is priced on a two-member class.

destinations.provenance: TWO INSTANCES IN EIGHTEEN ELECTIONS -- the UDF's 137 of 240 in 1997 and Progressive Bulgaria's 131 in April 2026 -- so 11% of elections, and the base weight says so. The durability weight is what lets the model re-produce the t=0 configuration when Bulgarian politics is running well, and it is the largest positive factor weight in the transition.

factorWeights.note: The formation-failure branch: the worse the political environment, the more likely the three mandates fail and the President must appoint a caretaker and dissolve again.

destinations.provenance: THE RE-ENTRY BRANCH, AND IT IS HALF OF WHY BULGARIA HOLDS SO MANY ELECTIONS. An election that produces no government sends the three-mandate sequence round again and Art. 99(5) then requires a fresh caretaker and a fresh dissolution: five of Bulgaria's thirteen early elections since 1990 came from this channel rather than from a government falling. It is a RE-DWELL when fired from caretaker-government, so it sits in the denominator of every other share here -- exactly the B3-audit trap. Shares checked with simcli transition-shares, not read off these base weights.

THE MODAL AND NEARLY THE ONLY CONSEQUENCE, and it is the pack's headline as a mechanism. Art. 99(5): after three mandates of seven days each, the President SHALL appoint a caretaker government, dissolve the National Assembly and schedule elections. Eight of Bulgaria's ten mid-term government falls since 1990 went this way, and since 2021 the three-mandate sequence has failed six times out of six. AND THIS IS THE ONLY TRANSITION bg.pm-exit FIRES, which is the pack's central authoring decision: in Bulgaria the leader, the government and the parliament die together, so ONE hazard drives all three. Compare ro.json in the same block, where pm-exit triggers NOTHING because Art. 110(3) re-designates inside the same chamber.

The three-mandate sequence SUCCEEDING -- a new government formed inside the same parliament. Two instances in ten mid-term falls (Popov, December 1990; Berov, December 1992), both before 1997 and neither since. Small and not zero, because the mechanism is unamended and the arithmetic that produced it can recur; and it is the branch that makes this pack's election cadence emerge at the right rate rather than at the maximum one.

states.name: Single-party majority government
states.provenance: THE t=0 STATE. New Democracy under Kyriakos Mitsotakis, elected 158 of 300 on 25 June 2023, now at 156 against a majority of 151. The majority bonus is what produced it: Article 54(1) makes an electoral law passed without a two-thirds majority apply only from the SECOND election after passage, so May 2023 ran under simple PR and produced nothing while June 2023 ran under the bonus and produced 158 seats. The bonus now applies from the first round -- 20 extra seats at 25% of the vote, one more per half-point above, to a maximum of 50 at 40%.

states.name: Coalition government
states.provenance: Greece's form in 2012-2015 and 2015-2019, and the one a hung parliament produces when the Article 37 mandates SUCCEED. Distinguished from the caretaker state because a coalition governs on a parliamentary majority with a political programme, where an Article 37 cabinet exists to run an election.

states.name: Article 37 caretaker premiership
states.provenance: THE STATE NO OTHER ROSTER POLITY HAS, and the pack's headline as a mechanism. Article 37: where no party holds an absolute majority the President issues exploratory mandates to the largest, second and third parties, EACH IN FORCE FOR THREE DAYS; failing all three he attempts an all-party cabinet and, failing that, 'appoints a senior judge to form a widely-accepted cabinet for conducting elections'. SEVEN USES IN 52.11 YEARS -- Tzannetakis (Jul-Oct 1989, cross-party), Grivas (Oct-Nov 1989, judge), Zolotas (Nov 1989 - Apr 1990, ecumenical), Papademos (Nov 2011 - May 2012, technocrat), Pikrammenos (May-Jun 2012, judge), Thanou-Christophilou (Aug-Sep 2015, judge), Sarmas (May-Jun 2023, judge). THE DWELL IS SIZED ON THE LIVE MECHANISM, NOT ON THE POOLED CLASS, and the split is the reason: the four JUDICIAL caretakers ran 0.8, 1.0, 1.1 and 1.4 months, while the three cross-party or ecumenical ones ran 3.3, 4.6 and 6.2 months and all three belong to eras (1989-90, 2011-12) whose governing arrangements were coalition rescues rather than election administrations. 1-3 months brackets the judicial route and reaches the shortest of the others. Pooling all seven would have put the modal dwell near four months against a live mechanism that produces one -- E2 §3.2's dwell defect avoided by reading the class rather than averaging it.

factorWeights.note: The bonus turns a strong plurality into a majority and a weak one into a hung parliament; this is the branch that condition buys.

destinations.provenance: What the majority bonus produces when the leading party clears roughly a third of the vote: 20 extra seats at 25%, rising to 50 at 40%. ND took 40.56% and 158 seats in June 2023. Weighted highest at base because Greece's electoral system is built to manufacture majorities, and weighted UP by durability because on today's polling the same system returns ~118.

The Article 37 mandates succeeding, or a pre-agreed coalition. Greece governed this way from 2012 to 2019. No factor weight: whether a hung parliament coalesces or reruns is a question about party arithmetic this pack does not model, and inventing a driver for it would be worse than leaving it at base.

factorWeights.note: The hung-parliament branch. A weak political environment is what puts the leading party under the bonus's effective threshold and sends the chamber to three three-day mandates.

destinations.provenance: THE RERUN'S RESIDUE, AND IT IS LIVE. On July 2026 polling ND at ~30% takes roughly 118 of 300 with the bonus -- Metron Analysis projected 120 on 30 June -- so the modal outcome of the scheduled 2027 election is a hung parliament, which under Article 37 means three mandates, a judicial caretaker and a second election. FOUR DOUBLE-ELECTION EPISODES in 52 years produced five intervals under eight months (0.10, 0.11, 0.38, 0.42, 0.65 years), and although two of the three mechanisms behind them have been legislated away, THIS one has not. It is a RE-ENTRY when fired from caretaker-government -- an election that again produces nothing -- so it sits in the denominator of every other share here, which is the B3-audit trap; shares checked with simcli transition-shares.

Single destination. Article 41(1) permits dissolution only when two governments have resigned or been voted down AND the composition fails to guarantee stability; Article 41(2) permits it on the proposal of a Cabinet that HAS confidence, to renew the mandate on a national issue. Either way the decree must proclaim elections within thirty days and convene the new Parliament within a further thirty -- so a Greek government that goes, goes to the country through a caretaker, not to a re-formation inside the chamber.

transitions.name: The government loses its majority position

states.name: HDZ-led coalition
states.provenance: THE t=0 STATE and the configuration Croatia has run for most of its independence. The Plenkovic III cabinet, in office since 17 May 2024: 16 HDZ ministers and 3 from the Homeland Movement, HDZ 61 + DP 14 = 75 of 151 against a majority of 76, working number 78. Defence: Ivan Anusic. Foreign: Gordan Grlic-Radman. The 17 April 2024 election gave the HDZ-led coalition 34.42% and 61 seats on 62.31% turnout.

states.name: SDP/Mozemo-led coalition
states.provenance: The alternation Croatia has produced twice (Racan 2000, Milanovic 2011). Rivers of Justice took 25.40% and 42 seats in April 2024; SDP polls 23.0% and Mozemo! 15.9% with 30 projected seats, so a left bloc is arithmetically live in a way it has not been since 2016. Note the personnel irony this pack does not model: the President whose veto hr.atlanticism is priced on is of SDP origin.

states.name: Caretaker government pending an early election
states.provenance: THE DWELL IS MEASURED ON THE ONE OCCURRENCE, and the pack says so rather than inventing a distribution. Croatia's only premature parliament in 34 years is the 2015-2016 sequence: Oreskovic was removed by a no-confidence vote 125-15 with 2 abstentions on 16 June 2016, the Sabor self-dissolved on 20 June effective 15 July, the election was held on 11 September and Plenkovic took office on 19 October -- FOUR MONTHS from removal to new government. Article 73 caps the election at 60 days after dissolution and Article 113 gives a 30-day replacement window before dissolution becomes automatic, so 2-4 months brackets the constitutional path and the single observation together. E2 §3.2's dwell defect is why this is authored rather than left to resolve at the next scheduled election.

destinations.provenance: HDZ has led every Croatian government except two since 1990 and has polled first continuously since 2016 -- 31.6% on the trend, 27.0-27.4% raw, against SDP's 23.0/18.8-21.5. Base weight above half because the historical record and the current polling agree, which they rarely do.

factorWeights.note: The alternation branch: a weakening incumbent is what has produced Croatia's two changes of governing bloc.

destinations.provenance: Racan 2000 and Milanovic 2011 are the two instances in nine elections. Weighted up as durability falls, because both followed a visibly failing HDZ administration rather than a normal swing.

factorWeights.note: The formation-failure re-entry, and it is small because Croatia has never taken more than a month to form a government after a scheduled election.

destinations.provenance: A RE-ENTRY branch, kept small and not zero. Croatian government formation after the 2024 election took exactly one month (17 April to 17 May) and after 2020 about three weeks; the protracted 2015-2016 case is the only one in the record and it followed an election that produced a near dead heat. Because this branch is a re-dwell when fired from caretaker-government it sits in the denominator of both other shares here -- the B3-audit trap -- and the shares were checked with simcli transition-shares rather than read off these base weights.

Single destination. Article 77's first limb -- 'The Croatian Parliament may be dissolved in order to call early elections if so decided by a majority of all of its Members' -- is the mechanism Croatia actually uses, and it is unusually permissive: no head-of-state involvement, no confidence vote required, 76 votes and the Parliament ends itself. That is what happened on 20 June 2016. Article 113's automatic dissolution after a failed 30-day replacement window exists and has never been used; Article 104's presidential dissolution requires a Government motion countersigned by the Prime Minister and has never been used either.

states.name: SDS-led government
states.provenance: THE t=0 STATE, and it is in office although its bloc came SECOND. Janez Jansa was elected Prime Minister by the National Assembly on 22 May 2026 with 51 votes and his cabinet confirmed on 4 June with 49 -- his FOURTH term (2004-2008, 2012-2013, 2020-2022), cumulative tenure 7.53 years, second in the roster behind Plenkovic on that measure and last but one on continuous tenure at 0.24 years. SDS 28 + NSi 7 + Demokrati 6 + SLS 1 + FOKUS 1 = 43 of 90, with confidence and supply from Resni.ca (5) and the two national-minority deputies. Defence: Valentin Hajdinjak (NSi). Foreign and European Affairs: Tone Kajzer (SDS). Finance: Andrej Sircelj (SDS). AND THE MACHINE HAS ONLY TWO STATES, WHICH IS THIS PACK'S HEADLINE AS A MECHANISM AND IS RECORDED HERE BECAUSE A MACHINE'S OWN `provenance` DOES NOT SURVIVE compose(). Article 116: the National Assembly may pass a vote of no confidence ONLY by electing a new President of the Government, and the incumbent 'together with his ministers must continue to perform his regular duties until the swearing in of a new Government'. Article 117 gives thirty days to elect a replacement after a lost confidence vote, failing which the President dissolves; Article 111 gives fourteen days for a second nominee. So SLOVENIA CANNOT BE WITHOUT A GOVERNMENT and has no caretaker premiership in the Greek or Bulgarian sense — the absence of a third state is the modelling claim, and it is the exact inverse of bg.json in the same block, whose caretaker state carries nearly half the probability mass.

states.name: Centre-left government
states.provenance: The configuration that WON the March 2026 election and did not form: Gibanje Svoboda took 28.66% and 29 seats, and with SD's 6 and Levica/Vesna's 5 the bloc reaches 40 -- six short of 46, which is why Golob is in opposition. It polls 26.0 + 8.8 + 8.8 = 43.6% now against the government bloc's ~42.4%. THE TWO-STATE MACHINE IS THE MODELLING CLAIM: Slovenia has alternated between these two blocs at every change of government since 1992, and Article 116 means a change is always a change TO a named alternative rather than an interval without one.

destinations.provenance: SDS has been the largest or second-largest party at every Slovenian election since 2000 and polls 27.9% now. Base weight just under half because SDS's problem has never been its vote -- it is COALITIONABILITY: it came first in 2018 and 2022 by vote or seats on occasions when it could not form a government, and 2026 is the third time in five elections that the largest bloc has gone into opposition.

Weighted marginally above the right branch, and the asymmetry is the pack's one soft judgement about Slovenian politics: the centre-left bloc has formed the government after five of the last seven elections, usually behind a NEW vehicle (LDS, Positive Slovenia, SMC, LMS, Gibanje Svoboda) that did not exist at the previous one. That pattern is real and this pack cannot represent its mechanism -- a machine has states, not new parties -- so it is expressed as a small base-weight tilt and named here rather than left implicit. NO FACTOR WEIGHTS ON EITHER BRANCH: si.nationalist_strength reads Resni.ca, a five-seat party outside the mainstream right, and using it to drive a bloc alternation would be exactly the referent error this pack's own nationalist-vehicle class exists to declare.

Article 116 requires the replacement to be ELECTED in the same act, so a constructive vote is always a switch to a named person with 46 votes behind them -- and in Slovenia the arithmetic for 46 against a sitting SDS government has only ever come from the other bloc. Jansa's 2013 removal by constructive vote elected Bratusek; Peterle's 1992 removal elected Drnovsek.

The RE-DWELL branch: a replacement from within the same bloc. Drnovsek's December 2002 resignation to become President produced Rop from the same party, and Sarec's January 2020 resignation produced a NEW majority assembled inside the sitting chamber. One of five class members kept the bloc, which is where 0.2 comes from. IT SITS IN THE DENOMINATOR of the other share -- the B3-audit trap -- so the printed shares are not 80/20; checked with simcli transition-shares.

transitions.name: Constructive vote replaces an SDS-led government

destinations.provenance: The mirror of the right-origin transition, and the record supports it symmetrically: Drnovsek's LDS government lost the April 2000 vote and Bajuk, of the centre-right, took office on 7 June; Sarec's LMS resignation in January 2020 produced Jansa's third government, assembled in the sitting chamber and sworn on 13 March.

The RE-DWELL branch, weighted identically to its mirror for the same one-in-five reason. The pack does NOT claim the two blocs differ in how they replace their own leaders; it claims only that a constructive vote is usually a switch.

states.provenance: No distinct constitutional category, but a well-established practice: Tosovsky (1998), Fischer (2009-10), Rusnok (2013, governed on despite losing its own confidence vote 93-100) all continued ordinary administration pending the next election. Three uses since 1993.

states.name: Opposition-led coalition
states.provenance: The only alternative government configuration this pack distinguishes -- which SPOLU/STAN/Pirati-flavoured combination takes office is not separately modelled, matching this pack's density elsewhere (Malta and Cyprus make the identical simplification for their own two-configuration systems).

transitions.name: The government loses its majority position

destinations.provenance: August 2026 polling (PolitPro) projects the sitting coalition at ~114/200 (57.0%) if an election were held then, LARGER than its actual 2025 result -- weighted as the modal outcome, gated on durability so a coalition that has visibly frayed by the time an election actually falls draws a lower share.

The opposition's floor, not its ceiling: SPOLU+STAN+Pirati held 92 seats in 2025 and current polling does not show them closing the gap, but a full decade horizon carries genuine uncertainty a single polling snapshot cannot resolve.

states.provenance: The 24 January-19 March 2025 precedent: two Hlas MPs expelled dropped the coalition below 76 for the first time; a bare loss of floor majority is NOT self-executing in Slovak practice -- only an actual lost confidence/no-confidence vote forces the President's hand, and none occurred during this ~8-week window.

A documented simplification.

The modal outcome on current polling, not a confident call: SNS sitting below its 5% threshold (a real seat loss for the coalition side) is a documented tailwind for this branch that the pack does not further quantify.

states.name: Independent, no major-party backing
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09). Nikos Christodoulides, in office since 28 February 2023, the FIRST Cypriot president elected without either major party's (DISY or AKEL) backing -- won the 12 February 2023 runoff 51.97%-48.03% against Andreas Mavroyiannis, with DIKO among his loose supporting coalition.

states.name: DISY-aligned presidency
states.provenance: The largest House party at the 24 May 2026 election (27.1%, 17 of 56 elected seats), liberal-conservative, EPP-affiliated.

states.name: AKEL-aligned presidency
states.provenance: The second-largest House party (23.9%, 15 seats), the Cypriot communist/Cypriotist left, traditionally the more accommodation-minded major bloc on the Cyprus problem.

states.name: Nationalist-aligned presidency
states.provenance: ELAM (ultranationalist far-right) DOUBLED its House seats in 2026 (8 of 56, +4), the single biggest mover of the election, with DIKO (10.0%, nationalist-leaning centrist) a possible coalition partner for a harder-line presidency. A named state rather than folded into disy-aligned, on the same argument the roster's other nationalist-right states use elsewhere: a distinct political family, not a shade of the centre-right.

destinations.provenance: DISY entered 2026 as the largest House party (27.1%). Weighted somewhat above its raw legislative share on the two-round runoff's centre-consolidating tendency (Cyprus's own history: no first-round leader has failed to be one of the top two since 1968, and the runoff has repeatedly favoured the more establishment-aligned of the two finalists).

AKEL's 2026 legislative share (23.9%) plus its standing as the traditional second pole of Cypriot presidential politics -- AKEL's own candidate (Christofias) held the office 2008-13, and its 2023 candidate Mavroyiannis reached the runoff and took 48.03%.

The re-dwell branch: Christodoulides is eligible for one further consecutive term (5y+5y, 10-year cap) or another independent could repeat his path. Weighted at the modal outcome's level despite a 28%-approval reading BECAUSE this is a re-DWELL branch sitting in the transition's own denominator (B3's rule), not a prediction that Christodoulides personally wins re-election -- gated positively on his own approval so a further slide de-rates this branch specifically rather than the whole distribution.

ELAM+DIKO's combined 2026 legislative share is ~21%, weighted DOWN from that raw figure on the same runoff-consolidation logic that weights DISY up: Cyprus's two-round system has repeatedly squeezed harder-line first-round finishers in the second round (no ultranationalist candidate has ever won the presidency), so ELAM's doubling of its LEGISLATIVE seats is not read as an equal gain in PRESIDENTIAL viability.
