states.name: Labour single-party majority
states.provenance: t=0. Robert Abela sworn in for a FOURTH CONSECUTIVE Labour term 1 June 2026 (30 May 2026 election, 51.77% first-preference, 42 of 79 seats after correctives) -- the first party/PM in Maltese history to win four elections in a row.

states.name: Nationalist Party single-party majority
states.provenance: The only alternative government Malta's electoral system produces: EVERY government since 1966 has been single-party, and Malta has never once needed coalition-formation modelling, so this machine has no coalition or minority state at all -- the two-party, corrective-seat system structurally excludes them.

destinations.provenance: 2026: Labour 51.77% (down 3.3pp from 2022's 55.11%). The margin over PN has narrowed two elections running; weighted just below an even split against the observed trend rather than at the 2026 landslide's own level.

2026: Nationalist 44.68% (up 2.9pp from 2022's 41.74%), Alex Borg leading as Leader of the Opposition since September 2025. The narrowing trend argues for a genuinely competitive next cycle rather than a fifth consecutive Labour landslide.

RE-DWELL, listed separately from the primary Labour branch above to keep the SAME-PARTY-CONTINUES-BUT-NARROWER outcome (a fifth term at a reduced margin) visible in the destination table rather than folded silently into the main branch -- both resolve to the same state, so the split has no effect on the drawn share, only on how the provenance reads.

states.name: Liberal majority government
states.provenance: t=0 (2026-09): Carney's Liberal government, 171 of 343 seats with 6 vacant, a majority reached 2026-04-13 through five floor-crossings and a sweep of three by-elections rather than a second general election. E7-CANADA-BRIEF §1. 171 of 343 is ONE SHORT of the nominal 172-seat majority and TWO ABOVE a majority of the 337 seats actually filled; the six vacancies are the whole of the gap. Against a combined opposition of 166 (CPC 139, BQ 21, NDP 5, GP 1), and with the Speaker voting only to break ties, the government carries a confidence vote 170-166. So this is a WORKING majority of the sitting House rather than a nominal majority of the full one, which is why the machine starts here and not in minority-parliament: the incumbent is not testing confidence vote-by-vote, it is winning them by four. NG1d: this read '174 of 343' until the standings were retrieved and counted. NG1b had already corrected the PREMISE to 171 and left this provenance behind, so the state's own argument and the premise that checks it disagreed by three seats — the drift NG1b measured reaching the checkable layer and stopping one field short of the state it justifies.

states.name: Conservative majority government
states.provenance: A Conservative government with a Commons majority after a future general election. Reachable only through ca.election-outcome. No third-party-majority state is authored (unlike uk.json's reform-majority): no third party currently polls at a scale where a federal majority is a live outcome -- the NDP holds 5 seats and Bloc Quebecois, at 21 (NG1b VERIFIED 2026-08-26: this read 7 and 22, which are the 2025 election-night figures rather than current standings; ourcommons.ca party standings, retrieved 2026-08-26), contests only Quebec ridings by mandate and does not seek to govern Canada as a whole.

states.name: Minority parliament
states.provenance: No single party holds a Commons majority. Named for Canadian convention rather than borrowed from Westminster's 'hung parliament': the incumbent continues to govern and tests confidence vote-by-vote, which is what actually happened 2025-04-28 to 2026-04-13 -- a recently-LIVED state (twelve months) rather than a hypothetical one, and the reference material this pack's severity and election-outcome weights are partly drawn from.

destinations.provenance: Incumbency plus the currently-strong polling lead, discounted because a three-year-out election is not read directly off today's numbers -- uk.json's identical caution about a mid-parliament peak not being a fixed point.

A Liberal government that has lost its durability is the condition under which a Conservative majority becomes live, mirroring the inverse relationship uk.json draws between its incumbent and its principal challenger.

The seat-translation branch, carrying no factor weight because it is governed by reference class ca.election-translation rather than any modelled quantity -- an honest flat weight rather than a fabricated dependence, on uk.json's identical reasoning for its own hung-parliament branch.

states.provenance: DYAD brief §5.1 S1 — Aug 2026 initial: kinetically quiet 15 months post-Sindoor while treaties are suspended, trade/airspace cut, rhetoric maximal; 2009-15 and 2017-18 are prior occupants.

states.name: Militarized crisis
states.provenance: DYAD brief §5.1 S2: named trigger + mobilization/ultimatum, no cross-border fires yet — 2001-02 (10 mo), 2008 (~6 wk), post-trigger windows 2016/2019/2025 (11-15 days ≈ the 1-month floor). The override is the off-ramp engaging: all six crises drew great-power de-escalation.

states.name: Cross-border strikes

All three de-escalated ≤ 4 days, hence the 1-2 month dwell at monthly resolution.

outcomeFlags.name: The t=0 Taoiseach left office
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form: the union of ie.government's states other than the one in which the t=0 Taoiseach holds office. READ THE CAVEAT BEFORE COMPARING THIS ACROSS PACKS. It is expected to read at or near 100%, and that is CORRECT rather than a defect: the Programme for Government fixes the departure at 16 November 2027, month 14, so in Ireland this class is a CALENDAR CERTAINTY where every other pack answers it with a hazard. Recorded at its true value rather than suppressed -- E3's ch.arms_export_referendum at 100% is the same decision for the same reason -- but a reader scanning the incumbent-exit column across the roster will see Ireland at the top and must not read that as instability. outcomeFlags.provenance: State form. Ireland has never had one; in practice this is a Sinn Fein-led government, and it is the single largest discontinuity this pack can express.

outcomeFlags.name: An early election was called

outcomeFlags.name: Prime Minister left office without an election
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form; the non-routine part of leaving office, and in Denmark much rarer than the parliament ending early.

outcomeFlags.name: The t=0 caretaker Prime Minister ceased to hold office
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form, the union fixed by the scenario class: the machine's states OTHER than the one in which the t=0 incumbent still holds office. Bolojan holds the premiership under Art. 110(4) and the model starts in no-government, so the union is exact by construction. IT OVER-READS BY A KNOWN AMOUNT AND THE AMOUNT IS PRICED: Polymarket puts Bolojan at 5.25% to be the next invested Prime Minister, and this flag would count that path as an exit. The comparable market -- 'Ilie Bolojan out by 31 December 2026', 86.95% on $320k -- is recorded and NOT bound as an anchor (E5.9), because it resolves at month 4 of 120.

outcomeFlags.name: The country was without an invested government
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form, and it reads 100% by construction because the model STARTS here -- E3's ch.arms_export_referendum and E4's ie.incumbent_exit are the same call, reported rather than suppressed. The OCCUPANCY carries the signal the 'ever' reading cannot: what this pack is actually claiming is how much of a decade Romania spends unable to invest a government, against a measured 119 days at t=0 and a previous record of 51.

outcomeFlags.name: AUR led a government
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form. The configuration AUR's 35.7% is bidding for, reachable in practice through the two scheduled parliamentary elections rather than through the current formation, which the market prices at 1.0%.

outcomeFlags.name: A Prime Minister left office mid-term
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form, and the quantity that supports a cross-pack comparison. This is the roster's second-highest leader-exit rate at 0.331/yr, and reading it beside ro.no_government is the pack's headline: Romania's leaders go often and its parliament never does.

outcomeFlags.name: A President left office mid-term
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form. One instance in 36.2 years, and it happened nineteen months before t=0.

outcomeFlags.name: Parliament was dissolved under Article 89
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form, and the pack's own tripwire on its softest number. Art. 89 has never been used; if this flag reads materially above a percent or two, the analyst-assessed rate on ro.article-89-dissolution is doing more work than its zero-instance evidence supports and should be revisited.

outcomeFlags.name: The t=0 Prime Minister ceased to hold office
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form, the union fixed by the scenario class: the machine's states OTHER than the one in which the t=0 incumbent holds office. Radev's Progressive Bulgaria government IS the single-party majority, so the union is the other three states. IT OVER-READS BY A KNOWN AND UNPRICED AMOUNT: a future election could return Progressive Bulgaria to a single-party majority under a different leader, which this union counts as the incumbent still in post, and it could return Radev at the head of a coalition, which it counts as an exit. Both are real paths and neither is separable in a configuration machine. The rate-bearing quantity that supports a cross-pack comparison is bg.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.274/yr.

outcomeFlags.name: A President-appointed caretaker government held office
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form, and THE PACK'S OWN CALIBRATION TRIPWIRE. Bulgaria spent 45.6% of the five years to the model's start month under a caretaker government, so the OCCUPANCY of this state -- not its 'ever' reading, which the A2 saturation pattern will drive toward 100% over 120 months -- is what should be read against that number. A pack whose caretaker occupancy comes out near zero has silently authored a different country.

outcomeFlags.name: A single party governed with an outright majority
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form, reading 100% by construction because the model STARTS here -- reported rather than suppressed, on E3's ch.arms_export_referendum precedent. Its occupancy is the informative half, against a base rate of two such governments in eighteen elections since 1990.

outcomeFlags.name: A Prime Minister left office mid-term
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form, and in this pack it is simultaneously the government-fall flag and the proximate cause of most elections, because Art. 99(5) makes those one event. Reading it beside ro.mid_term_leader_exit is the block's headline: 0.274/yr here against 0.331/yr there, in the country with 1.8x the elections.

outcomeFlags.name: A President left office mid-term
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form. One instance in 36.1 years, and it happened seven months before t=0 -- and the person it produced is the t=0 Prime Minister.

outcomeFlags.name: The t=0 Prime Minister ceased to hold office
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form, the union fixed by the scenario class. Mitsotakis's New Democracy IS the single-party majority, so the union is the other two states. IT OVER-READS, AND THE OVER-READ IS THIS PACK'S OWN HEADLINE FINDING WEARING A FLAG: the caretaker state is exactly the 32-day gap of May-June 2023 in which Mitsotakis had ceased to hold office and then returned, and counting it as an incumbent exit is the WIDE reading of gr.pm-exit that this pack's reference class declares and rejects. A reader comparing this column across the roster is reading Greece on the wide convention and gr.mid_term_leader_exit on the strict one, and the two differ by 4.17x in the crisis era.

outcomeFlags.name: A non-party caretaker held the premiership
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form, AND THE QUANTITY THIS PACK EXISTS TO CARRY. Seven non-party heads of government in 52.11 years -- 0.1343/yr, one every 7.4 years -- under an explicit constitutional provision rather than by improvisation. No other roster polity has done this even once. The A2 saturation caution applies to the 'ever' reading over a 120-month horizon containing three scheduled elections; the OCCUPANCY is the informative half, against a measured cumulative ~24 months in 52 years.

outcomeFlags.name: A Prime Minister left office mid-term
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form, on the STRICT reading, and the quantity that supports a cross-pack comparison. Read it against gr.caretaker_premiership: Greek instability discharges into an OFFICE at 0.1343/yr while the premiership itself turns over at 0.0576/yr.

outcomeFlags.name: Greece lifted its veto on Turkish access to EU defence instruments

outcomeFlags.name: Greece extended or delimited a maritime zone

outcomeFlags.name: The t=0 Prime Minister ceased to hold office
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form, the union fixed by the scenario class. Plenkovic's HDZ IS the hdz-led-coalition state, so the union is the other two. IT UNDER-READS IN A WAY THIS PACK CANNOT FIX AND WHICH IS UNUSUALLY LARGE HERE: Plenkovic has led three cabinets across two elections in 9.87 years, so an HDZ-led coalition under a DIFFERENT leader is a live and arguably likely path that this union counts as the incumbent still in post. He is the longest-serving head of government in the European Union and the roster's longest continuous tenure. hr.mid_term_leader_exit at 0.0775/yr is the rate-bearing quantity.

outcomeFlags.name: A Prime Minister left office mid-term
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form, on the modern-era reading, and the quantity that supports a cross-pack comparison.

outcomeFlags.name: The Sabor dissolved itself early

If this flag reads far above the roughly one-in-three a 0.0315/yr hazard implies over 120 months, the modifier is doing more work than the single observation supports.

outcomeFlags.name: The President's deployment veto expired
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form, reading ~100% by construction because it is a scheduled date at month ~41 -- reported rather than suppressed, on E3's ch.arms_export_referendum and E4's ie.incumbent_exit precedent. outcomeFlags.name: The t=0 Prime Minister ceased to hold office
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form, the union fixed by the scenario class. Jansa's SDS IS the right-led-government state, so the union is the single other state. THE UNDER-READ IS THE LARGEST IN THIS BLOCK AND IT IS STRUCTURAL: a two-state machine cannot see a change of Prime Minister WITHIN the right bloc, and one of the five class members (Drnovsek to Rop, December 2002) was exactly that. si.mid_term_leader_exit is the rate-bearing quantity and reads BOTH halves of the gated pair; this flag reads only bloc changes. A reader must not treat them as the same question.

outcomeFlags.name: A Prime Minister left office mid-term
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form, reading BOTH halves of the gated pair, which is what makes it the comparable quantity: 0.1421/yr, sixth-highest in the roster. Reading only one half would report Slovenia at whatever share of the horizon its bloc happened to hold office.

outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form. Two of nine Slovenian parliaments have ended materially early (the 2008-2011 and 2011-2014 crisis pair), and seven of nine ran between 3.89 and 3.97 years.

outcomeFlags.provenance: State form. Caretaker counts as an exit: all three historical caretaker administrations (Tosovsky, Fischer, Rusnok) were non-partisan or differently composed from the government that preceded them, not the ANO coalition continuing to govern.

outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form; the non-routine, intra-coalition part of a PM leaving office, reported separately from incumbent_exit on gr.json's and at.json's shared precedent.

outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form. The unambiguous, well-evidenced channel into caretaker status -- see government-falls's own provenance for why this pack keeps it separate from pm-exit.

outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form. Direct readout of the pack's central, novel mechanism.

outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form.

outcomeFlags.provenance: State form. coalition-minority deliberately excluded -- the same coalition and PM continue governing, just below a floor majority, so it is not an exit by this pack's own reading.

outcomeFlags.provenance: State form. The pack's own structural-fragility texture, distinct from an actual exit.

outcomeFlags.name: The Prime Minister resigned without a caretaker transition
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form, on cz.mid_term_pm_change's and gr.json's shared precedent.

outcomeFlags.name: The government lost a floor vote or resigned into caretaker status
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form. Small-n and illustrative (see the event's own provenance), not load-bearing alone.

outcomeFlags.name: A legislated debt-brake confidence vote was forced
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form. Direct readout of the pack's mechanically triggered fiscal channel.

outcomeFlags.name: A Russia/Ukraine-linked dispute flared
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form.

outcomeFlags.name: The presidency changed political orientation
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form, the union of every orientation OTHER than t=0's. THE CAVEAT: this under-counts by construction if a DIFFERENT independent wins re-election as an independent -- the machine has no way to distinguish 'Christodoulides re-elected' from 'a new independent elected,' since both read as the same independent-centrist state. No roster pack resolves this for a state-form incumbent-exit reading in general (B1 Section 4's correspondence limit); named here because Cyprus's genuinely high year-of-t=0 approval volatility makes it more likely to bite than in most packs that share the pattern.

outcomeFlags.name: A nationalist-aligned candidate wins the presidency
outcomeFlags.provenance: ELAM doubled its House seats in 2026, the single biggest mover of that election; no ultranationalist candidate has ever won the Cypriot presidency, so this reads the model's own judgment about whether 2026's legislative gain carries through to 2028 or 2033.

outcomeFlags.name: A full-format reunification conference convened
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form. Direct readout of the pack's central non-territorial mechanism.

outcomeFlags.name: Cyprus lifted its SAFE/EDA veto on Turkey
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form. See this event's own provenance for the double-counting note against gr.safe-veto-lifted.

outcomeFlags.name: The governing party changed
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form, the union of every configuration OTHER than t=0's. Malta has exactly two reachable government states (see machine provenance), so this is a clean binary read, unlike packs whose union spans three or more orientations. Deliberately DOES NOT include the intra-party pm-exit event -- a Mintoff-to-Mifsud-Bonnici or Muscat-to-Abela handover leaves the state unchanged, exactly the party-vs-person distinction nl.json draws for its own cabinet/PM split.

outcomeFlags.name: The Prime Minister changed without a change of governing party
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form; the non-routine, non-electoral part of a PM leaving office, reported separately from incumbent_exit exactly as at.mid_term_leader_exit is.

outcomeFlags.name: Malta acceded to PESCO
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form. Direct readout of the pack's central posture mechanism; see the event's own provenance for why this is bounded below Switzerland's equivalent.

outcomeFlags.name: A verdict was reached in the Fenech trial
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form. The pack does not model which way the verdict goes, only that reaching one is itself the modelled event.

outcomeFlags.name: Prime Minister left office without a general election
outcomeFlags.provenance: EVENT form, deliberately, on uk.json's identical construction. This is the NON-ROUTINE part of leaving office -- the part the incumbent-exit scenario class is really about -- kept separate from that class precisely because its fixed state-form union would sweep in routine election alternation. See the coverage declaration.

outcomeFlags.name: No party holds a Commons majority
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form over the machine's minority-parliament state. Reported as a configuration fact: Canada has governed as a minority as recently as 2025-04 to 2026-04, so this is a recently-lived condition rather than an instability tail.

outcomeFlags.name: NATO-Russia engagement above the munition threshold
outcomeFlags.provenance: ENGAGEMENT-THRESHOLD §1, quoting the market's own rules: qualifying fire is a two-way exchange or 'shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2)'; intercepting one-way munitions aimed at a third party does not qualify. §2: zero of the ten NATO weapon discharges over NATO territory since 2022 meet it, and the three resolved legs of the market family all resolved No across exactly those events — including the legs covering the Oresund Orlan-10 jamming and the Estonian and Latvian shoot-downs, which traders publicly argued should resolve Yes. the munition class is deliberately absent: it is DISJOINT from this one, not a looser reading of it, and this pack does not model it as an event.

outcomeFlags.name: India–Pakistan cross-border strike episode
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form over the S3 band. BROADER than the Polymarket anchor's question: includes the 2016-class deniable ground raid, where the market counts only air/missile/drone impacts — recorded on the anchor's resolutionMismatch. Every war run passes through limited-strikes first, so this flag also reads P(any kinetic escalation).

outcomeFlags.name: India–Pakistan war
outcomeFlags.provenance: State form: Kargil-class sustained combat (>1,000 battle deaths). 1 in 6 nuclear-era crises; 0/5 since 1999.

outcomeFlags.name: Nuclear signaling episode occurred
outcomeFlags.provenance: Event form (recurring, far from saturation at ~0.5 per crisis-year against ~0.2 crisis-years/yr): NCA convocation, crisis missile test, or arsenal-readiness intel — never mated/deployed in six crises.

premises.claim: The 2026 ordinary Riksdag election falls on Sunday 13 September 2026.
premises.ifChanged: riksdag-election's scheduled month moves, and every government-machine transition gated on it re-times. This pack's only anchor resolves on it.
premises.sourceQuote: Förtidsröstningen pågår fram till och med valdagen den 13 september

premises.claim: The 2018-19 formation ended on 2019-01-18 when the Riksdag accepted Stefan Lofven as prime minister under negative parliamentarism: 115 for, 153 against, 77 abstaining, 4 absent - fewer than the 175 votes against that would have rejected him.
premises.ifChanged: the formation-crisis state's severity citation. NG1b found the count stated as 'four failed votes', which is false and structurally impossible - four failures MANDATE an extraordinary election that Sweden did not hold. The true count is TWO failed (Kristersson, protokoll 2018/19:16, 2018-11-14; Lofven, protokoll 2018/19:29, 2018-12-14) and the third PASSED. NG1d narrowed the CLAIM to the decisive vote because no single retrievable page states the count, and a premise's claim must be settleable by one retrieval from its declared source; the two failed votes are recorded here with their protocol ids instead of asserted where nothing can check them.
premises.sourceQuote: Votering: 115 för godkännande 153 för avslag 77 avstod 4 frånvarande

premises.claim: The most recent Swedish government with an outright Riksdag majority was the Reinfeldt Alliance, 178 of 349 seats, 2006-2010.
premises.ifChanged: the right-majority state's 'priced low' argument. NG1b found this stated as 'no majority since 1979', which is false by three decades. NG1d re-pointed this from val (the election authority's FRONT page, which serves the 2026 campaign) to SCB, the statistics authority that publishes historical election results. It is expected to read UNVERIFIABLE nonetheless, and the reason is a limitation worth knowing: SCB publishes the 2006 result as a spreadsheet, so this claim is settled by a COUNT over a table rather than by a sentence anyone can quote - and the citation fence accepts a quote. A count is not a gloss; the fence cannot yet tell the difference.

premises.claim: The Riigikogu votes for President on 2026-09-02, with Chancellor of Justice Ulle Madise the sole candidate after passing the 68-signature threshold on 2026-08-18.
premises.ifChanged: presidential-selection's outcome distribution. NG1b found this pack asserting 'no consensus candidate had been reported' -- ALREADY FALSE on its own brief's date. A sole candidate is a coronation, not a contest.

premises.claim: Estonia has requested Article 4 consultations ONCE: the North Atlantic Council met on 2025-09-23 following Estonia's request, after three Russian fighter jets violated Estonian airspace on 2025-09-19.
premises.ifChanged: atlanticism's provenance. NG1b found this stated as 'twice within ten days'. NG1d re-pointed this from ee.kaitsemin (a defence-budget page that could never settle it) to NATO's own Article 4 enumeration, and dropped 'MiG-31' from the claim because the primary source says 'three Russian fighter jets' and does not name the type.
premises.sourceQuote: On 23 September 2025, the North Atlantic Council met following Estonia’s request for Article 4 consultations after three Russian fighter jets violated Estonian airspace on 19 September 2025

premises.claim: The Tweede Kamer's party composition is as published by the chamber itself, and no party or coalition holds the 76 seats needed for a majority.

premises.claim: A federal popular vote on the neutrality initiative falls on 2026-09-27.

presentation.note: Continuity. Not zero: the status quo is a wartime autocracy, and a flat zero would read as 'stable' rather than 'unchanged'.
Same class as putin-rule — the incumbent still holds office. The weakening shows in the hazards it opens, not in the fill.
Putinism without Putin: the leadership group survives the transition, so this is continuity with a new face.
Low, and deliberately so: liberalisation is a discontinuity but not a breakdown. Severity is instability, not desirability.
As above — a consolidated liberal outcome is stable, and rating it high would make the map say the opposite.
Divided authority without open contestation.
A hardliner turn is a stable regime with a more dangerous posture — mid-scale because the instability is external.
Contested succession: authority genuinely in question.
Same class as interregnum in the shipped table. Kept identical on the carry-across; arguably it should be higher, and that is now a one-line change in pack data rather than in a library.
The top of the scale: loss of central control over territory.
A functioning alliance is the zero of this scale, unlike a polity's continuity state — there is nothing to be unstable about.
Visible cracks, obligations still expected to hold.
The guarantee that makes the alliance load-bearing is gone.
Alliance breakup. Top of THIS scale, and not comparable to a polity's 1.0, which is state disintegration.
Continuity, and lower than Russia's 0.15 because the PRC's institutional order is not personalised to the same degree.
Orderly handover inside the party — continuity with a new face.
Collective leadership: diffuse authority, still one-party rule.
Stable domestically, more dangerous externally — the same reasoning as Russia's hardliner-successor, and the same value.
Authority genuinely in question.
Top of the scale. NOT state disintegration — the PRC pack does not model that at all (see this pack's coverage).
Which party holds the presidency is not an instability scale. Taiwan's map colour comes from the cn-tw dyad arc, because that is where its modelled risk lives — see this pack's coverage.
As above. A KMT government is a different foreign policy, not a less stable state, and colouring it would say otherwise.
Flat by design: orientation is not instability, and the pack carries no internal-stability content to differentiate on.
Flat by design; see maga-transactional.
Flat by design; see maga-transactional.
Flat by design, and below the admin states only so the primary machine's flat band is what the map reads.
Flat by design; divided government is not instability.
Orientation, not instability — the us pack's flat-severity rule.
Flat by design; see bjp-coalition.
Flat by design; wider variance lives in the dynamics, not the fill.
Flat by design; a change of government is not instability.
The one genuinely governance-unstable configuration (1996-98 analogue) — above the orientation band, below any crisis state.

The entrenched baseline: not calm (FH 32/100, an amendment-rewritten constitution, an imprisoned opposition leader) and not crisis — the registered 0.45 sits above every democracy state and below every contest state.
Slightly below the baseline: the historical episodes were contests the system contained for years before reasserting.
An open interregnum — the 2022/May-2023 class of crisis.
The highest pk severity: an unresolved contest inside a nuclear-armed army's chain of command.
Overt takeover: severe, but historically STABLE once established (mean spell 11.1 yr) — below the contest states by design.
Constitutionalized military presidency: the same dominance in legal form — above the hybrid, below overt rule.
Majority government: the durable configuration. Severity is assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY and is identical across the three majority states of this machine, whichever bloc holds them.
Identical to labour-majority by construction — see that note. A different party winning is not instability.

Identical to labour-majority and conservative-majority by construction. This is the load-bearing case for the symmetry rule: a nationalist-right government with a Commons majority is a majority government, and scoring it higher would encode a political preference as an instability metric. The Reform dimension is carried by nationalist_strength and by the nationalist_government flag, where it belongs.
No majority: confidence-and-supply or minority government, with budget passage genuinely uncertain. 2010 and 2017 are the referents. The step from 0.15 is the configuration change, not the politics.
Majority coalition: the durable configuration. Severity is assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY and is identical across the three majority-coalition states of this machine, whichever parties hold them.
Identical to grand-coalition by construction.

Identical to the other majority coalitions by construction, and this is the load-bearing case for the symmetry rule. An AfD-inclusive coalition would be a formation discontinuity with no post-war precedent, and its durability is therefore genuinely UNKNOWN — but unknown is not the same as unstable, and scoring it higher would encode a political judgement as an instability metric. The AfD dimension is carried by nationalist_strength and by the nationalist_in_government flag, where it belongs.
No majority: each bill needs an ad-hoc majority and the budget is not assured. The step from 0.20 is the configuration change.

No government formed; a caretaker cabinet with no mandate. 2017's 171 days is the referent, and the severity sits below France's caretaker-crisis because German caretaker government is constitutionally orderly.

Presidency with an Assembly majority: the Fifth Republic's designed and durable configuration. Severity is assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY and is identical across the three majority states of this machine, whichever bloc holds them.

Identical to centre-majority by construction, and the load-bearing case for the symmetry rule in this pack. An RN president with an Assembly majority would be a governing configuration with the same institutional durability as any other; scoring it higher would encode a political preference as an instability metric. The RN dimension is carried by nationalist_strength and by the national_presidency flag.
Identical to the other majority configurations by construction.

A functioning but constrained executive: all three post-war episodes ran their full term, which is why this sits BELOW the hung Assembly rather than above it. The step from 0.18 is the loss of a unified executive, not the identity of either half.

The t=0 state, and the highest starting severity of the four D8 packs. A government that can pass a budget only by suspending the vote on it, surviving censure by a handful of votes. This is a description of 2024-26, not a forecast.

No government able to command the Assembly. The highest severity in any of the four D8 packs; France is the only one of the four where a configuration this bad is reachable from t=0 without an election.
Majority government: the durable configuration, and the only one of the four states here that has it. Severity is assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY.

Minority government on an external confidence-and-supply arrangement. The t=0 state. Identical severity to red-green-government by construction: both are minority governments and which bloc holds one is not an instability scale.
Identical to tido-minority by construction — see that note. A Social Democrat-led minority government is the same configuration as a Moderate-led one.

No government formed; a caretaker cabinet with no mandate. 2018's 134 days is the referent. Equal to Germany's formation-crisis by construction — the same configuration in two constitutional orders that both handle it in an orderly way.
Minority-margin coalition government, the t=0 configuration. Severity assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY, matching se.json's convention.
Identical to tusk-coalition by construction — an ordinary democratic alternation between two governing configurations is not an instability scale.
No government formed within the normal window. Slightly above Sweden/Germany's equivalent (0.55): Poland's six-list fragmentation makes a resolved formation-crisis take structurally longer to unwind.

Majority government, the t=0 configuration. Lower severity than Sweden's minority-government equivalent (0.35): Finland's coalition holds a real floor majority. Severity assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY.
Identical to orpo-coalition by construction -- an ordinary democratic alternation is not an instability scale.
Below Sweden/Poland's equivalent state: no Finnish precedent exists for a formation crisis as protracted as Sweden's 2018 (134 days) or as fragmented as Poland's six-list Sejm.

A coalition that has already lost its floor majority -- above Sweden's minority-government baseline (0.35) since this is a step further along the same durability scale, not merely a minority arrangement but one already short of the votes to pass a no-confidence test. Severity assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY.

An ordinary democratic alternation, priced at the standard cross-pack baseline for a new but not inherently unstable configuration -- lower than michal-coalition's severity because it starts with a fresh mandate rather than an already-lost majority.
Matches Poland's equivalent (0.6): both packs' formation-crisis states reflect a six-way-fragmented party system.

A government explicitly characterised by outside analysis as caretaker -- the highest non-crisis severity of the five E1 packs, reflecting that Latvia's t=0 state is already closer to instability than any other pack's starting configuration. Severity assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY.
The standard cross-pack baseline for a freshly-formed government, matching Estonia's isamaa-led-government and Sweden's red-green-government.
Matches Poland and Estonia's equivalent (0.6): all three reflect a severely fragmented party system.
Above Sweden's minority-government baseline (0.35), reflecting the demonstrated within-bloc churn even though the coalition retains a real floor majority. Severity assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY.
The standard cross-pack baseline for a freshly-formed government following an ordinary alternation.
Matches Poland/Estonia/Latvia's equivalent (0.6).

A single party with a constitutional supermajority is, on the CONFIGURATION-ONLY scale this roster uses, the most durable arrangement expressible -- lower than Finland's majority coalition (0.25). Severity here measures durability, NOT desirability: a supermajority's capacity to amend the constitution unilaterally is a democratic concern and not an instability one, and conflating the two would be the same category error the tw pack's rule forbids.
An ordinary governing majority without the amendment power. Equal to Finland's orpo-coalition by construction.
Multi-party coalition -- the standard cross-pack baseline, and the configuration in which all three of Hungary's historical mid-term PM departures occurred.

A multi-party coalition with a real majority in both chambers. Slightly below the cross-pack coalition baseline (0.35) because the Senate and Chamber cushions are both comfortable. Severity is assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY and is equal across blocs at equal configuration.
Identical to right-coalition by construction -- which bloc governs is not an instability scale.

A cabinet with no electoral mandate, installed because the chamber could not produce a political majority. Priced at Sweden's formation-crisis level (0.55) rather than higher: Italy's technocratic governments are an ORDERLY constitutional mechanism with four modern precedents, not a breakdown -- Draghi's commanded one of the largest majorities in Republican history. What it measures is the absence of a governing coalition, not disorder.

A minority government with no confidence-and-supply arrangement, governing vote by vote after its investiture bloc dissolved. Above Sweden's Tido minority (0.35), which HAS a confidence arrangement, and below Estonia's already-lost-majority coalition (0.5), which cannot survive a no-confidence test -- Spain's constructive censure means this one can. Severity assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY.
The standard cross-pack baseline for a freshly-formed government following an ordinary alternation.
Matches Poland, Estonia and Latvia's equivalent (0.6). Spain's 2015-2016 precedent is the longest such episode in the roster's evidence base.
An ordinary Dutch coalition with a negotiated agreement and a Tweede Kamer majority. Equal to Finland's orpo-coalition by construction. Severity assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY.

A minority cabinet with NO confidence-and-supply arrangement -- above Sweden's Tido minority (0.35), which has one, and above Spain's vote-by-vote minority (0.45), which at least retains a censure-proof position. Equal to Estonia's already-lost-majority coalition (0.5): both describe a government that cannot assume a floor majority on any given vote.

A demissionary cabinet governing with authority restricted by constitutional convention. Marginally above the roster's formation-crisis band (0.6) -- it is the same kind of thing, a government without a current mandate, and the Dutch version is more orderly but typically LONGER, four to five months to an election plus a formation that ran 117 days in 2026.
A multi-party coalition -- the ordinary and essentially only Belgian governing configuration. The standard cross-pack baseline. Severity assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY.

A cabinet without a current mandate, governing while a coalition is negotiated. Equal to nl.caretaker-cabinet by construction: the same configuration, and in Belgium's case typically a LONGER one -- the federal record is 541 days against the Dutch 299.

A two-party majority coalition. Equal to Finland's orpo-coalition and the Netherlands' majority-cabinet by construction. Severity assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY -- that the CSV has led four fifths of post-war governments is a fact about Luxembourg's party system, not a durability property of this state.
Identical to csv-led-coalition by construction -- an ordinary alternation between two governing configurations is not an instability scale.
The ordinary Austrian configuration. Equal to Italy's coalition baseline by construction. Severity assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY.

Above the two-party form because a third partner is a third veto: the t=0 government took two failed negotiations to assemble and needed the Chancellor's personal intervention to survive an August 2026 policy dispute. A judgement about coalition WIDTH, not about which parties are in it.

Identical to three-party-coalition by construction, and the equality is deliberate. Severity here measures durability, NOT desirability -- the roster's rule since hu.json, whose supermajority state is the most durable arrangement expressible and is scored lowest. A government's politics are not an instability scale.
A cabinet without an electoral mandate. Equal to Italy's technocratic-government and Latvia's caretaker: the same configuration, and in Austria's case an orderly and short-lived one.

The status quo: neutrality as an executive practice, adjustable without constitutional change. Severity assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY, and for this pack severity does NOT mean instability -- Switzerland's government cannot fall. It reads how constrained the polity's security policy is, with the discretionary state the least constrained.

Lowest in the pack: a Switzerland cooperating more closely with European security structures is the least constrained configuration on this machine's own axis. NOT a judgement that alignment is desirable -- the roster's rule since hu.json is that these numbers measure configuration, not merit.

Highest in the pack, and the reason is constraint rather than disorder: a constitutional bar on alliance cooperation and on non-UN sanctions would remove policy instruments the government currently holds, and it is absorbing within this horizon. A Switzerland that entrenches neutrality is not less stable -- it is less able to change course.

The Portuguese norm rather than a crisis: minority government has been the governing form for most of the last decade under both major parties. Mid-scale because it is genuinely less durable than a majority, not because it is abnormal.

A DISPLAY judgement and an arguable one. Rated above the centre configurations because it is a discontinuity in Portuguese practice -- no party has governed with Chega -- and not higher, because severity here means departure from stable continuity and a 151-seat coalition is more durable than what it replaces, not less.
Same class as minority-government: an alternation, not an instability. Rated identically because the model should not encode a preference between the two blocs.
Authority is caretaker and the Assembly is dissolved. Above the governing configurations, well below a breakdown -- Portugal reaches this state readily and leaves it within a quarter.

Continuity, and the t=0 configuration. Not zero: severity here means departure from stable continuity, and a five-seat cushion tested once already in April 2026 is not the same as an unchallenged majority.

IDENTICAL to ff-led-coalition, and deliberately so. The rotation changes the officeholder and nothing else -- same coalition, same Programme, same supporting independents -- so rating it higher would make the map say a scheduled handover is an instability.

A DISPLAY judgement. The largest discontinuity in modern Irish politics -- no government has been led from outside FF/FG -- but a discontinuity is not a breakdown, and an SF-led coalition would be a normal parliamentary government. Rated well below the caretaker state for that reason.

Authority is caretaker pending formation or an election. Ireland reaches this state readily and can sit in it for months (2020: about five), which is why it is rated above the governing configurations rather than beside them.

The Danish norm rather than a crisis -- Denmark has had a majority government for only a handful of years since 1945. Rated slightly above Ireland's governing states because this one is eight seats short and depends on two parties outside it.

A cross-bloc majority is the MOST durable Danish configuration, not the least -- the Frederiksen II government (2022-2026) held 89 seats of its own. Rated below the minority coalition for that reason, which is the one place in this pack where a less usual configuration scores lower.

A DISPLAY judgement. An alternation rather than an instability, rated above the two centre configurations only because on the 2026 arithmetic it requires DF, which is a discontinuity in Danish governing practice since 2019.

Authority is caretaker pending formation. Rated at the same level as Ireland's for the same reason and despite the shorter dwell: severity is about the character of the state, and the dwell already expresses how long Denmark spends in it.

A DISPLAY judgement. Rated well above the governing configurations because the country has no invested executive and the parliament cannot legislate an RRF programme with roughly EUR 8.5-11.4bn at risk -- and well below a breakdown, because Art. 110(4) keeps a caretaker administering, the courts and the presidency function, and Romania has left this state every previous time inside two months.

Romania's post-2020 norm and the President's own stated preference, so mid-scale rather than low: a minority or technocratic cabinet needing 233 of 465 for anything is genuinely less durable than a coalition, without being abnormal.

The most stable configuration Romania produces, and the lowest severity in the pack. Rated below the minority state because it commands an investiture majority, and not lower because the last two such coalitions both died mid-term over austerity.

A DISPLAY judgement and an arguable one, on pt.right-coalition-government's precedent. Rated above the pro-European configurations because it is a discontinuity in Romanian practice -- no nationalist party has led a Romanian government since 1989 -- and not higher, because severity here means departure from stable continuity and a government with 135 of 330 behind it is more durable than the formation failure it would replace, not less.

The lowest severity in the pack and the second-lowest governing severity in the roster. A government with 131 of 240 needing 121 is the most durable configuration Bulgaria has produced since 1997. Not zero, because severity here measures departure from stable continuity and a four-month-old party formed two days before the election it won is not yet continuity.
Bulgaria's ordinary form for a quarter-century. Mid-low: a coalition holding 121 governs, and Bulgarian coalitions have fallen at 0.274/yr.

Rated meaningfully above the coalition state, and the reason is Art. 89: a no-confidence motion needs more than half of ALL 240 members, so a minority government survives exactly as long as the opposition cannot assemble 121 against it -- which in a chamber this fragmented is a genuinely precarious position rather than a nominal one.

A DISPLAY judgement, and the highest in the pack. Authority is caretaker, the Assembly is dissolved, and the government's constitutionally stated primary task is to organise the next election. Rated above every governing configuration and well below a breakdown, because Bulgaria has entered and left this state four times in five years without any institution failing -- and rated only 0.13 above the minority state rather than far above it, because on the record it is a routine Bulgarian condition rather than an emergency.

The configuration the Greek electoral system is built to manufacture, and the most durable one the country produces. Not lower, because ND's cushion over the majority is five seats and 53 of 300 members sit as independents.

A DISPLAY judgement. Rated above the single-party majority because in Greece a coalition is what a failed majority produces rather than a normal alternation -- the 2012-2019 coalitions were crisis governments -- and well below the caretaker state, because a coalition governs on a programme.

Authority is a judge appointed to run an election, and the chamber that could not produce a government is about to be replaced. Rated highest in the pack and well below a breakdown, because this is a NAMED CONSTITUTIONAL PROCEDURE that Greece has completed seven times without any institution failing -- Article 37 working is the opposite of Article 37 being needed.

The configuration Croatia has run for most of its independence, under a Prime Minister who is the longest-serving head of government in the EU. Low, and not lowest, because the coalition's junior partner is polling below the threshold and four ministers have gone in eighteen months.

An alternation, not an instability, and rated only marginally above the incumbent configuration for that reason -- the model should not encode a preference between the blocs. The four points of difference record that Croatia's two left-led governments both had shorter and more fractious lives than the HDZ norm, not that the bloc is worse.

Authority is caretaker and the Sabor has dissolved itself. Rated well above both governing configurations and well below a breakdown: Croatia has been here once in 34 years, for four months, and the exit was an ordinary election.

A DISPLAY judgement. Rated above the roster's typical governing severity because this government holds 43 of 90 and depends on a confidence-and-supply partner now polling below the threshold -- and well below a crisis, because Article 116 means removing it requires 46 votes for one named alternative, which the opposition has not assembled.

Rated two points below the incumbent configuration and NOT because the model prefers it: the centre-left bloc currently polls 43.6% against the government's ~42.4% and its component parties are all above the threshold, where the government's confidence-and-supply partner is not. Both sit in the same band, which is the intended reading -- an alternation, not an instability.
t=0. A tested, currently comfortable majority.
Rated above ordinary alternation but below outright crisis, on Denmark's and Greece's shared caretaker-state precedent: authority continues, but a government has actually fallen.

An alternation rather than an instability, on dk.right-bloc-government's precedent -- opposition parties taking office through an ordinary election is Czechia's constitutional mechanism, not a crisis.
t=0. Tested and holding, but not rated as low as a genuinely comfortable majority given the structural-fragility texture the notes field describes.
The pack's own documented resilience case: real fragility, historically resolved without collapse.

A government has actually fallen. Rated above cz.caretaker's 0.45 -- this state pools a partisan sub-mode alongside the neutral technocratic one, so on average it represents a somewhat less settled condition.
An alternation rather than an instability, on dk.right-bloc-government's and cz.alternative-coalition's shared precedent.

t=0. A DISPLAY judgement, not a policy verdict: independents govern via shifting coalitions in a fragmented House, which this pack's own legislative_fragmentation factor already prices as the source of friction, not this state.
The most institutionally continuous of the four states -- DISY has held or shared the presidency for the majority of the Republic's post-1974 history.

Rated above disy-aligned and below nationalist-aligned as a DISPLAY judgement about accommodation-track continuity, not about governing competence -- AKEL's own 2008-13 presidency (Christofias) is part of the Republic's ordinary alternation, not a crisis government.
Rated highest: the state this pack's reunification_momentum factor would most plausibly see reverse under, and the only one of the four with no precedent in the Republic's presidential history.
t=0. The roster's most durable single-party configuration by PM tenure, on the same register as Ireland's fixed-term stability.

A DISPLAY judgement, on dk.right-bloc-government's precedent: an alternation rather than an instability, rated modestly above continuity because two-party alternation is Malta's ordinary constitutional mechanism, not a crisis -- PN is EPP-aligned centre-right (see notes), not a discontinuity in kind.
Majority government: the durable configuration. Severity is assigned by CONFIGURATION ONLY and is identical across both majority states of this machine, whichever bloc holds them -- uk.json's rule.
Identical to liberal-majority by construction -- see that note. A different party winning is not instability.

No majority: the incumbent continues to govern, testing confidence vote-by-vote, with budget passage genuinely less certain. Set BELOW uk.json's hung-parliament severity (0.45): Canada's most recent minority (2025-04 to 2026-04) persisted a full year without a confidence collapse and ultimately consolidated into a majority, a materially less acute recent referent than the UK's 2010/2017 cases uk.json cites.
Below the base rung: an actively de-escalated relationship.
The base rung and the 2026 status quo — hostile but not shooting.
Below threshold DELIBERATELY: a crisis is not an exchange of fire, and the arc metric is about shooting.
At threshold. This is the rung `ru-nato.clash` names and the one the arc is drawn from.
Top of the ladder.
Actively de-escalated.
The base rung: the standing gray-zone campaign, which IS the 2026 status quo rather than an escalation.
Post-crisis freeze — not shooting, not resolved.
Below threshold deliberately: a quarantine is coercive but not an armed conflict, and the anchors treat it as its own rung.
At threshold — the first rung `cn-tw.attack_or_blockade` names.

At threshold. Shares outcomeClass `cntw-war` with `war`, which the old class-keyed table could not distinguish. Deliberately the SAME short label as `war`: the split is a modelling distinction (is the US decided yet), not one a one-line legend can carry, and consecutive duplicates collapse.
At threshold.
At threshold, and the widest war the dyad models.
Terminal: the outcome the ladder climbs toward.
A holding ceasefire between armed nuclear neighbours — quiet, not resolved; above cn-tw detente's 0.0 by design.
The 2026 status quo: no shooting, every non-kinetic channel hostile. Above cn-tw coercion (0.20): the treaties are suspended and a water red line is declared.
Mobilized crisis, no cross-border fires — below the map's conflict threshold like cn-tw quarantine.
At threshold — the first rung `in-pk.strikes` names; the 2025 exchange (S3c) is this rung's ceiling.
At threshold: Kargil-class war. Reachable only through limited-strikes, so the conflict flag's first-onset argument holds.

alternatives.predicate: The same event space under Marani's UNCONSTRAINED-spread coding: COVID corrected for containment (8x amplification, 2.63 per mille/yr), recurrence 209y (95% CI 182-244).
alternatives.whyNotAdopted: Same question, rival intensity definition — this is the coding behind the widely quoted '38% in a lifetime'. Not adopted because the model's impulses are sized from OBSERVED 2020 effects, and pairing unconstrained recurrence with observed-effect impulses would mix codings. The 3.5x spread between the two codings is the honest width of this hazard.

alternatives.predicate: Influenza-only actuarial classes (Madhav et al., DCP3), from the ~9 influenza pandemics since 1700: any flu pandemic 3%/yr; >=6M-death class 1%/yr; 1918-class <0.02%/yr.
alternatives.whyNotAdopted: A narrower cause class: influenza only, modern record. Its 1918-class rate disagrees with the adopted source's Spanish-flu class by an ORDER OF MAGNITUDE (<0.02%/yr vs 0.25%/yr) — recorded rather than papered over; COVID itself, a non-influenza event outside Madhav's class, is one observation for the broader coding.

alternatives.predicate: Live market: Polymarket 'New pandemic before 2028?' at 18.5% — resolves YES if WHO 'declares any disease a pandemic' by end-2027.
alternatives.whyNotAdopted: A different question three ways, from the rules text: ANY severity (2009-mild resolves YES); WHO word choice as criterion, an instrument WHO does not formally possess; thin book (~$5.3k liquidity). It brackets the model from above — any COVID-class event would draw the word, and the model's P(fire by 2028) ≈ 2.2% sits well below the market's broad class. NOT an anchor, for these reasons, read before they could mislead.

referenceClasses.codingRule: Adopted: the OBSERVED-intensity coding — an event of the intensity COVID-19 actually had (0.33 per mille/yr), mean recurrence 59y (95% CI 55-64) = 1.7%/yr — because the model wants a shock of the size that actually hits modelled quantities, containment partially in effect, as 2020's was. The Spanish-flu class (400y, 0.25%/yr) is priced as the event's extreme SIDE at the rate ratio 87.2/12.8. Marani's possible TRIPLING with zoonotic emergence is recorded here and deliberately not wired as hazard growth: pricing when the tripling arrives would be an invented schedule.
referenceClasses.name: Recurrence of extreme novel epidemics
referenceClasses.predicate: All novel epidemics regardless of pathogen, 1600-1945, intensity measured as deaths/1,000 persons/year of world population, generalized-Pareto fit to the tail (Marani et al., PNAS 2021; full text read via PMC 2026-08-21).
referenceClasses.question: How often does an epidemic of COVID-19-class intensity or worse occur, worldwide?
referenceClasses.source: docs/research/PANDEMIC-RISK-BRIEF-2026-08-21.md §2; Marani et al. 2021, PNAS 118(35)

alternatives.predicate: The model's own pre-C2.5 reading: 'systemic crises ~4-5/century (1929, 1973, 1997, 2008, 2020-adjacent)' at 0.045/yr.
alternatives.whyNotAdopted: Blends a pandemic-caused contraction into a financial-origin class, which double-counts 2020 the moment a pandemic event exists. Preserved here so the old rate is recoverable from the artifact rather than from git archaeology.

referenceClasses.codingRule: The 2020 contraction is excluded: its origin was a pandemic, and from C2.5 it is priced by `pandemic`, once. This declaration IS the correction 0.045 -> 0.040 — a class-boundary fix, not a retune, with the old reading preserved below.
referenceClasses.name: Systemic financial crises, ex-pandemic
referenceClasses.predicate: Global systemic financial crises with a financial-system origin: 1929, 1973, 1997, 2008.
referenceClasses.question: How often does a systemic global FINANCIAL crisis occur, excluding contractions caused by pandemics?
referenceClasses.source: W1 BASE-RATES brief as corrected by docs/C2.5-REPORT-2026-08-21.md §1.2

alternatives.predicate: The same class conditioned on NO DESIGNATED HEIR at the moment of exit — Lenin 1924, Stalin 1953, Mao 1976. All three contested.
alternatives.whyNotAdopted: n=3 is too small to price a weight on, and this pack's reading is that the party machinery rather than the person carries the transition. **But this is the condition China actually satisfies** — §3 of the same brief says no successor exists — and it is the largest unresolved judgement in this pack. A blind regeneration (B1) that took this branch put contestation three times higher and was not obviously wrong to do so.

alternatives.predicate: REGIME SURVIVAL at leader death, all autocracies: 79 dictators who died in office 1946-2012, regime intact one year later in 87%.
alternatives.whyNotAdopted: Answers a different question. A regime can survive a contested succession and per the Mao-1976 reading usually does, so 87% survival and a high contestation rate are compatible rather than substitutable. Recorded because `xi-exit`'s own comment cites this statistic, and B1 §5.1 flagged that citation as bound to the wrong quantity.

alternatives.predicate: Post-death COLLAPSE rates by regime type: ~6% for institutionalized strong-party autocracies, ~22% for highly personalized ones.
alternatives.whyNotAdopted: Also a survival question rather than a contestation one, and the brief places post-2012 China between the two categories rather than in either. It parameterises the `instability` destination weight, not the managed-vs-contested split.

referenceClasses.codingRule: Contested = an open intra-elite struggle visible within ~12 months of the exit. Coded by this project from the case list CHINA-DOMESTIC-POLITICS §7 enumerates: Lenin 1924, Stalin 1953 (Beria arrested and executed), Mao 1976 (Gang of Four arrested within a month) contested; Brezhnev 1982, Andropov 1984, Chernenko 1985, Kim Il-sung 1994, Kim Jong-il 2011 not. The coding is this project's; the case list is the brief's.
referenceClasses.name: Contestation at a ruling-communist-party succession
referenceClasses.predicate: Every death-in-office or forced exit of a ruling communist party's paramount leader, all cases, no conditioning on whether an heir had been designated.

The three added cases: LUCAS PAPADEMOS, 16 May 2012 -- the technocratic coalition ended ten days after the 6 May election produced no government; he never contested an election and therefore never lost one. ALEXIS TSIPRAS, 27 August 2015 -- resigned voluntarily on 20 August after the Left Platform split cost him his majority, Thanou-Christophilou ran the 20 September election, and Tsipras WON IT AND RETURNED on 21 September, out of office for 25 days. KYRIAKOS MITSOTAKIS, 25 May 2023 -- HE WON the 21 May election with 40.79%, could not form a government under simple PR, all three Article 37 mandates failed, Sarmas was appointed, and he returned on 26 June, out of office for 32 days; he ceased to hold office without losing an election BECAUSE HE WON IT. On the predicate's literal words all three qualify, and Mitsotakis unambiguously. AND HERE IS WHAT THE CHOICE DECIDES. On the strict reading Greece has NO ERA EFFECT: 2 departures in the 35.20 years to October 2009 (0.0568/yr) against 1 in the 16.90 years since (0.0592/yr), a ratio of 1.04x. On the wide reading it has a large one: 2 against 4 in the same windows, 0.0568 against 0.2366, a ratio of 4.17x. WHETHER GREECE'S CRISIS DECADE EXISTS IN THIS MODEL IS DECIDED ENTIRELY BY HOW THE CARETAKER INTERVAL IS TYPED, and nothing about the predicate as written settles it. Not adopted on E4's Ireland argument run backwards: a 32-day gap during which the same person returns is not a leader change, and a model counting it would report a change of government in June 2023 that no Greek voter experienced. The era arithmetic is recorded here because a reader who remembers 2011-2015 will not believe 0.058 and is entitled to see why.

Recorded because the mechanism that forced it NO LONGER EXISTS -- the 2019 revision decoupled the presidential election from dissolution -- so this class member cannot recur, and a future reader should know that the disagreement is about a dead mechanism.

Konstantinos Karamanlis, 10 May 1980 -- RESIGNED TO BECOME PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC, elected 5 May 1980; Rallis succeeded with no election. Andreas Papandreou, 22 January 1996 -- RESIGNED FROM HIS HOSPITAL BED, announced 15 January after being intubated in November 1995; Simitis elected by the PASOK group on 18 January and sworn on 22 January; Papandreou died 23 June 1996. George Papandreou, 11 November 2011 -- RESIGNED MID-TERM after the referendum announcement and its withdrawal, with the Papademos coalition following and NO election. THE PREDICATE'S SECOND CLAUSE IS THE CODING RULE AND IT IS WHERE THE JUDGEMENT LIVES: Article 37 produces a judicial or non-party caretaker premiership whenever formation fails, and between such an appointment and the next government the previous Prime Minister HAS ceased to hold office -- sometimes for 25 days, sometimes for six months -- in every case without having lost a general election. The predicate's literal words include those exits; its evident purpose excludes them. This class excludes them, and its rejected alternative includes them. EXCLUDED, and the first is the hard case: ANTONIS SAMARAS, 26 January 2015 -- he lost the 25 January 2015 election, which was NEITHER SCHEDULED NOR CALLED BY HIM but forced by the failed presidential election of December 2014 under the pre-2019 Article 32, so neither the predicate's exclusion nor its inclusion literally applies; excluded because the predicate's purpose is to separate electoral defeat from non-electoral exit and this was electoral defeat, and recorded as an alternative. KYRIAKOS MITSOTAKIS, 25 May 2023 -- excluded under the caretaker rule, and see the alternative. COSTAS SIMITIS, 10 March 2004 -- lost the March 2004 election having ceased to be PASOK leader in January 2004 while remaining Prime Minister; excluded, and it is the exact Brian Cowen 2011 shape E4 flagged for Ireland, where the political death was mid-term and the office-holding was not. classes.definition: The individual holding the polity's chief-executive office at t=0 ceases to hold it at any point before the horizon, by ANY mode — death, resignation, managed handover, removal. The class is deliberately mode-blind: how the incumbent left is a different question, and in this model it is one the machine cannot answer (all three exit routes reach the same successor states). OPERATIONALISATION, fixed and uniform: the union of the machine's states OTHER than those in which the t=0 incumbent still holds office. The event form is not interchangeable — for `cn` A2 measured it at 53.1% against the state form's 61.0% (pre-us composition), because `political-crisis` ends the incumbent order with no named exit event in 7.9pp of runs.
classes.provenance: Archigos 4.1 codebook (Goemans/Gleditsch/Chiozza), which codes EXIT over {Foreign, Irregular, Natural Death, Regular, Retired Due to Ill Health, Suicide} — any of which ends a leader's tenure. Primary source read for the exit taxonomy; the regular/irregular distinction it also defines is NOT used here, because this model cannot support it (see the definition).
classes.title: Incumbent leaves office

classes.definition: After the t=0 incumbent's rule ends, the succession is CONTESTED — an open intra-elite struggle over who rules — rather than a settled handover. A state-form SUBSET of `incumbent-exit`, and explicitly NOT the question of whether the regime survives: a regime that survives a contested succession (the China corpus's own Mao-1976 coding) answers YES here and NO to state-disintegration. OPERATIONALISATION, fixed and uniform: the union of machine states meaning an UNRESOLVED contest over leadership — in this pilot, exactly the states the packs themselves code with a contest outcome class. Excluded, each a recorded categorical choice: settled successor states (the contest, if any, is over); caretaker interims (`ru.collective-caretaker` — a governing arrangement, not an open contest; including it would change the question to 'was the succession non-instant'); and the instability/fragmentation family (B1 §4's exact lesson — a run that tips from contest into those states still counted, via the contest state it occupied on the way).
classes.provenance: Pre-registered in docs/C2-REPORT-2026-08-21.md §1 in a docs-only commit BEFORE the measurement ran, with five acceptance gates; all five passed (subset holds in-run, no cell saturated, ru/cn separate by 45× the larger cell's MC standard error against a 3× gate, no degenerate cell). The quantity is the one B1 (docs/B1-REPORT-2026-08-21.md §5) measured as the pilot's largest single authored-vs-generated gap: two readers of one corpus paragraph split it 72/28 vs 22/78, worth more than every parameter in either model. The coding rule is operational over the packs' own `outcomeClass` codes; no external codebook is claimed as read for this class.
classes.title: Succession contested

classes.definition: Contested dissolution, secession of a substantial area by extrajudicial means, or near-total collapse of central state authority. Internal disintegration ONLY — loss of sovereignty to an external actor (annexation, occupation, foreign-imposed leadership) is a different literature with different base rates and is deliberately NOT merged in. Merging them produced a row where Russia 10.0% sat beside Taiwan 9.4% meaning opposite things, which reads as comparable sovereignty risk and is not.
classes.provenance: PITF Problem Set Codebook 2018 §III.1, adverse-regime-change sub-criteria 3 and 4, quoted: "contested dissolution of federated states or secession of a substantial area of a state by extrajudicial means; and or near-total collapse of central state authority and the ability to govern." Primary source read.
classes.title: Loss of central control over territory

rejected.measurement: Attempts read 23.3%; the modelled *successful* irregular exit is ≈7.1%. A 3.3× gap between the name and the quantity.

A column headed "irregular executive change" reading 23.3% would be off by more than three times, in the direction that makes the world look more dangerous.

covers: ca.government_durability — whether the Carney government still holds a majority of 343
sources.name: House of Commons of Canada / Chambre des communes — Party Standings
sources.note: Fetched 2026-08-26, 45th Parliament: Liberal 171, Conservative 139, Bloc Québécois 21, NDP 5, Green 1, Vacant 6, of 343. THIS DOES NOT MATCH THE PACK, and the discrepancy is the point of pulling it: the pack asserts a 174/343 majority reached 2026-04-13 via floor-crossings and by-elections, while the live count reads 171 with 6 vacancies — 171 is one BELOW the nominal 172 and two ABOVE a majority of the 337 seats filled — the note used to say '171 is still above the 172-seat threshold only if the vacancies break right', which is arithmetically confused in both directions and was corrected by NG1d doing the sum. The government carries a confidence vote 170-166 with the Speaker voting only to break ties. The 2026-08-31 by-elections (see ca.elections) resolve three of those vacancies. Treat this as the standing check fo ONE THING THIS PACK CANNOT KNOW: the three by-elections fall 2026-08-31 and the model's t=0 is 2026-09, so the world STARTS after they are decided and their outcome is not in evidence at authoring time. A Liberal sweep restores the nominal majority at 174; three losses put the government at 171 of 340 filled, still a working majority of one. Both are liberal-majority, which is why the initial state is robust to the thing it does not know.
